title: Pannonia Osiguranje-Tech Crosses 9,000 Active Telematics Policies
text:
Subotica, 19 February 2024 — Pannonia Osiguranje-Tech a.d. has confirmed that the number of active PanDrive telematics motor policies passed 9,000 at the end of January, up from approximately 6,200 at the same point in 2023.

The PanDrive product, which uses the company's PanTrack G2 black-box device to record speed, braking and cornering data throughout the policy year, was first offered to new private-car customers in 2019. Uptake was slow in the first two years, partly because installation required a visit to a partner workshop and many customers were reluctant to arrange this. A 2022 change to the installation process — workshops now come to the policyholder's address in the Subotica, Novi Sad and Zrenjanin areas — contributed to the acceleration seen in 2023.

Chief Executive Mirela Bogdanović said: "We are pleased with the pace of growth in PanDrive, but we are honest with ourselves that the hard part — making the data actually influence prices at the individual level — is still ahead of us. Our goal for 2024 and 2025 is to make the telematics investment earn its keep in the loss ratio."

The company also noted that claim frequency among PanDrive policyholders has been measurably lower than in the comparable standard-product cohort over the past two calendar years, although it cautioned that self-selection effects make direct comparison difficult.

Pannonia Osiguranje-Tech currently operates a fleet of approximately 340 installation kits held across twelve partner workshops in northern and central Serbia. The company plans to extend the workshop network to cover the Niš corridor before the end of 2024.

title: About Our Products and How We Work
text:
Pannonia Osiguranje-Tech writes motor and property insurance for private customers, farmers and small businesses across Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina and North Macedonia. We are based in Subotica and have been operating since 2009.

Our motor product comes in two versions. The standard version prices by vehicle age, engine size and driver profile in the conventional way. The telematics version, which we call PanDrive, fits a small black-box device to your car and adjusts your premium based on how you actually drive over the policy year. We fit the device ourselves through a network of partner workshops, and the device stays the property of Pannonia for the life of the policy. About one in four new motor policies we write today uses the telematics version.

Our property product for private homes, PanDom, comes with a starter kit of sensors — a smoke detector, a water-leak detector and a door contact — that connect to an app on your phone and also send a signal to our claims team if the alarm runs for more than ninety seconds without being silenced. Claims handled through the sensor alert system close on average eleven days faster than claims reported by phone.

For farmers in Vojvodina we offer PanAgro, which covers farm buildings, stored equipment and standing crops against fire, flood, hail and storm. PanAgro can be combined with the standard PanDom policy if the farmer also insures a residential building on the same plot.

All our products are sold through independent brokers and agents, and through a direct online channel for straightforward motor and apartment policies. We do not use tied agents. Policyholders can manage documents, file claims and download their green card from the customer portal at any time.

title: What Three Hail Seasons Taught Us About Vojvodina Farm Exposure
text:
This post is written by Tijana Horvat, head of property claims at Pannonia Osiguranje-Tech.

In July 2021, a hail corridor roughly eight kilometres wide crossed the Bačka plain and produced the largest single-day farm claim total we had seen in our then-twelve-year history. A similar event followed in August 2022, and a third, smaller one in June 2023. After three years of watching the same story repeat, I think it is worth being honest about what we got wrong and what we are trying to do about it.

What we got wrong is geography. Our farm policies are rated by municipality, and our hail loading per municipality was set using provincial average data going back to the 1990s. The problem is that Vojvodina hailstorms are narrow and fast-moving. The 2021 corridor went straight through three municipalities but clipped only the eastern edge of each. Our loading treated the whole municipality as equally exposed, which means we collected inadequate premium from the farms in the path and adequate premium from those that saw blue sky all afternoon.

After the 2021 event we started overlaying claim locations on the MeteoVoj gridded hail data in QGIS. The correlation between high hail-kinetic-energy grid cells and our paid claims is striking — visually obvious, in fact. The difficulty is turning that visual observation into something systematic. A large share of our farm policy addresses are recorded only at the settlement level, not as coordinates, so we cannot automatically assign a grid cell to each policy.

We are now working through the address geocoding problem for the active farm portfolio, which has about 1,200 policies. Once that is done, we intend to look at whether we can build a field-level exposure index that updates our pricing rather than a municipal average. If anyone has practical experience with this kind of approach in a small-team insurance context, we would genuinely welcome a conversation.

title: Services — What We Build and Operate
text:
Kvantor Inženjering has been building and running data infrastructure for European manufacturers since 1997. Our work sits between ERP systems and the people who need to make decisions from them.

ERP Integration
Most of our clients run SAP — either older ECC landscapes or more recent S/4HANA deployments — alongside production systems that predate any integration standard. We connect these environments so that data flows reliably between them without manual export and import routines. We work with RFC connections, IDocs, REST APIs and direct database interfaces depending on what the client's systems support.

BI Dashboards and Reporting
We build and maintain monthly reporting packages for manufacturing clients covering production output, quality metrics, procurement and finance. Dashboards are delivered through Power BI or Metabase depending on client preference. We manage the full pipeline from raw extraction to delivered report, including the reconciliation work that most vendors prefer not to talk about.

Managed Infrastructure
We host client applications and data on Azure in EU regions, currently Frankfurt and Amsterdam. Hosting agreements include defined SLAs, backup schedules, access management and incident response. Clients with data-residency requirements receive written documentation of where their data is stored and how it is handled.

Legacy Connectivity
Older MES systems, custom-built plant databases and spreadsheet-based processes are a reality in manufacturing. We connect them rather than insist on replacement.

Who We Work With
Our clients are manufacturers with between 150 and 2,000 employees, mostly in Germany, Austria and the Netherlands. They have complex data environments, limited internal IT capacity for integration work, and a preference for a single reliable partner over a roster of specialists. We have held some client relationships for more than ten years.

Our team in Novi Sad is 220 people. Most of our senior engineers have been with us for more than five years and many have worked directly at client sites during project phases.

title: Senior Data Engineer — ETL and Pipeline Automation
text:
We are looking for a senior data engineer to join our BI delivery team in Novi Sad. This role sits at the centre of our manufacturing reporting work: you will design, build and maintain the pipelines that move data from SAP systems, legacy MES platforms and client-maintained spreadsheets into the databases that power our monthly dashboards.

What the work looks like day to day:
You will own pipeline reliability for a portfolio of German manufacturing clients. Each client has a different SAP configuration and a different set of supplementary data sources. Pipelines break when clients upgrade systems or change how they code data — handling that breakage quickly and cleanly is the core of the job. You will also work on improving how we detect and respond to schema changes before they cause report failures.

Technical environment:
We run pipelines in Apache Airflow on Azure. Source systems include SAP ECC and S/4HANA accessed via RFC and IDoc interfaces, several older MES databases on SQL Server and MySQL, and file-based inputs in various formats. Transformation logic is written in Python. Output goes to PostgreSQL or SQL Server and is consumed by Power BI or Metabase.

What we are looking for:
— At least five years of data engineering experience, at least two in an environment with SAP as a primary source

title: What Actually Goes Wrong When an LLM Writes SQL Against a Manufacturing Database
text:
We ran a pilot last year connecting a large language model to a client's BI database so that their managers could ask questions in plain German and get charts back. The idea was straightforward: take a question, generate SQL, run it, return a visualization. We knew it would need tuning. We did not expect forty percent of finance queries to produce wrong numbers.

Here is what we actually observed.

The model understood the German text well. It parsed questions about rejection rates, delivery performance and cost variances without much trouble. The failures were almost entirely in the SQL generation, and they clustered around a few specific patterns.

First: date handling. Manufacturing clients track performance by shift, by calendar week, by fiscal period and sometimes by all three depending on which department is asking. The database has separate columns and sometimes separate tables for each convention. The model consistently guessed wrong about which date dimension applied to a given question. A question about 'last quarter' in the context of a production query returned fiscal-period data; the same phrasing in a logistics question returned calendar-quarter data. Both were wrong for the specific question being asked.

Second: aggregation scope. Several metrics in the client's database are pre-aggregated at the line level. Summing them across lines double-counts. The model had no way to know this from the schema alone because the column names did not indicate it.

Third: missing filters. Some tables contain both active and archived records flagged by a status column. The model generated correct-looking queries that included archived data, producing totals that did not match any number a human analyst would recognize.

None of these problems are surprising in hindsight. The model was working from a schema and some column descriptions. It had no access to the business rules embedded in years of analyst practice.

We are now working on approaches that use our existing library of validated analyst-written queries as a constraint layer. The idea is to give the model examples of correct query patterns for the specific client database rather than asking it to reason from schema alone. Early results are better but we are not ready to publish numbers.

If you have worked on similar problems in industrial data environments, we are interested in comparing notes.

title: New maintenance contract with Mlekovita Sever dairy, Kikinda
text:
We signed a two-year maintenance contract with Mlekovita Sever, a dairy in Kikinda processing sheep and cow milk into a range of fresh and aged cheeses. The contract covers quarterly servicing of two ion-exchange softeners on their main process water line, annual UV lamp replacement on three disinfection units, and on-call response for faults.

Mlekovita Sever had been managing their own resin regeneration with mixed results — irregular cycle timing had led to hardness breakthrough events that left scale deposits on their pasteuriser plates. After we carried out a free inlet water survey in September, their production manager Dragana Filipov asked us to take over the full maintenance schedule.

The inlet water at their site tests at around 420 mg/L CaCO₃, which is on the harder end of what we see in the Kikinda area. We have adjusted the regeneration frequency accordingly and fitted a simple hardness test point on the outlet line so their staff can do a quick check between our visits using one of our indicator strips.

This brings our active maintenance contracts in the Kikinda municipality to five. We now have a technician scheduled in the area every three to four weeks, which makes emergency response faster for all clients there.

If you are a food producer in or around Kikinda and you are managing your own water treatment without a service schedule, it is worth having a conversation with us. A short site visit costs nothing and we will tell you honestly whether there is a problem worth addressing.

title: Field Water-Treatment Technician – Kristal Voda, Zrenjanin

Send a short CV and a note about your background to the address below. We do not need a formal cover letter — just tell us what you have worked on.

title: Our Services – Kristal Voda
text:
Kristal Voda has been working with food and beverage producers in Vojvodina since 2011. Our focus is simple: we make sure the water going into your product and your cleaning lines meets the quality your process requires.

We supply and install ion-exchange softeners sized for bakery, dairy, and bottling-line flow rates. Soft water reduces scale build-up on heat exchangers and filling equipment, lowers detergent consumption in CIP systems, and helps maintain consistent product quality. We hold stock of the most common resin types and replacement tanks in Zrenjanin, so downtime after a fault is short.

For disinfection, we fit UV-C units on inlet lines and on rinse-water returns. Unlike chemical dosing, UV leaves no residual in the water and requires no handling of chlorine or ozone. We service the lamp assemblies and sleeves on a scheduled basis under our maintenance contracts.

Our portable testing kits let your quality team — or ours — check turbidity and nitrate on the spot during a delivery inspection or a line start-up. Results take under five minutes. We supply the reagents and carry out annual calibration checks.

All installations come with a commissioning report and a plain-language summary of what we found in your inlet water. Clients on a maintenance contract receive a brief written report after every service visit.

We cover Zrenjanin, Kikinda, Vršac, Pančevo, and the surrounding municipalities. For clients further south in Vojvodina we can usually arrange a visit within two working days.

If you want to talk through a specific water problem before committing to any equipment, call us directly. We are a small company and we prefer a conversation to a glossy brochure.

title: What we learned at the Vojvodina Food Industry Suppliers Fair, Novi Sad
text:
We exhibited at the Vojvodina Food Industry Suppliers Fair in Novi Sad for the third time this year. It is a two-day event aimed at small and mid-sized suppliers to the regional food sector, and for us it is one of the few occasions where we meet potential clients outside our usual territory.

The conversations this year confirmed something we have been noticing in the field: water hardness is becoming a bigger topic for food producers in the Banat region. Several visitors mentioned problems they have been having with scale in filling equipment and inconsistent cleaning results in CIP systems, and a few were surprised to learn how hard their inlet water actually is when we ran quick conductivity checks at the stand.

We also had a number of questions about nitrate levels, particularly from smaller producers who draw from private wells rather than municipal supply. There is genuine concern in that group about whether their water is being tested reliably. We demonstrated our portable nitrate kit, but we had to be straightforward about its limitations at very high hardness levels — something we are actively working to address.

On the equipment side, the most interest was in compact UV disinfection units for smaller bakeries. Several visitors had been told by their buyers to document their water disinfection practice, and UV is the simplest way for a small operation to do that without chemical handling.

We left with around twenty serious enquiries and have followed up with all of them. Whether those convert to contracts we will see over the summer.

One practical note: the fair is worth attending if you are a supplier in this sector, but bring printed materials. Digital brochures on a screen do not get looked at during a busy stand.

title: Free water survey for Zrenjanin-area food businesses – June 2024
text:

One of our technicians will test your inlet water for hardness, turbidity, nitrate, and conductivity using calibrated portable instruments, and will inspect any water treatment equipment you already have in place. You will receive a written summary the same day.

We are running this programme for two reasons. First, we have capacity in June before our summer maintenance schedule fills up. Second, we have found that quite a few producers in the area have water treatment equipment — sometimes installed by previous contractors — that is either undersized, incorrectly configured, or simply not being serviced on any schedule. title: What We Do — Services
text:
Paleta Kreativa is a six-person content agency based in Subotica. We work with local retailers, restaurants, and tourism businesses across Vojvodina and the southern Hungarian border region. Everything we produce is written, filmed, and reviewed in both Serbian and Hungarian by people who actually live here.

Short-form video is the centre of what we do. We come to your location — your shop floor, your guesthouse courtyard, your restaurant kitchen — and we film the material that goes into reels, TikToks, and Stories. We handle scripting, filming, editing, and captioning. You do not need to prepare anything except to be open and doing what you normally do.

Community management means we respond to comments and messages on your behalf, post on schedule, and keep your audience active between bigger content pieces. We know the difference between how a customer writes in Subotica Serbian and how they write in Senta Hungarian, and that matters if you want replies to feel local.

Content calendars are built monthly. We sit with every client at the start of each month, agree on the themes and key dates, and then work independently from there. You approve the plan once; after that, the posting happens without you needing to chase us.

Performance reports go out at the end of each month. One page, plain language, the numbers that matter: reach, engagement rate, follower change, and the two or three posts that worked best and why.

We work with 34 clients right now. We take on new clients slowly so that service quality does not drop. If you are a retailer or tourism operator in our region and you want content that actually fits where you are, get in touch with Erzsébet at the contact below.

title: Freelance Video Editor — Short-Form Content
text:
We are looking for a freelance video editor to help with overflow work during our busier months. This is project-based, not a fixed position. We expect roughly 8 to 15 hours of editing work per month, possibly more in June through August when tourism client demand peaks.

title: What we learned from eight months of tracking our own posting times
text:
Since last summer we have been keeping a manual log of every post we publish across twelve of our most active accounts. Post time, day of week, language of the caption, type of content, and the engagement count 24 hours later. About 900 rows now in a shared Google Sheet.

We started because we kept noticing that the same quality of video would perform very differently depending on when it went up. A reel for a thermal spa client that got 40 interactions at 11:00 in the morning would sometimes pull 180 at 19:00. That is not a small difference when your client is measuring whether the work is worth the monthly fee.

What the data has told us so far, roughly: evenings from 18:30 to 20:30 consistently outperform midday slots for our tourism accounts, but that pattern is weaker for retail clients where lunch-hour browsing matters more. Hungarian-language content on accounts with a majority of followers from southern Hungary tends to get its engagement later in the evening than Serbian-language content on Vojvodina-based accounts. We do not fully understand why yet.

The honest problem is that reading patterns by eye across 900 rows is not reliable. We can see rough shapes but we cannot turn it into a clean rule we trust enough to apply every week without second-guessing it.

We are writing this partly to think out loud and partly because we suspect someone with more analytical experience could do something useful with the data we have already collected. If that sounds like you, we are genuinely open to a conversation. The data is real and the question is practical. Reach out to Tamás.

title: Završili smo sezonu 2023. sa rekordnim brojem uzorkovanih parcela
text:
Prošla agro-sezona bila je za TloCare najobimnija od osnivanja. U periodu od aprila do novembra 2023. godine naš terenske ekipa je uzorkovala nešto više od 11.200 hektara za ukupno 38 klijenata — od toga 31 kooperativa i 7 agro-input distributera.

Najveći novi klijent ove sezone bila je kooperativa 'Zlatna njiva' iz okoline Bečeja, koja je prethodno uzorkovanje radila jednom u sedam godina koristeći usluge pokrajinskog zavoda. Prešli su na dvogodišnji praćeni program i od prvog izveštaja identifikovali tri zone sa izraženim padom pH vrednosti za koje ranije nisu znali.

Što se tiče tehničkih rezultata — prosečan rok isporuke finalnog izveštaja od dana uzorkovanja bio je 11 radnih dana, što je dan kraće nego 2022. godine. Cilj za 2024. je da dođemo ispod deset dana, ali to zahteva da rešimo deo uskog grla u unosu laboratorijskih podataka.

Zahvaljujemo se svom timu, naročito terenskoj ekipi koja je radila i u otežanim uslovima tokom kišnih perioda u oktobru. Sledeća sezona uzorkovanja počinje u martu.

title: Naše usluge — TloCare d.o.o.
text:
TloCare pruža usluge analize zemljišta kooperativama i agro-input distributerima u Vojvodini od 2013. godine. Naš pristup je jednostavan: izlazimo na teren, uzimamo uzorke po planiranoj mreži, šaljemo ih u laboratoriju i rezultate vam dostavljamo u obliku mape i preporuke — ne kao tabelu punih brojeva, već kao konkretan akcioni dokument.

Uzorkovanje radimo po grid metodi sa jednom tačkom na četiri hektara. Za svaki uzorak beleži se GPS koordinata, dubina i datum. Rezultati iz laboratorije obrađuju se i unose u naš portal gde svaki klijent ima pregled svojih parcela po godinama. Mape se mogu preuzeti u PDF formatu ili kao shapefile za klijente koji koriste vlastite GIS alate.

Izveštaj o kalcifikaciji je poseban dokument koji izlazi uz analizu i sadrži procenu trenutnog pH stanja po zonama parcele, preporučenu dozu krečnjaka i napomenu o prioritetu tretmana za sledeću sezonu.

Godišnji praćeni programi namenjeni su kooperativama koje žele da prate promene plodnosti tokom više sezona. U tom slučaju uzorkujemo iste tačke svake dve do tri godine, što nam daje mogućnost da zajedno sa agronomom klijenta tumačimo trend, a ne samo trenutno stanje.

Kontaktirajte naš tim da dogovorite termin za uvodni razgovor. Dolazimo na teren i sami procenimo šta je za vaše parcele najsvrsihodnije pre nego što potpisujemo bilo kakav ugovor.

title: Tražimo: Junior backend programer (Python/Django) — TloCare d.o.o.
text:

Radićeš na Django backendu koji prima, obrađuje i prikazuje laboratorijske rezultate analize zemljišta. Deo posla podrazumeva rad sa PDF dokumentima koje šaljemo iz tri različite laboratorije — svaka u svom formatu — i razvijanje boljih rešenja za automatizovano čitanje tih podataka. Drugi deo je unapređenje API-ja za naš portal i integracija sa PostGIS bazom podataka u kojoj čuvamo prostorne podatke o parcelama.

Šta tražimo:
– Poznavanje Pythona i Django frameworka (barem jedna završena stvar, ma kako mala)
– Osnovno razumevanje SQL baza podataka
– Volja da razumeš kontekst agronomije onoliko koliko je potrebno da razumeš šta podaci znače
– Urednost u pisanju koda — radimo u malom timu i tuđ kod čitamo svakodnevno

Prednost:
– Iskustvo sa PDF parsiranjem (pdfplumber, PyMuPDF ili slično)
– Poznavanje PostGIS ili prostornih upita u PostgreSQL-u
– Iskustvo sa Leaflet.js (frontend strana mapa)

Šta nudimo:
– Puno radno vreme, rad u kancelariji u Novom Sadu (Bulevar cara Lazara)
– Uvid u ceo lanac od terena do podatka — nisi samo programer, razumeš zašto nešto radiš
– Ekipa od dvadeset dvoje ljudi gde ima prostora da se čuje tvoj predlog

Molbe sa kratkim opisom šta si do sada pravio/la i GitHub linkom (ili drugom primernom referencom) slati na: posao@tlocare.rs

title: Zašto pH nije dovoljan za preporuku kalcifikacije — i šta nameravamo da uradimo po tom pitanju
text:
Kad god u razgovoru sa agronomom pomenemo preporuku za kalcifikaciju, pre ili posle čujemo isto pitanje: 'Ali koliko tačno da stavim krečnjaka?'. I naš odgovor godinama je bio: uzmi pH, pogledaj u tabelu, dodaj preporučenu dozu. Funkcionisalo je na velikom broju parcela. Ali ne na svima.

Problem je u tome što dve parcele sa istim pH od 5,4 mogu da reaguju na istu dozu krečnjaka potpuno različito — jedna će se popraviti za dve sezone, druga ostaje kisela. Razlog je puferska sposobnost tla: glinovita i humusna tla 'upijaju' dio dodate baze pre nego što pH počne da raste, dok peskovita tla reaguju brže. Ako ne znamo kakvo je tlo u pitanju, preporuka je otprilike tačna, ali samo otprilike.

Mi to znamo. I naši klijenti to znaju, jer nam govore. Kooperativi 'Sever Agro' iz Ade smo jedne sezone preporučili iste doze na svim parcelama, i agronomi su nam posle rekli da su na ritskim parcelama uz kanal rezultati bili puno lošiji nego na ostalima. Imali su pravo.

Zbog toga ove godine krenuli smo u istraživanje kako da u naš sistem preporuke uvedemo podatak o teksturi tla i sadržaju humusnih materija kao korektor doze. Imamo podatke iz deset godina uzorkovanja — za mnoge parcele imamo i pH i teksturu i humus. To je osnova od koje možemo da krenemo.

Nemamo gotovo rešenje. Ali smatramo da je važno da naši klijenti znaju šta radimo i zašto. Ako imate iskustvo ili podatke koji bi mogli da pomognu, kontaktirajte nas.

What we do

DriveLogic Vojvodina provides software integration and testing services for automotive ECU projects built on the AUTOSAR Classic platform. All work is carried out by our in-house team in Novi Sad. We do not subcontract.

AUTOSAR Configuration and Integration
We take your System Extract and deliver a complete, compiled, and reviewed BSW and SWC configuration ready for the next phase of your V-cycle. Diagnostic Tooling and ECU Flashing
We write and maintain UDS service handlers, configure the Diagnostic Communication Manager, and produce the ODX/CDD files your after-sales tooling needs. We also set up and document flashing procedures for production and end-of-line environments.

Toolchain Migration
If you are moving from an older AUTOSAR release or from one toolchain vendor to another, we have done this migration several times and can provide a structured plan with known risk points documented up front.

Where we work
Most of our contracts are with Tier-1 and Tier-2 suppliers. We embed into your process rather than running a parallel one. If you use a specific configuration tool version, a specific CI system, or a specific code review workflow, we follow it.

title: What we learned from four integration faults in twelve months
text:
Over the last twelve months we had four CAN communication faults reported by customers during their own integration testing — after we had already delivered. Each one cost us time to diagnose and fix, and two of them required a re-delivery with a new test report. That is not acceptable at the rate we want to work, so we spent some time in February pulling the four cases apart to see what they had in common.

In every case the fault was at a component boundary. One SWC sending a signal with an assumption about update timing. Another SWC on the receiving side, from a different supplier, with a different assumption. Both components passed their own module tests. Both matched the interface specification as written. The fault only appeared when they were connected and running on the same OS schedule.

Our coverage reports showed 87–89% branch coverage in all four projects. That number did not predict the faults at all. Branch coverage tells you whether your test cases reached the code. It does not tell you whether your test cases asked the right questions about what happens when two components disagree about the timing, range or sequence of a shared signal.

We have known for a while that interface testing is weaker than module testing in our process. What this review made concrete is that we do not have a systematic method for generating test cases that specifically target the contract between two components — and that writing those cases by hand, based on our own reading of the spec, tends to reproduce our assumptions rather than challenge them.

We do not have a solution yet. We are looking at what information is already available in the ARXML and COM configuration that could drive a more targeted test generation step. If you have worked on this problem or have a view on it, we are genuinely interested in talking — reach us at office@drivelogicvoj.rs.

Miroslav Vučić wrote the first version of this post. Andrej edited it.

title: Two years of returns data: what we have learned and what we still cannot predict
text:
Every logistics company talks about forward delivery rates. We want to talk about what happens when parcels come back.

In 2023, roughly 11% of the parcels we delivered were returned by recipients. That sounds like a manageable number until you think about what it means operationally. On a day when we send out 4,200 parcels, we might receive 300 returns — or we might receive 550. We genuinely do not know until the vans start rolling back in.

That uncertainty creates a specific problem at our returns desk. If we staff for 300 and 500 arrive, parcels pile up, re-dispatch is delayed, and two of our client contracts have clauses that charge us for exactly that delay. If we staff for 550 every day on the conservative side, we spend about €3,200 a month on labour we did not need.

For the past six months, our operations analyst Bojan Latinović has been digging into our PostgreSQL transaction history — two years of parcel records, delivery attempts, return events, driver reason codes, and sender manifests. Some patterns are clear: returns from one particular fashion sender spike on Mondays following weekend promotional emails; returns of electronics are three times more likely when the recipient postal code is outside Novi Sad city. But a reliable day-level forecast has so far been out of reach with the tools and time Bojan has available.

We are not writing this to complain. We are writing it because we think there is a tractable problem here for someone with the right skills — a combination of time-series modelling and sender-level segmentation that takes what is going out today and predicts what comes back Thursday. If you work in data science or applied statistics and this sounds interesting, we would be glad to share the data structure and talk through what a working solution might look like. Reach out to operacije@brzaposta.rs.

title: DriveCore completes verification programme for Hartfeld Automotive's new door module
text:
DriveCore Software has completed the software verification phase for a new door control module developed by Hartfeld Automotive, a tier-1 supplier based in southern Germany. The module is scheduled to enter series production later this year and will be fitted to a vehicle platform from a German OEM.

The programme ran for fourteen months. DriveCore's verification team of eight engineers produced just over 1,100 test cases covering normal operation, fault injection, and boundary conditions required by the project's ASIL-B classification under ISO 26262. Testing was carried out using a combination of software-in-the-loop methods early in the programme and hardware-in-the-loop testing on DriveCore's dSPACE SCALEXIO bench during integration.

Marko Vujanović, DriveCore's head of verification, said the programme was technically straightforward but demanding in terms of throughput. "Hartfeld had a tight schedule and the requirement document went through three significant revisions during the programme. Keeping test traceability clean through those revisions took a lot of manual effort. It reinforced for us how much time we spend on work that should be at least partly automatable."

Hartfeld's programme manager, Ida Bremer, said she was satisfied with the quality of the deliverables and the responsiveness of the DriveCore team during the audit preparation phase.

This is the sixth series-production programme DriveCore has completed since 2018. The company currently has two active programmes in verification and is in discussion with a third potential customer.

title: What we learned trying to reuse test cases across programmes
text:
We have six completed series-production programmes in our archive. Every one of them produced a set of test cases that we documented carefully, stored in DOORS, and told ourselves we would reuse on the next project. The reality has been less satisfying than we hoped.

The carry-over rate on our last three programmes was between 15 and 22 percent. That means for every hundred test cases in the new project, fewer than a quarter started from something we had written before. The rest were written from scratch by engineers reading a requirement document and working out what to test.

Why is carry-over so low? The short answer is that requirements documents from different customers — and sometimes different programmes from the same customer — are structured differently enough that direct mapping is unreliable. A requirement for window anti-trap behaviour in one customer's template is not written the same way as the equivalent requirement in another customer's template, even though the underlying behaviour is similar. When we tried to match them by keyword, we got enough false positives that the engineers stopped trusting the suggestions and went back to doing it manually.

We have not given up on the idea. Our archive is a real asset — over 5,000 test cases across six programmes, all traceable to requirements, all reviewed and approved. The question is how to make that archive useful during authoring rather than after the fact.

This is one of the reasons we are hiring a research engineer to work on the problem directly. If you have thoughts on how to approach it, or if you are working on something similar, we are happy to talk. We are not looking for a polished product; we are looking for approaches that work in practice on real requirement documents. Reach us at info@drivecore-software.example.

title: Research Engineer — Test Automation (Internal Tooling)
text:
DriveCore Software is hiring a research engineer to work on an internal project aimed at reducing the manual effort in writing ISO 26262 test cases.

Background
We have six completed programmes worth of requirements and test case archives in DOORS. We want to explore whether we can use that material to partially automate the generation of test cases for new programmes, or at least to surface relevant historical cases during authoring. This is not a research project in the academic sense — we need something that works inside our existing Jenkins and DOORS environment within a reasonable timeframe.

What the job involves
You will spend the first few months understanding how our requirements and test cases are structured, then prototype approaches to matching or generating test content from requirement text. If a prototype shows promise, you will be responsible for hardening it into something the verification team can use day to day.

Nice to have

This role sits within our verification team and is funded for an initial period of eighteen months with the expectation of a permanent position if the project delivers. Salary is negotiable based on experience.

title: DriveCore at Embedded Automotive Forum Novi Sad — May 2024
text:
DriveCore Software will be presenting at the Embedded Automotive Forum being held at the Science and Technology Park Novi Sad on 14 May 2024. The event brings together embedded software teams from companies based at NTP and guests from the regional automotive supply chain.

DriveCore will give a 30-minute presentation titled "HIL testing on a limited budget: what works and what does not." The talk will be given by Stefan Radovanović, one of our senior verification engineers, and will cover our experience setting up and running hardware-in-the-loop test benches for body control module programmes of different sizes.

The talk will cover three areas. First, what a minimal HIL setup needs to do to be useful for BCM work: CAN and LIN simulation, load simulation for outputs, and fault injection for the cases that matter most. Second, where the cost actually goes in a conventional dSPACE-based setup, and why that cost structure does not scale down well for short or early-phase programmes. Third, what we have tried and where we are still looking for a better answer.

This is not a sales presentation. We will show real data from our own projects and be straightforward about the constraints we have not yet solved. The audience we are hoping to reach is other embedded teams who face the same scaling problem and engineers who have built or worked with leaner test bench approaches.

The Forum runs from 9:00 to 17:00. DriveCore's session is scheduled for 14:00. Attendance is free but registration through the NTP Novi Sad event page is required.

title: Zašto nam batch rekoncijacija više ne odgovara — i šta planiramo da uradimo
text:
Kada smo projektovali prvu verziju rekoncijacionog engine-a, batch pristup je bio logičan izbor. Payment provideri isporučuju podatke u intervalima — Stripe šalje webhook-ove u realnom vremenu, ali settlement izveštaje šalje na kraju dana; Adyen ima sopstveni raspored; lokalni acquireri najčešće šalju fajlove jednom ili dva puta dnevno. U takvom svetu, batch job koji se pokreće na sat vremena bio je sasvim razuman.

Ali stvari su se promenile. Imamo klijente koji procesiraju 50.000 porudžbina dnevno, i oni imaju finansijske sastanke u 08:30. Naš job traje 70 do 90 minuta. Matematika ne štima.

Pokušali smo da optimizujemo postojeće Spark jobove — promenili smo strategiju particioning-a, podesili executor memoriju, smanjili shuffle operacije. Dobili smo 10 do 12 minuta. To nije dovoljno.

Jasno nam je da rešenje nije u podešavanju batch sistema već u promeni pristupa. Imamo Kafku u infrastrukturi — koristimo je za prijem podataka od providera koji podržavaju streaming. Sledeći korak je da rekoncijacioni proces pomerimo ka streaming ili hibridnoj arhitekturi gde obrađujemo transakcije čim stignu, a batch korak zadržimo samo za finalno zatvaranje perioda.

Ovo nije trivijalna promena. Rekoncijacija zahteva konzistentnost — ne možeš da prijaviš klijentu broj koji se može promeniti. Exactly-once semantika u distribuiranom streaming sistemu je rešiv problem, ali zahteva pažljivo projektovanje.

Zato i tražimo senior data inženjera sa Kafka iskustvom. Ako ste prošli sličan put, pišite nam.

text:

The 320th account belongs to the Kovačević family, who farm roughly 180 hectares of maize and sunflower near Crvenka. They came to us last autumn after a neighbour recommended us. Getting them set up took two field visits, a full parcel mapping session, soil zone preparation, and a half-day training session with the two family members who will use the tablet in the field.

We do not think 320 is a large number in absolute terms — there are thousands of commercial farms in Vojvodina. Milica and Jovana Šeremešić, Directors

title: About Our Services – Njivomer Agro d.o.o.
text:
Njivomer Agro started with a GPS receiver, a pickup truck, and a retired surveyor who thought farmers deserved the same quality of spatial data that engineers get for construction sites. Branko Šeremešić spent his career measuring land and he knew that most farm parcels in Vojvodina were either unmapped or mapped badly. He founded this company in Sombor in 2008 to fix that, one parcel at a time.

Today we offer four main services. First, we go to your farm and map every parcel boundary using RTK GPS, then we clean and register those boundaries against the official cadaster so your records match both the physical ground and the legal documents. Second, we prepare agronomic GIS layers — soil type zones, historical yield maps, variable-rate prescription files — so you can make input decisions based on spatial data rather than a single average for the whole field. Third, we maintain NjivaManager, our own farm management information system, which runs on Android tablets and lets operators log field operations, track input use, and view their prescription maps while sitting in the tractor cab. Fourth, we fly drone surveys for crop scouting, producing multispectral index maps that show canopy stress and uneven establishment before it is visible from the ground.

We cover farms across western Vojvodina. Our clients range from families farming forty hectares of sunflower to agricultural cooperatives with several thousand hectares of mixed arable. We currently serve about 320 active farm accounts.

Our team of sixty-one includes surveyors, agronomists, GIS analysts, software developers, and drone operators. Most of us grew up in this region and understand what the soil and the seasons here actually look like. That combination of local knowledge and technical work is what we think makes the difference.

title: Why Cadaster Boundaries Are Not Good Enough for Variable-Rate Farming
text:
We get asked occasionally why we insist on re-surveying parcel boundaries with RTK GPS when the client already has their parcels in the state cadaster. The answer comes down to a practical problem we see on almost every farm we work with for the first time.

The cadaster boundary files we receive through the official web service are digitised from older paper maps. The original maps were drawn at scales where a pencil line represented several metres on the ground. When those lines were digitised, positional errors of two to four metres were introduced and have stayed in the system. For most legal and administrative purposes, that level of error does not matter. But for precision agriculture it matters a great deal.

Here is a concrete example. Suppose a field is 800 metres long and 200 metres wide. The headland area — the strip along the boundary where the tractor turns — might be twelve metres wide. A four-metre error in the boundary position means that your variable-rate prescription layer, which was built to reflect soil zone data right up to the field edge, is misaligned from reality by four metres. The section control on the sprayer or spreader is making decisions based on the wrong location. You get a four-metre strip of over-application on one side and a four-metre strip of under-application on the other. Across 200 metres of headland, that is a meaningful area of wasted input or missed crop.

We have measured this effect on client fields and in the worst cases the headland error strips account for six to eight percent of total input cost on the affected boundary. For a farm with a lot of smaller, irregular parcels, the proportion is higher.

The fix we use is straightforward: we survey the actual physical boundary with RTK GPS, then align the cadaster polygon to our measured points. It takes a few hours per farm on the first visit and we update it if the physical boundary changes. The result is a parcel layer that matches the ground within half a metre, which is accurate enough for any current variable-rate equipment.

If you are using cadaster boundaries directly in your precision agriculture work without this step, it is worth checking how much the error is costing you.

title: InspektAI Deploys at Mertex Components, Cuts Escape Rate on Bracket Line
text:
InspektAI completed a full production deployment at Mertex Components, a pressed-metal parts manufacturer based in Inđija, in January 2024. The project covered a single inspection station on their aluminium bracket line, which produces parts for white-goods assemblers in Central Europe.

Mertex had been running manual visual inspection on that line for several years. Their quality manager, Dragan Horvat, told us the escape rate — defective parts that passed inspection and reached the customer — was running at around one point four percent, which was above the threshold their customers had set for the coming contract year.

We installed InspektAI Line over four days in December, working around Mertex's production schedule. The main technical challenge was the polished surface of the brackets, which creates strong specular reflections. We used a combination of structured LED lighting and a custom exposure setting to reduce reflection noise, then retrained the model on images captured at the Mertex line specifically.

After four weeks of parallel running — manual inspection and InspektAI running side by side — Mertex switched to full automated inspection in late January. The escape rate on that station dropped to zero point three percent over the first three weeks of live operation, measured against a sample audit the Mertex quality team ran independently.

Dragan Horvat: 'The dashboard is the part the shift supervisors actually use. They can see within the first hour of a shift whether something is going wrong.'

The defect dashboard is now running on a tablet mounted at the line supervisor's station. Mertex has asked us to quote for a second station covering a different part family.

title: What InspektAI Does — Services Overview
text:
InspektAI builds visual quality control systems for factories that run at production speed. Here is what that means in practice.

We mount industrial cameras above your conveyor, robot arm, or inspection station. Our software, InspektAI Line, processes every frame in real time and flags any part that shows a defect — scratch, crack, chip, burr, discolouration — before it moves to the next stage. The decision takes less than thirty milliseconds. The part does not slow down.

All processing happens on an edge device installed at your line. Nothing goes to a cloud server. Your production data stays on your floor.

Our defect dashboards run on a standard browser. Shift supervisors see a live feed of pass and fail rates, a photo of every rejected part, and a chart of when defects spiked during the shift. Quality managers can pull weekly or monthly reports in two clicks.

For clients whose product changes regularly — new part numbers, new surface finishes — we offer a Model Refresh Service. Send us a new sample batch, we retrain, and we push the update to your edge device over your local network.

We handle installation ourselves. One of our engineers comes to your site, maps the line, sets up the cameras and lighting, and does not leave until the system is passing your own quality checks. Typical installation takes two days for a single-station setup.

We work with metal fabricators, plastic injection shops, and electronics assembly lines. Our smallest client runs one line with eight workers. Our largest runs four lines across two shifts. The system scales.

If you want to see it running before you commit, we can arrange a two-week trial on one station. You keep the defect data either way.

title: Why We Stopped Trying to Solve Reflection With Augmentation Alone
text:
We spent about six weeks last year convinced that the right answer to specular reflection on polished metal was better data augmentation. Our thinking was straightforward: if we expose the model to enough synthetic brightness variations, highlight blobs, and random glare patches during training, it will learn to ignore them.

It did not work well enough.

The model got better at ignoring static glare, but real factory lighting is not static. The overhead LEDs on most lines cycle at a frequency that interacts with camera exposure in ways that change frame by frame. A highlight that sits in one corner of a bracket at frame one has moved to a different corner by frame fifteen because the part has rotated slightly on the conveyor. The model kept flagging those moving highlights as scratches.

We tried three things before we accepted that augmentation alone was not enough.

First, we added random highlight shapes to training images using a simple procedural generator. Helped a little. Second, we trained with a longer sequence of frames rather than single images, hoping the model would learn that a true scratch stays in the same position while a reflection moves. This helped more, but it made inference slower and the Jetson ran warm. Third, we switched to polarised illumination on one client's line. This cut the highlight problem significantly at the hardware level, which is the lesson we should have learned earlier: some problems are easier to fix with a thirty-euro polarising filter than with two weeks of model work.

We now treat lighting as part of the model design process. Before we collect training data on a new part type, we run a lighting test. It adds half a day to an installation but it saves weeks later.

We are still not satisfied with our scratch detection on very smooth surfaces. If anyone has worked on this problem, we are genuinely interested in talking.

title: Services – Elektro Bačka a.d.
text:

Substation and network installation. We design and build medium-voltage substations from 10 kV to 35 kV and all associated low-voltage distribution infrastructure. Switchgear manufacturing. Our production hall in Subotica manufactures low-voltage distribution and motor-control cabinets to IEC 61439 standards. Maintenance and inspection contracts. We hold long-term maintenance agreements with eight municipal utilities and eleven industrial clients. Project documentation and commissioning. For clients tendering for EU-funded infrastructure projects, we provide technical documentation, as-built drawings, and commissioning reports. title: Data Analyst / Junior Software Developer
text:

title: Statement on tender result – Pécs regional grid modernisation project
text:

We were informed in May that our submission did not pass the technical-compliance evaluation stage. This is the second time in eighteen months that we have received this type of finding on a cross-border tender. On the previous occasion, involving a project in Romania, we engaged an external consultant to assist with the documentation. The current submission reflected that experience and incorporated additional CIM-structured asset data, but the result was the same.

We are publishing this note because we believe in being direct with our clients, partners, and staff about setbacks as well as wins. Cross-border EU tenders represent a significant opportunity for companies of our size, and we are committed to developing the internal capability to compete for them on a sustainable basis rather than depending on piecemeal external support for each submission.

Our engineering team is reviewing the evaluation feedback in detail. We are also actively looking for partners — whether technical consultants, software specialists, or research collaborators — who have direct, practical experience with IEC 61968 implementation in the context of grid-project documentation. If your organisation works in this area and is open to a conversation, please contact our chief engineer Aleksandar Boras at a.boras@elektrobacka.rs.

We expect further tenders in this category to be published in the fourth quarter of 2024 and the first half of 2025, and we intend to be ready for them.

title: Nexara Embedded Wins Multi-Board Development Contract with Adriatek Automotive
text:
Nexara Embedded has signed a contract with Adriatek Automotive d.o.o., a Slovenian automotive component supplier, to design and validate three embedded hardware modules for a new brake and chassis sensor platform.

The contract covers a wheel-speed sensor interface board, a brake-pressure acquisition module, and a gateway board that aggregates both signal streams onto a CAN FD bus for the vehicle's main ECU. All three boards are targeted at an ASIL-B functional safety level under ISO 26262, which represents the most demanding automotive safety work Nexara Embedded has taken on to date.

Miroslav Tanić, head of hardware design, said: "Adriatek came to us after working through two other design houses who could not commit to the ISO 26262 documentation requirements on their timeline. We have the hardware competence for this type of board, and we are building the functional safety process in parallel with the design work. It is not the easiest way to do it, but the client's programme schedule does not allow for a later start."

The project is scheduled across three phases. Schematic and layout work on the first board began in January. Prototype builds are planned for April, with functional safety documentation — including a full FMEDA — due to the client by June.

Adriatek's programme manager, Tina Bertoncelj, noted that the decision to place the contract in Novi Sad was partly driven by Nexara Embedded's in-house pre-compliance facility, which reduces the risk of late-stage EMC failures on the automotive component certification path.

The contract represents one of the larger single engagements in Nexara Embedded's 20-year history in terms of technical scope and compliance requirements.

title: Contract Embedded Design and Assembly — Nexara Embedded d.o.o.

title: What We Learned From Three EMC Re-Tests in Twelve Months
text:
Last year three of our PCB designs failed radiated emissions on first submission at an external EMC lab. All three had passed our own pre-compliance scans before they left our facility. We think it is worth being direct about what happened and what we are doing about it.

In each case the failure was in the 150–450 MHz range. Two failures were linked to clock harmonics coupling onto power planes via the return path, and one was a case where a switching regulator's layout had a longer-than-expected high-di/dt loop that we had not caught in simulation. In all three cases the fix was found, the board was modified, and the redesign passed. But the cost — roughly €9,000 per re-test visit plus the project delay — adds up fast, and it is the kind of delay that damages client relationships regardless of whose fault it technically is.

The gap between our pre-compliance lab and the certified lab results partly comes down to the difference between a 3-metre semi-anechoic setup and a 10-metre fully anechoic chamber. But we also think we have been relying too much on post-layout scanning and not doing enough analytical work during layout review. Our HyperLynx licences have been used mainly for impedance checking. We are now trying to use SIwave more systematically for power distribution network analysis before sign-off.

We do not have this fully solved yet. We are looking for better methods to identify emission hotspots at the layout review stage rather than after the first test submission. If you have experience with this problem — whether from a simulation, measurement, or process angle — we are genuinely interested in talking.

Contact us at technical@nexara-embedded.rs.

title: Machine Learning Engineer — Industrial Vision (Part-Time Project Contract)

title: What We Do — Services and Operations
text:
Zelena Petlja a.d. provides the full chain of solid waste services for municipalities and industrial clients across northern Bačka. Here is what that looks like in practice.

Collection. Twelve vehicles — eight rear-loaders and four hook-lift trucks — run fixed routes six days a week. Each route has an assigned driver and a co-worker who has known the street layout for years. We collect mixed household waste, separately bagged paper and light packaging where municipalities have introduced source separation, and bulky items on a scheduled call-out basis.

Sorting. At our facility on the Bajmok road, incoming mixed and separately collected streams pass through a tipping hall, a manual pre-sort cabin, a shredder for oversize items, and then the optical sorting line. The line separates PET clear, PET coloured, HDPE, PP, paper, cardboard and film into individual fractions. Each fraction is baled and stored until a load accumulates for dispatch.

Regranulate production. Clean HDPE and PP fractions that meet our internal quality threshold go through a wash tank, a dryer, and a twin-screw extruder that produces pellets. We sell regranulate primarily to packaging manufacturers in Serbia and to one buyer across the border in Hungary.

Industrial services. Several industrial park tenants in Subotica contract us directly for collection of production scrap, wooden pallets and hazardous-item removal. These contracts run on annual terms.

Our sorting hall is open for inspection visits by prospective customers and by technical or academic partners by appointment. Contact our operations manager Tibor Varga at the address below.

title: Zelena Petlja Signs Three-Year Extension with the Municipality of Kanjiža
text:
We are pleased to report that we have signed a three-year extension of our municipal waste collection contract with the Municipality of Kanjiža, covering household mixed waste, recyclables collection from 34 bring-sites across the municipality, and bulky-item removal. The contract runs from 1 February 2024 to 31 January 2027.

Kanjiža has been a customer of ours since 1998. Over that time collection coverage in the municipality has expanded from the town itself to include eleven surrounding settlements. The new contract introduces two changes requested by the municipality: a quarterly reporting format that shows fraction weights separately for paper, plastics and glass, and a response time guarantee of 48 hours for call-out bulky-item collection.

Our fleet manager Zoran Horvat notes that the Kanjiža route accounts for roughly 15% of our total annual vehicle kilometres. The extension allows us to plan maintenance scheduling for those vehicles with more certainty than short-term contracts permit.

Mayor of Kanjiža, in a brief statement at the signing, noted that the municipality values working with a company that has operated locally for decades rather than selecting on price alone.

This contract extension is one of the supporting elements in the documentation we are preparing for our planned bond issuance later in 2024 or early 2025, as it demonstrates stable long-term revenue from a public-sector counterparty.

title: Process Technician — Sorting Line and Regranulate Production
text:
Zelena Petlja a.d. is hiring a process technician to support daily operation and incremental improvement of our plastics sorting and reprocessing equipment.

What the job involves

You will work alongside our two existing technicians on the sorting line floor and in the pelletising area. Day-to-day tasks include monitoring the NIR optical sorter's rejection rates and logging results by material category, adjusting baler parameters, maintaining the extruder and pelletiser (cleaning, die changes, temperature profile checks), and helping the maintenance crew with planned and unplanned downtime. You will also run a manual audit sample once a week to measure the purity of outgoing bales — we weigh and hand-sort a 200 kg sample and record the results in a simple spreadsheet we have been keeping since 2021.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have experience with NIR-based sorting equipment or who have worked in polymer processing and understand how melt flow and contamination interact. We use a secondhand optical sorter originally manufactured by a Central European equipment maker; the control software is a proprietary system from that manufacturer, and configuration access requires a specialist password we obtained from the reseller. Who to contact

title: Environmental Compliance Officer (Part-Time, Fixed Term)
text:
We are looking for a part-time environmental compliance officer on a fixed-term contract of twelve months, with the possibility of extension.

Background

Zelena Petlja operates a waste management site under an integrated environmental permit. Following a routine inspectorate visit in February 2024 we have received a formal order to install groundwater monitoring wells and submit a remediation proposal for leachate seepage at our temporary storage yard. We need someone who can manage this process from site assessment through to submission of documentation to the Subotica Environmental Inspectorate.

Responsibilities

Review existing site hydrogeological data and identify gaps. Coordinate with a licensed drilling contractor to install the ordered monitoring wells. Oversee sampling and chain-of-custody documentation. Prepare or commission a leachate characterisation and containment proposal in the format required by the inspectorate. Maintain our permit compliance register and prepare responses to any follow-up queries from regulators. Provide guidance to site staff on leachate management practices in the interim.

Requirements

Degree in environmental engineering, civil engineering, geotechnical engineering or a closely related field. Familiarity with Serbian environmental permitting regulations for waste facilities. Experience with groundwater sampling or contaminated site assessment is strongly preferred. Ability to write clear technical reports in Serbian, with working English for reading equipment documentation.

Practical details

Approximately three days per week on site; some remote work possible for report writing. Start date: as soon as possible, ideally by 1 April 2024. Deadline for the inspectorate submission is late June 2024. Salary negotiable based on experience. Contact: Marta Fekete, general director.

title: What We Learned at the Balkan Recycling Forum in Belgrade
text:
Three of us from Zelena Petlja attended the Balkan Recycling Forum in Belgrade at the beginning of March: Tibor Varga from operations, our quality technician Anita Kereš, and Marta Fekete from management. It was a two-day event with about 180 attendees from Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia, Bulgaria and Romania, mostly operators, equipment dealers, and a handful of municipal procurement officers.

A few things worth noting for anyone following the plastics recycling market.

Dark packaging is a shared headache. We asked around during the breaks about dark HDPE and PP and found that at least four other operators are dealing with the same NIR misclassification problem. One company from Niš said they had applied a secondary detection step using a different sensor type and cut their reject rate by about a third, but they were not ready to share specifics. We exchanged contacts and will follow up. It was useful to have our own numbers to bring to those conversations — most people were talking in rough estimates, while we have a dataset going back to 2021.

Regranulate quality standards are tightening. Two Hungarian and one Romanian buyer at the event mentioned that their quality threshold for HDPE regranulate is moving from 95% to 97% purity within the next eighteen months, driven by their own customers in packaging. This is relevant to the investment case for our sorting line upgrade — better purity does not just prevent discounting, it may become a condition of sale.

We also attended a short session on structured financing for mid-size operators, which was mostly aimed at companies larger than us, but it confirmed that the documentation issues we have heard from investment funds are not unique to our situation. Several operators are working with outside advisors to reformat their accounts.

Overall a useful trip. We will attend again next year.

title: O nama i naše usluge — Lumina Data Solutions
text:
Lumina Data Solutions d.o.o. je softverska kompanija sa sedištem u Novom Sadu, specijalizovana za analitiku radne snage. Naš proizvod je platforma koja HR odeljenjima daje uvid u to šta se stvarno dešava sa zaposlenima — bez nagađanja i bez tona ručno pravljenih izveštaja.

Osnovali smo kompaniju 2017. godine sa ubeđenjem da većina HR podataka u kompanijama postoji, ali nije organizovana ni iskorišćena. Godinama smo radili kao konsultanti i videli isti obrazac: menadžeri donose odluke o rasporedu, angažovanju i napretku zaposlenih na osnovu intuicije, jer podaci su ili razbacani po sistemima ili nerazumljivi.

Naša platforma se implementira za četiri do osam nedelja i integriše se s kalendarskim sistemima, HRIS alatima i internim anketama koje kompanija već koristi. Klijentima nudimo tri osnovna modula: optimizaciju rasporeda smena, praćenje dobrobiti i analitiku produktivnosti. Svaki modul može da se koristi posebno ili zajedno.

Radimo s kompanijama iz proizvodnje, logistike i finansijskih usluga u Srbiji, Sloveniji i Slovačkoj. Tipičan klijent ima između 200 i 2.000 zaposlenih i HR tim koji nema kapaciteta da sam razvija analitiku.

Tim čini 74 zaposlenih: inženjeri, data analitičari, konsultanti za implementaciju i tim za podršku. Sedište nam je u NTP Novi Sad, a imamo i ured u Ljubljani.

Ako želite da vidite kako platforma funkcioniše na vašim podacima, možemo da organizujemo demonstraciju bez obaveza.

title: Lumina Data Solutions potpisala ugovor s Jadran Packaging grupom
text:
Sa zadovoljstvom objavljujemo da smo u januaru 2024. godine potpisali dvogodišnji ugovor s Jadran Packaging grupom, proizvođačem ambalaže sa sedištem u Šapcu, koji zapošljava oko 600 radnika u tri pogona.

Jadran Packaging je prišao nama s konkretnim problemom: planiranje smena u pogonu s velikim brojem kategorija radnih mesta i stalnim promenama u narudžbinama trajalo je danima i rezultiralo čestim greškama. HR direktorka Milena Đorđević rekla je da su planeri smena trošili gotovo dva radna dana svake druge nedelje samo na izradu rasporeda, a i tada bi se redovno javljali propusti u pokrivanju specijalizovanih radnih mesta.

Implementacija našeg modula za optimizaciju smena počela je u februaru 2024. u jednom pogonu, a proširenje na ostala dva planira se do juna. Uz optimizator smena, Jadran Packaging će koristiti i modul za praćenje dobrobiti zaposlenih, što je za nas prvi slučaj kombinovane implementacije oba modula kod istog klijenta od samog početka saradnje.

Ovaj ugovor je za nas značajan iz još jednog razloga: Jadran Packaging je naš prvi klijent koji dolazi direktno preporukom drugog klijenta — Voćar Komerca, s kojim radimo od 2019. godine. Zahvalni smo na poverenju i na tome što naši klijenti prepoznaju vrednost i dele iskustvo s kolegama iz industrije.

title: Oglas za posao: Senior Backend Inženjer (Python / optimizacija)
text:
Lumina Data Solutions traži iskusnog backend inženjera koji će raditi na jezgru naše platforme — pre svega na servisu za optimizaciju rasporeda smena.

Šta radimo: razvijamo SaaS platformu za HR analitiku koja se koristi u kompanijama s nekoliko stotina do nekoliko hiljada zaposlenih. Backend je pisan u Pythonu, podaci se čuvaju u PostgreSQL i TimescaleDB bazama, a cela infrastruktura radi na Kubernetes klasteru.

Šta će biti vaš posao:
— Rad na optimizatoru rasporeda zasnovanom na OR-Tools i PuLP bibliotekama
— Identifikovanje uskih grla u performansama i predlaganje rešenja (paralelizacija, bolje modelovanje, aproksimativni algoritmi)
— Pisanje čistog, testiranog koda koji kolege mogu da razumeju i nadograđuju
— Povremeni rad s klijentskim timovima kako biste razumeli stvarne operativne zahteve

Šta tražimo:
— Pet ili više godina iskustva s Pythonom u produkcijskom okruženju
— Iskustvo s kombinatornom optimizacijom ili operacionim istraživanjem (ILP, CP, heuristike)
— Poznavanje Dockera i Kubernetesa
— Sposobnost da objasnite tehničke kompromise nestručnoj publici

Biće nam drago ako imate iskustvo s distribuiranim računanjem ili radom na vremenski kritičnim algoritmima.

Nudimo: kompetitivnu platu, hibridni rad (Novi Sad ili Ljubljana), 25 dana godišnjeg odmora i budžet za profesionalni razvoj.

Prijave šaljite na posao@luminadata.rs uz kratko pismo o relevantnom iskustvu.

title: Oglas za posao: HR Analitičar / People Science saradnik
text:
Tražimo osobu koja razume i psihologiju rada i podatke — nekoga ko može da postavi pitanje 'da li ovo zaista merimo ono što mislimo da merimo?' i da sistematski pronađe odgovor.

Kontekst: Naša platforma uključuje modul za dobrobit zaposlenih koji prikuplja podatke kroz periodične ankete. Imamo anonimizovane podatke od više od 30 klijenata i počinjemo da shvatamo da nam je potreban neko ko će ozbiljno pristupiti validaciji instrumenata koje koristimo.

Šta ćete raditi:
— Analizirati vezu između anketnih odgovora i operativnih ishoda (odsustvovanje, fluktuacija, produktivnost)
— Predlagati revizije anketnog instrumenta i metodologije bodovanja
— Pisati interne smernice i dokumentaciju za naš tim i za klijente
— Sarađivati s data inženjerima koji rade u Pythonu i SQL-u

Šta tražimo:
— Obrazovanje ili iskustvo u psihologiji rada, organizacionoj psihologiji, sociologiji ili srodnom polju
— Solidno poznavanje kvantitativnih metoda (faktorska analiza, regresija, pouzdanost skale)
— Sposobnost da radite s podacima u Python okruženju ili R-u, ili spremnost da to naučite
— Preciznost i sklonost ka preispitivanju pretpostavki

Ovo nije isključivo tehnička pozicija — isto toliko je važno da možete da komunicirate nalaze HR direktorima koji nisu statistički stručnjaci.

Rad je moguć iz Novog Sada ili hibridno. Plata zavisi od iskustva. Prijave na posao@luminadata.rs.

title: Šta smo naučili na sajmu HRtech Central Europe u Bratislavi
text:
Početkom marta deo našeg tima bio je na sajmu HRtech Central Europe u Bratislavi, jednom od retkih događaja u regionu gde se na istom mestu nalaze HR direktori, softverski vendori i zakonski stručnjaci.

Najviše razgovora vodili smo o dve teme koje su nam i inače na umu poslednjih meseci: ROI kalkulacije i pravni okvir za prikupljanje podataka o zaposlenima.

Kada je reč o ROI-ju, nismo jedini koji se s tim bore. Nekoliko vendora s kojima smo razgovarali ima isti problem — klijenti prihvataju da je angažovanost važna, ali finansijskim direktorima to nije dovoljno. Jedan od govornika, konsultant iz Praga, predložio je pristup zasnovan na izračunavanju troška fluktuacije po poziciji kao polaznoj tački za sve ostale procene. To nije nova ideja, ali načina na koji je to razradio bio je konkretniji nego što smo mi do sada pokušavali. Razgovor nastavljamo.

Kada je reč o pravnim pitanjima vezanim za GDPR i praćenje rada, panel koji je moderirao advokat iz Bratislave privukao je izuzetno puno pažnje. Jasno je da kompanije koje nude ikakvo praćenje aktivnosti zaposlenih moraju da imaju mnogo solidniji pravni temelj nego što je to do sada bio standard u industriji. Ovo nije iznenađenje za nas, ali nas je učvrstilo u uverenju da ovo pitanje moramo rešiti sistemski, a ne slučaj po slučaj.

Vratili smo se s nekoliko kontakata i s više otvorenih pitanja nego što smo imali kad smo krenuli. Što je, zapravo, pravi cilj ovakvih događaja.
