title: Why We Track Confidence Distribution Across Shifts, Not Just Overall Accuracy
text:
When we talk to hospital IT teams or radiology managers about ClearFrame's performance, the first question is almost always about accuracy. What is the sensitivity? What is the specificity? Those numbers matter, but they do not tell you where your model is struggling or when it is struggling.

Here is something we noticed in the Radović deployment data: ClearFrame Bone's average confidence score on flagged studies is meaningfully lower on the overnight shift than during daytime hours. The overall sensitivity figures look similar across shifts, but the distribution of confidence scores is different. More flags in the overnight window fall in the 0.55–0.70 range — above our flagging threshold but not firmly above it.

The reason is not that the model behaves differently at night. It is that the case mix changes. Overnight, the department sees a higher proportion of trauma studies — falls, road accidents — where the anatomy is often positioned differently from a standard protocol study. Those cases are also the ones where our training data is thinner.

What we do with this: RadReview Dashboard now shows confidence distribution by shift as a standard panel for radiology leads. It is not an alarm — it is a prompt for a conversation. If the overnight distribution shifts over time as we add training data from those case types, that is a signal the model is improving in a specific area. If it does not shift, we know we have a data gap to address.

Tracking distribution rather than point estimates also helps with our active-learning queue. We are currently working on changes to how that queue routes cases, and the shift-level confidence data is one of the inputs we are using to understand which case types are generating the most repeated uncertainty. More on that in a later post.

title: Šta radimo i kako — TeraRoot usluge i tehnologija
text:
TeraRoot pravi senzore koji ostaju u tlu i prate koren tokom cele sezone. Ne merimo samo vlažnost ili temperaturu — merimo elektrohemijski otpor i reaktansu korenske zone da bismo zaključili šta koren u datom trenutku radi: da li prima fosfor, da li je pod stresom od suše, da li postoji zona zaražena patogenom.

Naša osnovna alatka je RhizoProbe S1. To je metalna šipka dužine 22 centimetra sa setom elektroda raspoređenih duž tela, zaštićenim kućištem od tehničke plastike. Farmer je postavi jednom, na početku vegetacije, gurajući je ručno ili malom letvom na željenu dubinu. Odatle pa do kraja sezone proba radi samostalno na baterijskom napajanju, šalje podatke svakih sat vremena na najbliži RhizoGateway prijemnik koji ih prosleđuje na naš server.

RhizoDash je veb aplikacija u kojoj farmer vidi kartu svojih parcela, grafik zdravlja korena po zonama i upozorenja kada sistem detektuje odstupanje od normalnog obrasca. Aplikacija ne daje savete u smislu 'dodaj još azota' — daje signal da nešto nije u redu i kada, a šta dalje odlučuje farmer ili agronomska služba.

Kalibracioni servis postoji zato što kukuruz sorte Zoran 450 i sorte Dunav 600 ne formiraju isti korenov sistem i naš senzor to 'vidi' drugačije. Za korisnike koji žele preciznije podatke nudimo jednokratno kalibracijsko merenje na njihovim parcelama pre sezone.

Naš API omogućava da se podaci iz RhizoDash-a uvezu u farmske upravljačke sisteme koje korisnici već koriste, bez potrebe da menjaju navike.

Tim čini dvadeset dva zaposlena u Novom Sadu. Direktorka razvoja hardvera je Jelena Marković, a za softverski deo odgovoran je Nikola Stanišić. Terenska mreža pokriva Vojvodinu i delove Srema.

title: TeraRoot završio pilot projekat sa gazdinstvom Bačka Polja — 120 sondi, jedna sezona
text:
U martu 2024. na imanju Bačka Polja d.o.o. u okolini Bečeja postavljeno je 120 RhizoProbe S1 sondi na parcelama pod kukuruzom i suncokretom. Pilot je trajao do sredine juna, a cilj je bio da proverimo kako sistem funkcioniše u komercijalnim uslovima — ne na probnom polju, nego tamo gde se stvarno radi.

Upravljač gazdinstva Stevan Mišković rekao je da je iznenađen korisnosću upozorenja o vodnom stresu: 'Sistem je dva puta javio problem ranije nego što smo ga mi uočili na terenu. Jedan od tih slučajeva doveo je do brzog navodnjavanja jednog bloka, verovatno smo time sačuvali prinos na oko sedam hektara.'

Tehnički tim TeraRoot-a konstatovao je tokom pilot projekta i problem koji smo već uočili u prethodnim sezonama: na teškim glinenim parcelama u delu bloka prema Tisi, šest sondi je pokazalo pad kvaliteta signala između osme i desete nedelje, što odgovara koroziji elektroda. Te sonde su zamenjene, ali incident potvrđuje da moramo rešiti taj problem pre sezone 2025.

Podatkovni sistem je tokom pilot projekta generisao ukupno oko 21 gigabajt sirovog senzorskog sadržaja za dva i po meseca. Prekoračenje cloud troška nije bilo dramatično u ovom manjem opsegu, ali je modelovanjem jasno da se pri punom kapacitetu od 600 i više sondi problem višestruko uvećava.

Bačka Polja d.o.o. potpisala je ugovor za punu sezonu 2025. sa proširenjem na 200 sondi. Zahvaljujemo timu na terenu na strpljenju i preciznoj povratnoj informaciji.

title: Zašto nam nije dosta što model objašnjava 51 posto — objašnjenje za nespecijaliste
text:
Pitanje koje često dobijamo od korisnika i investitora glasi: 'Vaš model radi — zašto još uvek nije dovoljno dobar?'

Objasniću konkretno.

Naša sonda meri električni otpor i reaktansu između dve elektrode u tlu. To su fizičke veličine. Iz njih pokušavamo da zaključimo koliko je aktivnog korena u blizini sonde i kako koren funkcioniše. Problem je u tome što tlo nije čista sredina — u njemu ima vode, minerala, mikroorganizama, organskih čestica i svega ostalog što utiče na električne karakteristike. Koren je tu negde unutra, ali signal koji dobijamo nije samo od korena.

Naš trenutni model, treniran na tri sezone podataka i referentnim uzorcima koje smo dobili destruktivnim kopanjem, objašnjava 51 posto varijanse merene biomase korena. To znači da polovina onoga što vidimo u podacima ostaje neobjašnjeno.

Za upozorenja o naglom vodnom stresu to je dovoljno — sistem detektuje brzu promenu i javlja alarm. Ali za preporuke o ishrani ili za poređenje dve parcele, tačnost od 51 posto je premalo.

Kako do boljeg modela? Pretpostavljamo da su tri moguća pravca: bolja ekstrakcija karakteristika iz spektra (ne koristimo sve što spektar nudi), bolji dizajn terenskih ogleda za prikupljanje referentnih podataka, i eventualno model koji uzima u obzir i tip tla i vrstu hibrida kao kontekstualne varijable.

To je razlog zašto tražimo saradnike — ne zato što je naš tim nekompetentан, nego zato što je problem na granici više disciplina i ne može ga rešiti jedna osoba sama.

Ako vas ova tema zanima ili imate iskustva sa spektralnim podacima iz tla, kontaktirajte nas.

title: CropView Adopted by Agro Dunav Cooperative Across 8,400 Hectares in Serbia
text:
AgroVid Solutions has signed a two-year platform agreement with Agro Dunav, a farmer cooperative based in Sremska Mitrovica that manages arable operations across 47 member farms totalling approximately 8,400 hectares of maize, sunflower and winter wheat.

The agreement covers full CropView platform access for all member farms, four scheduled drone scouting flights per season per farm, and integration of the CropView agronomic alert API with Agro Dunav's existing farm management records system.

Marko Filipović, field operations coordinator at Agro Dunav, said the cooperative had tested three platforms over the previous two seasons before settling on CropView. The main factor was the combination of satellite monitoring with drone follow-up in a single workflow, rather than having to move data between separate tools. He also noted that the CropView Field App's offline capability was important for members farming in areas with unreliable mobile coverage.

For AgroVid, the contract is the largest single agreement the company has signed to date by hectare coverage. Tatjana Vuković, head of customer accounts at AgroVid, said the cooperative model is one the company wants to develop further — a single technical onboarding process can bring in dozens of farms at once, and cooperative agronomists often become effective internal advocates for the platform.

Onboarding for Agro Dunav member farms began in January and is expected to be complete before the spring planting window. AgroVid's training team will run three on-site sessions at the cooperative's offices in Sremska Mitrovica during February.

title: What CropView Does — AgroVid Solutions
text:
CropView is a subscription platform for commercial arable farmers who need field-level information without having to manage multiple disconnected tools. You log in and see your parcels on a map. Each parcel has a current status — based on the latest satellite pass, any recent drone imagery you have uploaded or we have flown, and the weather forecast for that specific location. When something changes, you get an alert with enough context to decide whether you need to act.

The satellite layer updates every three to five days depending on cloud cover, using data from Sentinel-2 and PlanetScope. When satellite resolution is not enough — early-season stand assessment, detailed scouting after a storm, pre-harvest quality checks — our drone team can fly within 48 hours of a request, or you can fly yourself and upload directly through the Field App.

The Field App works offline. If you are in a valley with no signal, you can still log a scouting observation, take a photo and mark the GPS location. It syncs when you are back in coverage.

CropView is not built for smallholders. It is built for farms running 200 hectares and above, where the cost of a missed spray window or a late harvest decision is measured in thousands of euros, and where a farm manager oversees more parcels than one person can physically visit every week.

We currently cover Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina and North Macedonia. Support is available in Serbian, Bosnian and English. Pricing is per hectare per year with a minimum contract size; contact us for a quote based on your farm area and the services you need.

title: What We Learned Exhibiting at AgriConnect Balkans 2024 in Belgrade
text:
We had a stand at AgriConnect Balkans for the second year in a row this March. Last year we went mostly to see who else was in the market. This year we went to talk to farmers, and the conversations were more useful than we expected.

A few things stood out.

First, the gap between what farmers say they want in a survey and what they actually engage with at a trade fair is real. On paper, everyone wants better yield prediction. At the stand, what people kept asking about was the drone scouting turnaround — specifically, how fast they get a report after a flight and whether they can actually see problem areas marked on a map rather than described in text. We have known this anecdotally but hearing it from fifteen different people over two days reinforces it.

Second, Hungarian and Romanian interest was higher than we anticipated. We had four serious conversations with visitors from those countries, including a cooperative representative from near Debrecen and an input distributor based in Timișoara. Both already knew roughly what CropView does, which means word travels. Neither was ready to sign anything — they had regulatory questions about drone operations and data storage that we could not answer on the spot, which is a gap we are aware of and working to close.

Third, the competitive landscape is shifting. There are two platforms that did not exist two years ago now targeting roughly the same segment we serve in the Western Balkans. Neither has a local drone operations component, which is still a differentiator for us, but the satellite-plus-weather layer is becoming table stakes.

We will be back next year. If you were at the fair and want to pick up a conversation we started at the stand, drop us a line at office@agrovid.rs.

This is a part-time engagement — we expect roughly 20 to 30 hours of work over three to four months, with the possibility of an ongoing retainer if the relationship works well.

What we need help with:
— Reviewing and adapting our existing data-processing agreements for compliance with local GDPR implementation in Hungary and Romania, particularly around the storage and processing of georeferenced farm data
— Mapping out the steps and realistic timelines for registering as a commercial drone operator in both countries under EASA open and specific category rules and any national additions
— Identifying whether our current Serbian operator documentation and insurance coverage transfers in any meaningful way or whether we are starting fresh in each jurisdiction
— Producing a short practical checklist for each country that our operations team can follow

We are not looking for a lengthy legal opinion document. We need actionable guidance that a non-lawyer can use.

Preferred background:
— Familiarity with EASA drone regulation (UAS.OPEN, UAS.SPEC categories)
— Experience with cross-border data processing agreements in an EU context
— Some understanding of agricultural data or IoT data is a plus but not required
— Romanian or Hungarian language skills would be helpful but we can work in English

Engagement fee negotiable based on scope. Contact us at office@agrovid.rs with a short description of relevant experience.

title: O nama i uslugama – KartografTech
text:
KartografTech je studio za putnu kartografiju osnovan u Zrenjaninu 2019. godine. Naš posao je jednostavan: vozimo puteve, merimo ih preciznom opremom i od tih podataka pravimo mape koje navigacioni uređaji i ADAS sistemi mogu da koriste.

Krenuli smo od frustracije – kupovati mape od globalnih distributera za tržište Balkana znači plaćati za podatke koji su snimani pre tri ili četiri godine i koji ne beleže ni novije kružne tokove ni reklasifikovane lokalne puteve. Odlučili smo da to uradimo sami.

Danas naša baza podataka pokriva putnu mrežu Srbije, Bosne i Hercegovine i Crne Gore. Isporučujemo:

• HD putne mape u vlasničkom KTF formatu, pogodnom za ugradnju u navigacione uređaje
• ADAS slojeve sa geometrijom traka, nagibom i pozicijama saobraćajnih znakova
• Mape u prilagođenim formatima, uključujući OpenDRIVE, po posebnoj narudžbini
• Terenske survej usluge za kompanije kojima treba pokrivenost određene rute ili područja

Naši klijenti su proizvođači i integatori navigacionih sistema koji opremaju vozila u segmentu niže i srednje cene – tamo gde skupi licencni ugovori sa globalnim provajderima ne dolaze u obzir. Trudimo se da im ponudimo podatke koji su aktuelni, precizni i isporučeni na vreme.

Tim broji šest osoba. Osnivači Dragana i Miroslav Kolarević vode studio od prvog dana; Nikola Vranić odgovoran je za softver i formate podataka; Ana Petrović i Stevan Lukić rade kartografsku obradu i validaciju; Đorđe Mišković vodi terenska snimanja. Svi radimo iz istog malog ureda u Zrenjaninu, a veći deo radnog vremena provodimo ili na terenu ili ispred mapa.

Ako tražite pouzdan izvor putnih podataka za Zapadni Balkan, pišite nam na office@kartograftech.rs.

title: Tražimo: Inženjer za geoprostorne podatke i formate mapa (m/ž)
text:
KartografTech traži jednu osobu koja bi pojačala naš mali tim na poslovima razvoja i konverzije mapa.

Šta radimo: Prikupljamo survej podatke s terena, obrađujemo ih u PostGIS bazi i isporučujemo klijentima u različitim formatima. Naš primarni format je vlasnički binarni KTF; sve češće klijenti traže OpenDRIVE i druge otvorene formate.

Gde nam treba pomoć:
– Razvoj i poboljšanje in-house alata za konverziju KTF → OpenDRIVE
– Validacija topologije putnih mreža, posebno raskrsnica i kružnih tokova
– Pisanje skripti za automatizovanu detekciju grešaka u geometriji traka
– Po potrebi, analiza satelitskih ili avionskih snimaka radi detekcije promena na terenu

Šta koristimo svakodnevno:
– Python (shapely, pyproj, gdal)
– PostGIS / PostgreSQL
– QGIS
– Git
– Interni KTF parser (dokumentacija dostupna pri onboardingu)

Poželjno poznavanje OpenDRIVE 1.6+ specifikacije i osnova geometrije krivulja (Bezier, clothoid). Nije obavezno, ali dobrodošlo: iskustvo s LiDAR point cloud podacima ili ROS-om.

Nudimo:
– Puno radno vreme, rad u Zrenjaninu (delimično moguće hibridno)
– Plata 90.000–110.000 RSD neto, zavisno od iskustva
– Mali tim bez nepotrebne birokratije
– Realne šanse da vaš kod direktno utiče na proizvod koji koriste pravi klijenti

Prijave slati na posao@kartograftech.rs sa kratkim opisom relevantnog iskustva i, ako postoji, linkom na javni repozitorijum.

title: Tražimo: Terinski survej tehničar (m/ž)
text:
Naš tim za terenska snimanja traži pojačanje. Pozicija je prigodna za osobu koja voli voziti, ne smeta joj rad na otvorenom i zanima je kako nastaju digitalne mape.

Šta bi radio/la:
– Upravljanje survej vozilom po unapred definisanim rutama u Srbiji i regionu
– Pokretanje, nadgledanje i osnovna dijagnostika LiDAR i GNSS opreme tokom snimanja
– Vođenje terenske dokumentacije i dnevnih izveštaja
– Poluautonomna kontrola snimljenih deonica mobilnom Android aplikacijom
– Povremena ručna validacija podataka u QGIS-u (obuka se pruža)

Uslovi:
– Vozačka dozvola B kategorije, najmanje tri godine iskustva
– Spremnost na višednevna putovanja (troškovi su pokriveni)
– Osnovna kompjuterska pismenost
– Prethodno iskustvo s terenskim merenjima ili geodezijom je prednost, ali nije uslov

Nudimo:
– Puno radno vreme
– Plata 65.000–75.000 RSD neto
– Naknada za terenske dane, dnevnice po važećim propisima
– Vozilo i oprema su naši

Radno mesto: Zrenjanin, s čestim izlascima na teren širom Srbije i regiona.

Zainteresovani kandidati mogu poslati prijavu na posao@kartograftech.rs. Razgovaramo sa svima koji se jave u roku od tri nedelje od objave.

title: Potpisali smo trogodišnji ugovor s Adria Drive Systems
text:
Drago nam je da objavimo da smo u aprilu 2024. potpisali trogodišnji ugovor o licenciranju mapa s kompanijom Adria Drive Systems iz Sarajeva.

Adria Drive Systems integriše navigacione i ADAS sisteme u vozila nekoliko regionalnih proizvođača karoserija i autobusa. Dosad su koristili mape jednog austrijskog provajdera čije su ažuriranje i tehnička podrška za Bosnu i Hercegovinu bili neredovni. Nakon šestomesečnog testnog perioda u kome su naši HD podaci pokazali manje grešaka na lokalnoj putnoj mreži u BiH nego konkurentski izvor, odlučili su da pređu na nas.

Ugovorom je predviđena godišnja isporuka ažuriranih mapa za BiH i Srbiju u KTF formatu, kao i prioritetan odgovor na prijave grešaka u roku od sedam radnih dana.

Ovo je naš do sada najveći klijentski ugovor po vrednosti, i za nas znači stabilnost u narednom periodu, ali i jasnu obavezu da ažurnost podataka podignemo na viši nivo. Upravo zbog toga intenziviraemo potragu za rešenjima koja bi nam omogućila brže otkrivanje promena na terenu između dva ciklusa surveja.

Hvala timu Adria Drive Systems na strpljenju tokom testnog perioda i na otvorenim povratnim informacijama koje su nam pomogle da popravimo pokrivenost nekoliko koridora u Federaciji BiH.

title: Šta smo naučili na Map Data Balkans susretu u Beogradu
text:
Početkom maja prisustvovali smo Map Data Balkans susretu koji je organizovalo udruženje AutoNav Southeast u Beogradu. Bila su to dva dana razgovora između proizvođača navigacionih sistema, dobavljača podataka i nekoliko kompanija koje razvijaju softvere za vozila.

Najviše vremena proveli smo u razgovorima oko dva pitanja koja su se ponavljala: kako smanjiti vreme između pojave promene na terenu i njenog odražavanja u mapi, i kako da manji dobavljači podataka budu relevantni u trenutku kada simulacioni softveri sve glasnije traže OpenDRIVE.

Prvo pitanje nam je blisko – sami se borimo s tim. Čuli smo od jedne slovenačke firme da eksperimentišu s detekcijom promena koristeći javno dostupne satelitske snimke niske rezolucije kao signal za to gde treba poslati survej vozilo. Ideja je gruba, ali logična: ne moraš da znaš tačno šta se promenilo, dovoljno je da znaš gde da pogledaš. To nam je dalo materijal za razmišljanje.

Drugo pitanje nas pogađa direktno – tri naša klijenta traže OpenDRIVE i naš alat za konverziju još uvek nije na nivou koji bi zadovoljio ADAS simulacione zahteve. Razgovarali smo s dvojicom inženjera koji su radili na sličnim problemima i obojica su rekli isto: topologija raskrsnica mora biti eksplicitno modelirana u izvornom formatu, ne rekonstruisana pri konverziji. To je potvrda onoga što naš Nikola već neko vreme govori.

Vratili smo se iz Beograda s nekoliko kontakata i s jasnijom slikom gde nam je najhitnije da nađemo pomoć. Ako ste radili na OpenDRIVE konverziji ili na detekciji promena na putnoj mreži i zanima vas razgovor, pišite nam.

title: KartografTech prisustvuje NTP Demo Danu u Novom Sadu
text:
U oktobru 2024. učestvujemo na Demo Danu koji organizuje Naučno-tehnološki park Novi Sad. Ovo je prva formalna prilika da kao firma predstavimo naše izazove zajednici istraživača i inženjera koji rade u okviru parka.

Predstavićemo tri konkretna tehnička i poslovna problema na kojima nam treba podrška:

1. Kako automatizovati ili ubrzati detekciju promena na putnoj mreži između dva survej ciklusa, kako bismo smanjili troškove i povećali ažurnost mapa.

2. Kako popraviti konverziju mapa iz našeg internog formata u OpenDRIVE, posebno u delu modeliranja topologije raskrsnica, da bismo mogli da isporučimo podatke za ADAS simulaciju.

3. Kako naći put do prvih kupaca ili partnera na tržištu Evropske unije, gde nemamo postojeće kontakte ni reference.

Nismo akademska firma i ne tražimo istraživački projekat koji će da traje godinama – tražimo ljude koji razumeju ove probleme i s kojima možemo da razgovaramo konkretno. Ako izađe i jedna saradnja od ovog događaja, smatraćemo ga uspešnim.

Demo Dan se održava u prostorijama NTP Novi Sad. Zainteresovani istraživači ili timovi mogu nas kontaktirati unapred na office@kartograftech.rs da dogovorimo kratak razgovor pre ili posle zvaničnog programa.

title: What We Do — Orbis Edukacija
text:
Orbis Edukacija builds learning software and materials for primary schools in Vojvodina where children grow up using both Serbian and Hungarian every day. We started in 2019 because the family behind the company had sat through enough parent evenings to notice that digital tools either ignored Hungarian entirely or handled it as an afterthought. We thought there was a better way to do it.

Our main product is OrbisČitanje / OrbisOlvasás, a reading-comprehension app for children in grades one through four. A pupil can work through a story and its exercises in Serbian, switch to Hungarian, or move between both within a single session. The content is not translated — each language version is written separately by someone who teaches in that language, so the vocabulary and examples feel natural rather than borrowed.

We also make OrbisMatematika / OrbisMatemtika, which covers number sense, basic operations, and word problems for the first three grades. The word problems are localised properly — names, places, and units that children in this region will recognise.

For schools that prefer paper, we produce printed workbook sets that follow the same structure as the app. Some teachers use both; others use only the books. We do not mind either way.

All of our digital tools run on Android tablets. We keep the interface simple: large buttons, clear audio, and no in-app purchases or advertising. A child can pick up a tablet for the first time and get started without a tutorial.

Schools buy annual licences through our online portal. A licence covers unlimited pupils at one school and gives the head teacher and class teachers access to a progress dashboard. We offer a free 30-day trial for any school that wants to test the app before committing.

If you run a school in Vojvodina and want to talk, contact us at skole@orbisedukacija.rs.

title: Junior Android / Flutter Developer — Subotica (full-time)
text:
We are a small edtech company in Subotica and we are looking for a developer to join our four-person team. The work is mostly Flutter, with some native Android when we need to get closer to the hardware.

What you would do day to day:

title: Freelance Hungarian-Language Curriculum Reviewer (part-time, ongoing)
text:
We are looking for one or two Hungarian-speaking primary school teachers or retired teachers who can review and pilot our Hungarian-language reading exercises on a freelance basis.

The context: we have been getting consistent feedback from schools that our Hungarian reading exercises are harder for pupils than the Serbian equivalents at the same grade level. We have session data that supports this. We have already revised the vocabulary lists once, but the gap has not closed. We need someone who can sit down with the actual exercise texts, read them as a teacher would, and give us honest structured feedback — not just impressions, but specific observations about where the difficulty sits.

What the work involves:
- Reading through exercise sets for grades 1–4 (we send PDF drafts)
- Completing a review sheet we provide, covering vocabulary, sentence length, task type, and sequencing
- Optionally: piloting exercises with your own class or a class you have access to and reporting back on how pupils responded
- One or two video calls per month to discuss findings with our curriculum team

We expect this to be roughly 6–10 hours per month. We pay 2,500 RSD per hour. Work is ongoing with no fixed end date, but we review the arrangement every six months.

Requirements:
- Active or recently retired primary school teacher
- Native or near-native Hungarian; Serbian also needed for communication with our team
- Based in Vojvodina (not a strict requirement, but it helps to understand the local context)

If this sounds like something you can do, write to nastavnici@orbisedukacija.rs with a few lines about your background.

title: What We Learned at Učimo Zajedno 2024 in Novi Sad
text:
We had a stand at Učimo Zajedno 2024, the regional educational fair held in Novi Sad in early April. It was the third time we exhibited there and probably the most useful one yet, for reasons that had less to do with new leads and more to do with conversations we did not expect to have.

The practical result: we spoke to representatives from 14 schools we had not previously contacted, and three of those have since asked for trial accounts. We also met two other small publishers working in minority-language education in the region. We have not done anything formal with either of them, but it is useful to know they exist.

The more interesting part was a roundtable session on the second day about digital tools in bilingual classrooms. We joined as participants rather than presenters. Several teachers said something that we have heard before but had not taken seriously enough: they trust software more when they can see that the people who made it understand what a mixed-language classroom actually feels like. They were not talking about credentials. They meant small things — whether the interface switches languages in a way that feels natural, whether the audio sounds like someone from here, whether the example sentences mention places children in Vojvodina have actually heard of.

We think we do some of this well and some of it less well. The session was a reminder that the content side of the work matters as much as the technical side, maybe more.

One thing we will change based on this trip: we are going to add a short section to our website where teachers can hear audio samples from the app before they request a trial. Several people at the fair asked whether they could hear the Hungarian narration before committing to a demo. We did not have a good answer for that. We will.

title: 31 Schools in the 2023–24 Year: A Quick Look Back
text:
The school year ended last week and we wanted to put a few numbers down in writing, mostly for ourselves, but also for anyone curious about what a small edtech company in Subotica actually looks like in practice.

In the 2023–24 school year, 31 schools in Vojvodina held active licences for our apps. That is up from 19 the previous year. Together, roughly 4,200 pupils used OrbisČitanje / OrbisOlvasás or OrbisMatematika / OrbisMatemtika at some point during the year. The schools are spread across Subotica, Kanjiža, Senta, Ada, Mali Iđoš, and a handful of smaller settlements.

The number we are most pleased about: 24 of those 31 schools renewed their licences for next year before the end of June. That matters to us more than the raw growth number, because it means the schools that tried us are choosing to continue.

The number we are least pleased about: Hungarian-language reading exercise completion rates averaged 58% across all schools, compared to 81% for the Serbian equivalents. We have been watching this gap for two terms now. We changed the vocabulary lists after the first term and the gap barely moved. We do not yet know what is causing it. We are treating it as the main technical and content problem to solve over the summer and into the autumn.

We also shipped the teacher dashboard in February, later than planned. The delay was mostly our fault — we underestimated how much variation there was in how different schools wanted to see their data. The version we shipped covers the basics and teachers are using it. We will add the comparison view and the export feature in September.

Thank you to everyone who sent feedback this year, including the teachers who told us things we did not want to hear. That is the most useful kind.

title: What We Do — Adrialink Technologies
text:
Adrialink Technologies has been delivering IT services to European financial institutions since 1998. We are based in Novi Sad, Serbia, with a client-facing office in Rotterdam and a delivery team in Belgrade. Our 312 staff work across three main service lines.

Managed Cloud Operations. We take responsibility for the cloud environments our clients rely on — provisioning, monitoring, incident response, and cost management. Most of our client workloads run on AWS or Azure. We use Kubernetes, Terraform, and a GitLab-based pipeline to keep deployments consistent and auditable. Our SLA templates are aligned with the operational risk requirements typical in EU financial regulation.

Legacy Modernisation. A significant portion of financial infrastructure in Western Europe still runs on mainframe systems built in the 1980s and 1990s. We have experience migrating COBOL and PL/I applications to Java-based microservices without disrupting live operations. We do this in phases, running old and new systems in parallel until confidence is high enough to cut over.

Staff Augmentation. Clients who need to expand a specific capability without a permanent hire can bring in Adrialink engineers to work directly within their teams. Our engineers follow client processes and tools, and we manage HR, payroll, and compliance from our side.

We work with clients on long-term contracts, typically three to five years, because the kind of work we do — operating critical systems and migrating core applications — does not lend itself to short engagements. Our average client relationship is nine years.

If you are a financial institution looking for a dependable IT partner in the EU regulatory environment, we are happy to talk through your situation without any obligation.

title: Senior Java Architect (multiple positions) — Novi Sad or Remote Serbia
text:
Adrialink Technologies is looking for experienced Java architects to join project teams working on modernisation and cloud migration engagements for EU financial clients. We have multiple open roles and are actively interviewing.

What the work involves:
You will be the technical lead on one of our active migration or cloud projects. That means making architecture decisions, reviewing code produced by mid and junior engineers, communicating technical trade-offs to project managers and occasionally to clients, and keeping the project aligned with its quality and timeline targets. You will not be spending most of your time in meetings — we expect senior architects to be hands-on.

The technical environment:
Our standard stack is Java 17 and 21 with Spring Boot and Spring Cloud. Containerisation is Kubernetes, deployed via Helm charts. We use Terraform for infrastructure and Jenkins or GitLab CI for pipelines. Our clients are in financial services, so experience with transaction processing, data consistency under load, or regulated environments is a genuine advantage. Several active projects involve migrating legacy COBOL logic to Java, so familiarity with that type of work — or a willingness to learn quickly — is relevant.

What we are looking for:
— At least eight years of professional Java development, with at least three in an architect or technical lead role
— Solid understanding of distributed systems, including failure modes and consistency trade-offs
— Experience with cloud platforms, preferably AWS or Azure, at a level beyond basic deployments
— Ability to write clear technical documentation
— Working English; Dutch or German is a bonus but not required

What we offer:
Competitive base salary (we are reviewing our grade bands and are open to discussion), full benefits package, hybrid working, and the option to work fully remotely from anywhere in Serbia. Novi Sad office access for those who prefer it.

To apply, send your CV to careers@adrialink.rs with the subject line 'Java Architect 2024'.

title: QA Engineer — Test Automation (Java / Financial Systems)
text:
We are looking for a QA engineer with a strong automation background to join one of our longest-running migration projects. The project involves moving a large insurance client's core processing platform from a COBOL mainframe to a microservices architecture in Java. The QA challenge on this project is significant and the work is technically interesting.

The specific problem you would be working on:
The migrated codebase currently has 34% automated test coverage. Manual regression takes three weeks per release cycle. That is too slow for the release cadence the client wants to reach. Your job would be to analyse the existing codebase and test data, prioritise which areas need automated coverage most urgently, write those tests, and help the rest of the team do the same. You would also be expected to identify where the manual process can be reduced or eliminated entirely.

Technical environment:
Java 17, Spring Boot microservices, JUnit 5, Testcontainers, PostgreSQL, Jenkins pipelines. The legacy side involves IBM Z transaction logs and partial COBOL source that we use to validate business logic. You do not need to know COBOL, but you need to be comfortable working with incomplete documentation and inferring business rules from data.

What we are looking for:
— Three or more years in a QA automation role working with Java-based systems
— Experience writing integration and contract tests, not just unit tests
— Familiarity with test data management, including generating synthetic financial data for testing
— Good instincts for prioritisation when you cannot automate everything at once
— Clear written communication — you will be producing test plans and coverage reports for a non-technical client stakeholder

Nice to have: experience in financial services, insurance, or any regulated domain.

This is a full-time position based in Novi Sad, with hybrid flexibility. Salary is negotiable based on experience. Send applications to careers@adrialink.rs.

title: Adrialink renews managed services contract with Venthoven Assurance for four years
text:
Adrialink Technologies has signed a four-year renewal of its managed cloud services agreement with Venthoven Assurance, a mid-sized insurance group based in Antwerp. The original contract began in 2017 and covers the operation and monitoring of Venthoven's policy administration and claims processing infrastructure, which runs on AWS across two European regions.

Under the renewed agreement, Adrialink will also take on responsibility for a platform modernisation workstream that Venthoven had previously managed in-house. This includes migrating several batch processing components from a legacy mainframe environment to a containerised Java stack — work that Adrialink has been preparing for over the past 18 months in parallel with the standard operations contract.

Miroslav Gajić, CEO of Adrialink, said the renewal reflects the kind of client relationship the company has built its model around. 'Venthoven's internal teams know our engineers by name. That familiarity matters on a platform that processes claims around the clock. We are not starting over every few years.'

The contract is one of Adrialink's three largest by revenue. The company declined to disclose financial terms.

title: What we have learned running financial workloads on Kubernetes for three years
text:
Three years ago we moved the first of our managed client workloads from virtual machines to Kubernetes. At the time, the decision felt straightforward: better resource utilisation, consistent deployments, easier scaling. The reality has been more complicated, and we think it is worth writing down what we have actually found.

Scaling is harder than it looks for financial workloads. The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler works well for web-facing services with unpredictable traffic. It works less well for back-office financial processing, where load is highly predictable — heavy overnight batch, a morning peak when markets open, quiet afternoons — but the default CPU-based triggers do not know that. We have ended up with clusters that scale up for a spike that is already over and stay inflated for an hour afterwards. The cost impact over a quarter is not trivial. We are actively looking at ways to incorporate time-based scheduling and dependency-aware scaling, but we have not solved this yet.

Test environments are a persistent headache. Financial systems have complex state — account balances, policy records, transaction histories. Spinning up a realistic test environment in a Kubernetes namespace is much harder than it sounds when the data has to be synthetic but behaviourally accurate. We have invested in Testcontainers-based setups and they help, but generating synthetic financial data that actually exercises the edge cases in the business logic remains a manual effort on most projects.

The operational benefits are real. Deployment consistency has improved significantly. Rollbacks that used to require a phone call to a data centre contact now take two minutes. Onboarding a new engineer onto a client environment is faster because the infrastructure is described in code. These gains are genuine and they compound over time.

We are still learning. Anyone who tells you Kubernetes is a solved problem for production financial workloads is either very advanced or not being honest about their situation.

title: What Four Months of Hiring for a Cloud Architect Role Has Taught Us
text:
We started interviewing for a senior cloud architect in February. It is now June and the role is not filled. We thought it was worth writing down what we have observed, because we suspect other companies in Vojvodina are running into the same problem.

The supply of qualified candidates is not the issue. We have spoken to eight people in the past four months who had the right skills — strong AWS and Terraform backgrounds, experience making infrastructure decisions in production environments, and the communication ability to work with clients directly. These are real engineers, not people who have studied for certifications and never shipped anything.

The problem is speed and salary. In two cases, candidates we had spoken to once received formal offers from German or Dutch companies before we had finished our internal discussion about whether to proceed. In both cases the competing offers were 20 to 30 percent higher base salaries, fully remote. In the remaining cases, candidates were already in late-stage conversations with other employers when we reached them.

We have tried adjusting. We made our process shorter. We increased the benefits package. We added more flexibility on office attendance. We have not been able to close the salary gap on base compensation, and for candidates who can work remotely for a Western European company, that gap is real and we understand why it matters.

What we have not tried yet is developing the capability from within. We have engineers who are technically strong and interested in moving toward infrastructure architecture. The gap is seniority and breadth of experience. We are thinking about whether a structured external collaboration — mentoring, joint project work, that kind of arrangement — could accelerate that path faster than we could do it alone.

We are genuinely open to unconventional approaches to this problem. If you have ideas or have solved something similar, we would be interested in talking.

title: Elektro Morava Signs Three-Year Contract for GridSense Assets and Outage
text:
We are pleased to announce that Elektro Morava d.o.o., the distribution operator covering a network of roughly 280,000 metering points in central Serbia, has signed a three-year managed-service contract for GridSense Assets and GridSense Outage.

The contract follows a six-month pilot that began in the second half of 2023. During the pilot, Elektro Morava's planning team migrated approximately 14,000 transformer and switchgear records from their previous GIS system into GridSense Assets, and the control room began using GridSense Outage alongside their existing SCADA console.

According to Elektro Morava's technical director Radomir Stanković, the main reason for signing the full contract was the outage reporting functionality. Under Serbian regulatory rules, operators must submit structured interruption reports each quarter. The manual process previously took the planning department four to six working days. With GridSense Outage, that has come down to under a day, because the structured log entries made during each event are already in the right format for the regulatory template.

For us, this is our largest single contract to date and our first customer in Serbia outside the Vojvodina region. It also gives us a deployment at a scale — network size, data volume, and user count — that will test parts of GridSense Assets we have not stressed before. We are treating the first six months of the full contract as a hardening period and have assigned two engineers to be on call for Elektro Morava issues specifically.

Milena Vranić, who led the sales process, noted that the pilot structure was essential: 'Utilities do not sign multiyear contracts based on demos. They need to see the software working on their own data, with their own staff. The six-month pilot was the right approach and we will use it again.'

We thank the Elektro Morava team for their patience during the migration and their clear feedback throughout the pilot.

title: What We Do — GridSense Analytics
text:
GridSense Analytics builds operational software for electricity distribution companies in the Western Balkans. We have been at it since 2017, and every product we ship comes out of direct conversations with the people who run distribution networks day to day — control room operators, planning engineers, and the maintenance crews who go out in the rain to inspect switchgear.

Our core product is GridSense Assets, an asset register that replaces the mixture of spreadsheets, paper binders, and disconnected GIS files that most operators inherited from the privatisation era. It stores equipment records, inspection results, and network topology together, and it keeps a full change history so that operators can answer audit questions without digging through email archives.

GridSense Outage sits alongside Assets and gives control rooms a live dashboard of faults and interruptions. When something trips, operators see location, affected customers, and a structured log they can annotate in real time. That log feeds the outage analysis reports that regulators in Serbia and Bosnia require, which saves planning departments several days of manual work per quarter.

GridSense Network Planner is our newest tool. It lets network planning engineers run load-flow scenarios on their medium-voltage grids without sending data to a consultant in another city. They import their topology from Assets, set up a scenario — say, adding a new industrial customer or a solar farm — and get results in minutes.

All three products run on Azure and are offered as a managed service. We handle updates, backups, and security patching. Operators connect through a browser; there is nothing to install on site beyond our DataBridge agent, which pulls data from SCADA and metering systems.

We are based at the NTP Novi Sad building, which puts us close to the university and to other technology companies working on infrastructure problems. If you work for a distribution operator and want to see a demo, get in touch with our sales contact Milena Vranić.

title: What Dissolved Gas Analysis Actually Tells You — and What It Does Not
text:
We have been talking to maintenance teams at distribution operators for several months about transformer health data, and we keep running into the same situation: the operator has years of dissolved gas analysis results sitting in a spreadsheet, and nobody is doing much with them beyond checking whether individual readings cross a single threshold.

Dissolved gas analysis, for those unfamiliar, is a test performed on the insulating oil inside oil-filled transformers. When insulation degrades or electrical faults develop, specific gases dissolve into the oil. Measuring those gases — hydrogen, methane, ethylene, acetylene, and a few others — gives you a chemical signature of what is happening inside the transformer without opening it up.

The classical approach is to compare individual gas concentrations against published limit values. If ethylene is above a certain level, flag the transformer for inspection. This is a reasonable first step, but it misses two things.

First, trend matters more than a single reading. A transformer with ethylene at 80 percent of the limit and rising quickly is more concerning than one that has been stable at 110 percent of the limit for three years. Single-point thresholds cannot capture that.

Second, DGA does not stand alone. A transformer running at high load in summer will generate more gas than the same transformer at half load in winter, simply because of temperature. Load history changes how you interpret the chemical picture.

This is the gap we are trying to close with the predictive maintenance work we are developing. We are not trying to replace DGA — it is a well-established and genuinely useful test. We are trying to combine DGA trends with load history to produce something more useful than a threshold alarm: a relative risk ranking across a whole transformer population, updated each time new results come in.

We will write more about the modelling approach once we have results worth sharing. If you work on transformer maintenance and want to talk about your data, contact Dragan Milošević.

title: Machine Learning Engineer (part-time / project) — GridSense Analytics
text:
We have two concrete modelling problems that are beyond what our current team can handle alone, and we are looking for an ML engineer who wants to work on them, either as a part-time contractor or through a structured project arrangement.

Problem one: transformer health scoring. We have dissolved gas analysis results and multi-year load data for roughly four hundred distribution transformers, plus a labelled failure history. We need a model that produces a ranked failure-risk score per transformer, updated when new DGA results arrive. The output needs to be simple enough that a maintenance planner can understand why a transformer is flagged.

Problem two: day-ahead feeder load forecasting. Rooftop PV has made standard load profiles unreliable on some feeders. We have half-hourly smart meter data, weather observations, and licensed irradiance estimates. We need a forecast model that runs nightly on Azure, produces per-feeder predictions for the following day, and achieves below fifteen percent MAPE on recent test data.

For both problems we can provide clean, documented datasets, access to our Azure environment, and regular meetings with our domain engineers. We are not looking for a paper; we need working code that our team can maintain.

You should have:
— Strong Python and experience with scikit-learn, XGBoost, or similar
— Experience taking a model from notebook to a scheduled production job
— Willingness to engage with the domain — you will need to understand what dissolved gas ratios mean and why feeder topology matters

This is not a full-time permanent hire. Duration is approximately eight to twelve months. We are open to different arrangements including thesis co-supervision if that structure fits. Contact Dragan Milošević at d.milosevic@gridsense.rs.

title: O nama i uslugama — Agrosan IoT
text:
Agrosan IoT je sombarska firma koja projektuje, sklapa i isporučuje merne stanice za praćenje uslova u polju. Osnovali smo je 2021. godine Dragoljub i Marko Veselinović, otac i sin, s idejom da malim i srednje velikim gazdinstvima u Vojvodini damo pristup podacima kakve do tada nisu mogli da priušte.

Šta radimo

Naše stanice mere temperaturu zemljišta na dubini od 10 i 30 centimetara, temperaturu i relativnu vlažnost vazduha na visini od 2 metra, dnevnu količinu padavina i jačinu sunčevog zračenja. Podaci se šalju bežično putem LoRaWAN mreže i dostupni su u realnom vremenu kroz naš web portal i mobilnu aplikaciju.

Kome prodajemo

Najveći deo naše opreme ide zemljoradničkim zadrugama i porodičnim gazdinstvima s površinom između 50 i 500 hektara. Zadružni sistemi cenimo jer jednom instalacijom pokrivaju veći broj članova koji dele trošak, a svaki član vidilac sopstvenu parcelu.

Kako radimo

Svaku stanicu sklapamo sami u radionici u Somboru. Pre isporuke svaki uređaj prolazi trodnevni test u klimatskoj komori — simuliramo temperaturne cikluse i proveravamo da nema curenja napona ni vlage. Nakon isporuke nudimo godišnji servisni ugovor koji uključuje jednu fizičku proveru na terenu i besplatnu zamenu senzora u slučaju kvara.

Zašto baš mi

Nisamo distributeri strane opreme. Svaki firmware i svaki deo portala napisali smo sami, pa možemo brzo da reagujemo kada kupac ima poseban zahtev. Dragoljub je proveo trideset godina u poljoprivredi pre nego što smo osnovali firmu — znamo šta farmer zapravo treba da vidi ujutro pre nego što izađe na njivu.

title: Tražimo: inženjer firmvera i embedded sistema (pola radnog vremena ili honorarno)
text:
Agrosan IoT traži iskusnog inženjera firmvera koji bi nam pomogao da unapredimo pouzdanost i energetsku efikasnost naših mernih stanica.

O poslu

Trenutno naše stanice rade na ESP32 mikrokontroleru s firmverom pisanim u C-u. Sistem funkcioniše, ali imamo nekoliko otvorenih problema koje ne stižemo da rešimo sami pored tekućih narudžbina: optimizacija sleep modova da se smanji potrošnja u toku noći, robusnije upravljanje greškom pri slanju paketa preko LoRaWAN-a i bolje logovanje dijagnostičkih podataka koji bi nam pomogli da na daljinu prepoznamo kvar senzora pre nego što kupac uopšte primeti.

Šta nudimo

Posao je zamišljen kao honorarni angažman, otprilike 40 do 60 sati mesečno, s mogućnošću prelaska na puno radno vreme ako obim posla poraste. Radite pretežno od kuće, s dolaskom u Sombor jednom mesečno. Plata je dogovornog karaktera i u skladu s tržišnom stopom za ovaj profil.

Šta tražimo

— Praktično iskustvo s ESP32 ili sličnim ARM/Xtensa mikrokontrolerima
— Pisanje firmvera u C-u, poznavanje FreeRTOS-a je prednost
— Razumevanje LoRaWAN protokola i TTN ili sličnog network servera
— Iskustvo s mernim senzorima (I2C, SPI, UART interfejsi)
— Nije potrebno iskustvo u poljoprivredi

Šta ne tražimo

Ne tražimo akademske kvalifikacije — tražimo nekoga ko zna da otvori osciloskop i pročita signal. Portfolio projekata ili GitHub profil vredi više od diplome.

Kontakt: posalji mejl na marko.veselinovic@agrosan-iot.rs s kratkim opisom projekata na kojima si radio.

title: Isporučili smo 60 stanica Zadruzi Tisa — najveća narudžbina do sada
text:
U martu 2024. završili smo isporuku i instalaciju 60 mernih stanica AgroSen-1 za Zadrugu Tisa iz okoline Odžaka. Ovo je naša najveća pojedinačna narudžbina od osnivanja firme.

Zadruga Tisa obuhvata 43 zadrugara koji zajedno obrađuju oko 1.800 hektara, pretežno kukuruz, suncokret i pšenicu. Predsednik zadruge Slobodan Ćirić rekao nam je da su dugo tražili rešenje koje bi mogli da priušte i koje ne zahteva poseban IT tim za održavanje.

Instalacija je trajala sedam radnih dana. Marko i dva naša saradnika su obišli sve lokacije, postavili stanice i povezali svaki uređaj s portalom. Svakom zadругaru je demonstrirana aplikacija na telefonu.

Tehničke napomene

Za ovu instalaciju koristili smo vlastiti LoRaWAN gateway koji smo postavili na silosi zadruge, čime smo pokrili radijus od oko 8 kilometara bez oslanjanja na komercijalne operatere. Svih 60 stanica slalo je podatke stabilno tokom prvog meseca rada.

Šta smo naučili

Ovaj projekat je pokazao da nam treba bolji alat za planiranje napajanja pre terena — dve stanice postavljene na severno orijentisanim međama pokazale su nižu napunjenost baterije nego što smo predvideli. Nismo imali kvar, ali morali smo da repozicioniramo solarne panele u drugoj poseti. Ovo je ubrzalo našu odluku da potražimo sistemsku pomoć oko modela dimenzioniranja napajanja.

title: Tražimo: asistent za sklapanje i testiranje elektronike (puno radno vreme, Sombor)
text:
Zbog porasta broja narudžbina za sezonu 2024. tražimo još jednu osobu koja bi radila u našoj radionici u Somboru na sklapanju i testiranju mernih stanica.

O poslu

Radionica je smeštena u Somboru. Radite sa šablonima i uputstvima koje smo sami napravili — iskustvo u elektronici je korisno ali nije neophodno ako ste pažljivi i uredni. Posao uključuje lemljenje THT i SMD komponenti na PCB pločama, kabliranje i ugradnju u kućišta, trodnevno testiranje gotovih stanica u klimatskoj komori i pakovanje za isporuku.

Uslovi

Puno radno vreme, rad u jednoj smeni. Plata počinje od 65.000 dinara neto mesečno i raste s iskustvom. Nudimo i obuku u prvom mesecu.

Profil kandidata

— Uredno i precizno rukovanje malim komponentama
— Osnovno poznavanje elektronike ili iskustvo u montaži (nije obavezno)
— Vozačka dozvola B kategorije (terenske posete su retke ali ih ima)
— Poželjno: stanovanje u Somboru ili okolini do 20 km

Firma je mala i neformalna — za sva pitanja zovite Dragoljuba direktno na broj koji je naveden u kontaktu na sajtu.

title: Zašto naše stanice ponekad dozvole vlagu unutra — i šta radimo po tom pitanju
text:
Ovo nije ugodna tema za pisanje, ali smatramo da naši kupci zaslužuju da znaju šta se dešava i šta radimo da to popravimo.

U toku zimske sezone 2023–2024. zamenili smo 34 stanice pod garancijom jer se kondenzat skupio unutar kućišta i oštetio konektore na elektronskoj ploči. Sve te stanice imaju IP67 sertifikovana kućišta i brtvljenje koje odgovara specifikaciji. Ipak, problem postoji i ne možemo da ga ignorišemo.

Šta smo do sada probali

Dodali smo vrećice silikagela pri sklapanju — privremeno pomoglo, ali gelu treba zamena na svakih nekoliko meseci što nije praktično na terenu. Pregledali smo 12 vraćenih kućišta i nismo pronašli vidljivo oštećenje brtve. Sumnjamo da su u pitanju termički ciklusi — dnevno zagrevanje kućišta i noćno hlađenje verovatno pumpaju vlagu kroz naslage koje nisu vidljive golim okom.

Gde smo sada

Prikupili smo fotografije svih oštećenih ploča, podatke senzora iz perioda kvara i specifikacije materijala kućišta. Razgovaramo s NTP Novi Sad o mogućoj saradnji s nekim ko se bavi materijalom i termomehanikom — potrebna nam je nečija stručnost, naša sopstvena analiza je stigla do zida.

Šta kupci treba da znaju

Garancija važi i dalje pokriva ovaj kvar bez pitanja. Ako primetite da portal ne prima podatke s vaše stanice duže od 24 sata, pozovite nas odmah — ranije reagovanje znači manji rizik od trajnog oštećenja senzora. Cilj nam je da do jeseni imamo konstruktivnu izmenu koja ovaj problem eliminiše u budućim serijama.

title: Posetite nas na Sajmu poljoprivrede u Novom Sadu — Hala 3, Štand B-17
text:
Agrosan IoT biće prisutan na ovogodišnjem Međunarodnom sajmu poljoprivrede u Novom Sadu od 20. do 25. maja 2024. Naći ćete nas u Hali 3, na štandu B-17.

Šta možete da vidite

Doneli smo oba modela stanica — AgroSen-1 i AgroSen-2 — u punoj radnoj konfiguraciji s demo solarnim panelom i baterijom. Na licu mesta možete pratiti kako podaci stignu na portal i aplikaciju. Marko će biti dostupan za tehničke razgovore svaki dan od 10 do 13 sati.

Demonstracija portala

Pokazaćemo live prikaz podataka s naših testnih stanica postavljenih u polju. Videćete temperaturne trendove, upozorenja pri niskim baterijama i izvoz podataka u CSV koji mnogi agronomi koriste za daljnju analizu.

Za zadruge i veće kupce

Ako zastupate zadrugu ili gazdinstvo s više od 200 hektara i zanima vas pilot instalacija, zakažite razgovor unapred — na sajmu bude gužve i ne želimo da propustimo ozbiljne razgovore. Mejlom ili telefonom, kontakt podaci su na ovoj stranici.

Novost na sajmu

Po prvi put pokazujemo prototip senzora lisne vlažnosti koji planiramo da uvedemo u AgroSen-2 do kraja godine. Radi se o kapacitivnom senzoru koji bi trebalo da pomogne u praćenju rizika od plamenjače. Prototip još nije spreman za prodaju, ali voleli bismo da čujemo reakcije farmera pre nego što finalizujemo dizajn.

title: Our Services — Kadrovski Servis Vojvodina
text:

Client portal. Existing clients access their payroll summaries, contract archive and monthly reports through our online portal. You can download documents, check contribution histories and send us questions directly.

title: What the March 2024 Labour Law changes mean for your employment contracts
text:
The amendments to the Serbian Labour Law that came into force at the beginning of March 2024 include changes to fourteen provisions that appear in standard employment contracts. If you are a client of ours, you do not need to worry — we are updating all affected templates and will contact you individually about any contracts that may need to be re-issued or supplemented. If you manage your own contracts without us, here is a plain-language summary of the areas to check.

Probation periods. The rules around how probation periods can be set and ended have been clarified. The maximum length for most positions remains unchanged, but the grounds on which an employer can end employment during probation have been restated in more specific language. If your contracts use the old wording, the substance may still be correct but it is worth having them reviewed.

Notice periods. The minimum notice requirements have been adjusted for employees with longer service. If you have staff who have been with you for more than ten years, check that your contracts reflect the updated figures.

Fixed-term contracts. There are new provisions relating to the maximum total duration of successive fixed-term contracts with the same employee. The previous rules already limited this, but the amendments tighten them and add a reporting obligation in certain circumstances.

Remote and hybrid work. The section covering remote work arrangements has been expanded. If you have employees working from home either regularly or occasionally and your contracts do not include a specific remote work clause, you should add one.

We will be publishing a fuller checklist for our clients in the next few weeks. In the meantime, if you have a specific question about how these changes affect your situation, you can reach us at saveti@kadrovski-vojvodina.rs.

title: What We Do — MojaKutija Commerce
text:
MojaKutija Commerce operates a fulfillment centre in the NTP Novi Sad business park. We store goods, pick and pack orders, prepare customs documents and book carriers so that small Serbian brands can sell into Germany, Austria, Slovenia, Hungary and beyond without building their own logistics operation.

Our warehouse covers 2,400 square metres of racked storage. We can hold goods under standard ambient conditions or in our dedicated dry-food section, which is temperature-monitored and logged daily. We process incoming stock within one business day of receipt, photograph each SKU for catalogue purposes if the client needs it, and assign barcode locations so every unit is traceable.

When an order arrives — through MojaVitrina, WooCommerce or a direct API connection — our WMS creates a pick list, routes it to the nearest bin location and generates all required paperwork: packing slip, shipping label and, where required, a CN22 or commercial customs invoice in the language of the destination country.

Parcels leave the building once a day at 14:30 via DPD, GLS or DHL, depending on the destination and the client's preference. We hand carriers a pre-sorted manifest and photograph the trolley before it leaves. Tracking numbers are pushed back to the client's storefront automatically.

For clients whose products are fragile or irregularly shaped we design custom cardboard inserts and foam pads in-house. We source packaging materials from suppliers in Serbia to keep lead times short.

MojaVitrina, our white-label webshop platform, gives clients a branded online store without development costs. The design is simple and tested on mobile. Clients manage products and prices through a dashboard; everything else — stock levels, order routing, dispatch — happens on our side without any action needed from them.

We currently serve 28 active client brands. If you make something and want to reach EU buyers, contact us at prodaja@mojakutija.rs.

title: What Happened When German Customs Returned 23 Parcels in One Week
text:
In the last week of March we had 23 parcels returned from the DHL processing hub in Leipzig. Every one of them had a blank or missing customs invoice. That is not 23 annoyed customers — it is 23 replacement shipments, 23 refund conversations and a cost we have calculated at roughly €320 in direct charges plus the softer cost of our clients wondering whether we know what we are doing.

We traced all 23 failures back to a single root cause: our Brother laser printer had a paper sensor fault that caused it to report a successful print job while feeding through blank sheets. Our WMS received a confirmation from the print driver, marked the job done and allowed the parcel to move to the sealing station. The operator saw a green tick on the screen and sealed the box. Nobody looked at the paper.

We fixed the immediate problem by replacing the faulty printer within 24 hours. But the episode showed us something bigger: our print confirmation logic asks the driver whether the job was accepted, not whether ink actually reached paper. Those are different questions and we were only asking the first one.

Since then we have added a mandatory visual sign-off field in the WMS for each customs document, which the operator must tick before the parcel barcode can be scanned to the dispatch trolley. It is a manual control and it slows the line by a few seconds per parcel, but it has caught two further silent failures in the six weeks since.

This is not the permanent fix. A manual tick can be clicked without looking, and on a day when we are pushing 1,800 parcels out the door that is exactly what happens. We know the real solution is a print workflow that confirms actual output at the device level. We are working on it, and if you have experience in industrial print middleware or ZPL-level printer status reporting, we would genuinely like to hear from you. Write to tehnologija@mojakutija.rs.

title: Novi Sad City Tourist Organisation Extends TrailPortal Licence for Three Years
text:
PeloTrack Solutions a.d. has signed a three-year licence renewal with the Novi Sad City Tourist Organisation (NSGTO) covering continued use of the TrailPortal platform for the management and public display of the official municipal cycling route network.

The renewed agreement covers 14 active trail routes totalling approximately 380 km, including segments of the Fruška Gora cycling circuit and the riverside paths along the Danube south of the city. Under the new contract NSGTO will also enable the white-label embed module, allowing trail maps to appear directly within the organisation's official tourism website with the organisation's own visual identity.

'We have been using TrailPortal since 2019 and the data quality for our region is something we have not found anywhere else,' said Dragana Petrović-Ilić, director of digital services at NSGTO. 'Extending for three years gives us a stable foundation for the cycling content we are expanding in 2025 and 2026.'

Renáta Fodor-Varga, head of municipal partnerships at PeloTrack, said the renewal was the longest-term municipal contract the company has signed to date. 'Novi Sad is one of our most active municipal clients in terms of data updates and user volume. Locking in a three-year term gives both sides room to plan.'

The white-label embed rollout for the NSGTO website is scheduled for the second quarter of 2024. PeloTrack's technical team will handle the integration. NSGTO processes approximately 18,000 unique visitor sessions per month on its cycling section during peak season.

PeloTrack currently holds municipal licences with 28 local governments across Vojvodina, Hungary and Croatia.

title: About PeloTrack Solutions — Hardware, Software and Trail Data for Cycle Tourism
text:
PeloTrack Solutions a.d. has been building tools for cycle tourism since 1998. We started in Subotica as a small workshop and grew into the company we are today by staying close to the routes, the terrain and the people who use them for a living.

Our core products are the CycloNav X4 cycling computer and the TrailPortal subscription platform. The CycloNav X4 is assembled at our Subotica facility. Every unit is calibrated and tested before it ships. TrailPortal is used by tour operators to build itineraries, manage bookings and track fleet positions, and by municipalities to publish and maintain their official trail networks.

We cover the geography that other providers treat as an afterthought. Our map layers include verified surface data, seasonal condition flags, barrier information and points of interest collected over fifteen years of fieldwork in Vojvodina, eastern Hungary and the Croatian Danube-Drava corridor. When a tour operator in Sombor or a municipality in Vukovar uses our platform, they are working with data we have gathered and maintained ourselves, not a third-party feed.

Our team of 112 includes hardware assembly technicians, software developers, a GIS data team and a customer support group that speaks Serbian, Hungarian and Croatian. Sales and account management are handled by Renáta Fodor-Varga, who joined us in 2017 and now leads the municipal partnerships programme. Technical operations are overseen by Borivoj Stanković, our CTO, who joined from a telecoms equipment firm in 2013.

We sell hardware directly and through regional distributors. TrailPortal is sold as an annual licence, with pricing based on the number of active routes and user accounts. White-label embedding for municipal tourism websites is available as an add-on.

If you are a tour operator, a municipality or a regional development agency working on cycling infrastructure, contact our sales team at sales@pelotrack.rs.

title: Job Opening: Mid-Level Backend Developer — Route Engine and API Team
text:
PeloTrack Solutions a.d. is looking for a mid-level backend developer to join the four-person software team at our Subotica office. This is a full-time, on-site role.

You will work primarily on the route recommendation engine and the Django REST API that serves both TrailPortal and the CycloNav X4 firmware update system. The route engine is written in Python and uses PostGIS for spatial queries. Most of your time will be spent on improving how the engine calculates physical effort scores for trail segments — this is an area where we know our current model has gaps and we are actively working to close them.

What we expect you to know: Python at a solid working level, Django and Django REST Framework, PostgreSQL including basic spatial queries with PostGIS, Git. You do not need to be a GIS specialist, but you need to be comfortable reading and writing geometry data.

Useful but not required: experience with graph-based routing algorithms, familiarity with GPX or GeoJSON formats, any background in sports science or biomechanics data (we are not joking — it is genuinely relevant to the effort-estimation problem).

The team works in two-week sprints. We use GitLab for version control and issue tracking. Deployment is on our own servers; we do not use cloud infrastructure for the core platform. The codebase is about seven years old in places and is not always tidy. We are honest about that.

Salary range: 130,000–165,000 RSD net per month depending on experience. We offer 25 days annual leave, flexible start times between 07:00 and 09:30, and a CycloNav X4 device on loan.

Send a CV and a short note about why this role interests you to posao@pelotrack.rs. We review applications on a rolling basis. The position is open until filled.

title: What We Learned at VeloTur Expo Budapest 2024
text:
Earlier this month three of us from PeloTrack attended VeloTur Expo in Budapest, a trade fair for cycle tourism operators, regional development bodies and equipment suppliers from across Central and Eastern Europe. It was our fourth time exhibiting there and probably the busiest stand we have had.

A few things stood out.

First, municipal interest in white-label trail portals has grown noticeably compared to two years ago. Several municipalities from the Hungarian Tisza region stopped by specifically asking about embedding interactive trail maps into their own sites. The common request was mobile performance — they wanted to know how fast the maps loaded on phones. That question came up more than any other, which confirmed something we already know we need to fix.

Second, the conversations with tour operators were heavily focused on effort prediction. Two separate operators from the Croatian Zagorje hills — hilly terrain, not flat like most of our core market — said they had looked at our platform and decided against it because they did not trust the difficulty ratings for ascent-heavy routes. That was direct feedback and we appreciated them saying it plainly. We are working on this.

Third, we met a distributor from Brno, Cykloobchod Morava s.r.o., who expressed serious interest in carrying the CycloNav X4 for the Czech market. We have had informal talks before but this was the first time their purchasing manager was in the room. Nothing is signed, but we will be following up.

Overall the fair reinforced what our own data already tells us: the product works, the data layer is genuinely valued, and the two technical areas we most need to improve are well-known to the market. We came back with a longer prospect list and a clearer sense of what is blocking growth.

title: Job Opening: Electronics Technician — Assembly and Calibration Line
text:
We are hiring an electronics technician to join our hardware assembly team in Subotica. This is a full-time role based entirely on-site.

The assembly team produces the CycloNav X4 GPS cycling computer. Your day-to-day work will include component placement inspection, operation of the RF calibration bench, firmware flashing and end-of-line functional testing. You will be working alongside two other calibration technicians and reporting to the production supervisor, Miroslav Đurić.

The calibration bench work is the most technically demanding part of the role. We use a proprietary reference oscillator setup to verify and trim each antenna board. Full training is provided; if you have experience with RF test equipment or trimmer capacitor adjustment that is useful, but we have trained people from scratch before.

We are also interested in technicians who have any background in test automation or bench instrumentation scripting, because we are planning changes to the calibration process over the next 12 to 18 months and we want people who can contribute to that work, not just operate the current setup.

What we need: a completed vocational qualification in electronics or electrical engineering, the ability to work accurately under production-floor conditions, basic computer literacy for logging test results. Experience with SMD handling is a plus.

title: NebulaFly Agro završio sezonu 2023. sa 9.400 hektara i novim klijentima u Mađarskoj
text:
Sezona 2023. bila je do sada najobimnija u istoriji kompanije. Prekrili smo 9.400 hektara u Vojvodini i pograničnoj Mađarskoj, od čega je 6.200 hektara prskano, 2.600 hektara snimljeno multispektralnom kamerom, a ostatak obuhvata setvu i kombinovane pakete.

Novi klijenti ove sezone bili su Napfény Kft. iz Segedina i gazdinstvo porodice Kertész iz okoline Baje — oba sa farmama pšenice i suncokreta između 400 i 800 hektara. Saradnja je počela pilot-letom u aprilu i nastavljena je tokom cele vegetativne sezone.

Usluge snimanja bile su posebno tražene: šest klijenata je po prvi put koristilo NDVI karte za donošenje odluka o tretmanu, a dvoje je na osnovu tih karata smanjilo ukupnu količinu primenjenog fungicida.

Najveći operativni izazov bila je koncentracija zahteva u maju. Na vrhuncu sezone imali smo aktivnih naloga za više od 800 hektara dnevno, što je premašilo naš kapacitet planiranja ruta. Deo narudžbina je morao biti pomeren za kasniji termin, što je za tretmane fungicidom suboptimalno.

Za narednu sezonu planiramo povećanje broja letelica i uvođenje delimične automatizacije planiranja ruta. Zahvaljujemo svim klijentima i partnerima koji su nam ukazali poverenje.

title: NebulaFly Agro na sajmu AgroNova Expo 2024. u Novom Sadu
text:
NebulaFly Agro a.d. učestvovao je na sajmu AgroNova Expo 2024. koji je održan u Novom Sadu od 19. do 21. februara. Bili smo izloženi u hali za preciznu poljoprivredu zajedno sa dvadesetak kompanija iz regiona.

Na štandu smo predstavili naš paket usluga za sezonu 2024., demonstrirali klijentski portal za pregled NDVI karata i prikazali snimke iz protekle sezone. Posebno interesovanje izazvao je prikaz uspoređenih karata iz dva navrata snimanja na istoj parceli suncokreta — pre i posle tretmana — koji je pokazao razliku u vegetativnom indeksu.

Imali smo razgovore sa nekoliko novih potencijalnih klijenata iz okoline Zrenjanina i sa jednim distributerom agrohemikalija koji je zainteresovan za zajednički paket usluga. Konkretnih dogovora još nema, ali razgovori se nastavljaju.

Direktor Branko Vukelić bio je panelista na okruglom stolu o primeni bespilotnih letelica u zaštiti bilja, gde je govorio o ekonomičnosti preciznog prskanja u poređenju sa traktorskim prskalicama na parcelama nepravilnog oblika.

Sledećeg izlaganja planiramo na sajmu u Budimpešti u septembru, u okviru napora za ulazak na mađarsko tržište.

title: O nama i uslugama — NebulaFly Agro a.d.
text:
NebulaFly Agro pruža usluge iz vazduha za velika ratarska gazdinstva u Vojvodini i pograničnim područjima Mađarske. Ne prodajemo droneove — prodajemo rezultat: tretiran usev, isporučena NDVI karta, zasejana parcela.

Naša flota obuhvata fiksnorilne letelice dugog doleta za snimanje i višerotorne platforme namenjene preciznom prskanju i setvi. Sve letelice su opremljene RTK GPS sistemom i lete prema automatski generisanim rutama koje prilagođavamo svakoj parceli.

Usluge koje nudimo:
• Prskanje pesticidima, fungicidima i folijarnim đubrivima po normi
• Multispektralno snimanje i izrada NDVI/NDRE karata
• Setva pokrovnih useva i sitnosemenih kultura
• Sezonski paket monitoringa za pšenicu i suncokret
• Izveštaji o stanju useva dostupni kroz naš klijentski portal

Radimo sa gazdinstvima od 200 do više od 3.000 hektara. Naši stalni klijenti uključuju preduzeća kao što su Zlatna ravnica d.o.o. iz okoline Kikinde i Agro Palić grupa, kao i nekoliko porodičnih gazdinstava u Bačkoj. Svaki klijent dobija georeferencirane karte posle svakog leta.

Timom rukovodi Branko Vukelić, koji je pre osnivanja kompanije radio deset godina kao agrotehničar na semenskim farmama. Tehnički direktor Maja Horváth dolazi iz oblasti ugrađenih sistema. Naši piloti su licencirani prema nacionalnoj regulativi i prolaze sertifikaciju svake sezone.

Zaposleni smo u Subotici, a bazu opreme imamo i u Somboru radi brže reakcije za klijente na zapadu Vojvodine.
