title: What We Do — OrtoPrint Solutions
text:
OrtoPrint Solutions makes custom orthopaedic orthoses and prosthetic components for patients across the Western Balkans. Every device we produce starts with a 3D scan of the patient and ends with a fitting carried out by one of our certified orthotists. Nothing leaves our facility without that clinical step.

Our production process begins in our Zrenjanin workshop, where a structured-light scanner captures the patient's limb geometry in under two minutes. The scan is cleaned and modelled by our design team using OrthoFlow Studio, then sent to one of our four FDM print units. Most devices are printed in PA12 nylon, chosen for its combination of stiffness, chemical resistance and the ability to be post-processed without losing dimensional accuracy. For softer interfaces and paediatric work we use TPU. Print time for a standard ankle-foot orthosis is six to nine hours; a transtibial socket takes ten to fourteen.

Every load-bearing component is fatigue-tested on our in-house servo rig before dispatch. Our quality system is certified to ISO 13485, and we maintain full traceability from scan file to finished device.

We supply orthopaedic and rehabilitation departments at more than forty hospitals and thirty private clinics. Repeat orders account for around 70% of our annual volume, which we take as a reasonable measure of whether the products are working. Patients who need adjustments are seen at our Zrenjanin workshop or our Novi Sad fitting room; we do not post devices and ask patients to figure it out themselves.

For institutions that want to trial our service, we offer a ten-device pilot programme — you send us referrals, we scan, produce and fit, and you receive a full quality and outcomes report at the end. Contact our sales coordinator Milica Jovičić at the address below.

The agreement covers custom ankle-foot orthoses, knee orthoses and upper-limb splints for adult and paediatric patients referred through the network.

Under the terms of the agreement, OrtoPrint Solutions will conduct monthly scanning visits to Ortomed Centar's main clinic using its portable Artec Leo scanner, with finished devices delivered within ten working days of each visit. A fitting appointment is included as standard for every device.

The contract follows a six-month trial that began in September 2023, during which OrtoPrint Solutions produced forty-three devices for Ortomed Centar patients. According to Ortomed Centar's clinical lead Jovana Šarić, the trial demonstrated acceptable fit quality and turnaround times comparable to the Sarajevo suppliers the network had previously used, at a lower per-unit cost.

"The scanning process is faster than plaster casting and the patients find it much more comfortable," said Šarić. "We had three devices returned for adjustment over the forty-three produced, which is within the range we see from any supplier."

For OrtoPrint Solutions, the Banja Luka agreement is the company's first multi-site contract in Bosnia-Herzegovina and its largest single framework deal outside Serbia. Production director Aleksandar Vukić said the company would add a second monthly scanning visit to the schedule by the end of the second quarter to accommodate expected referral volumes.

Ortomed Centar joins a customer list that currently includes thirty-two hospitals and clinics across five countries in the Western Balkans.

title: What we learned from two years of logging rework
text:
Since mid-2022 we have been keeping a structured log of every device that comes back to us for adjustment or reprint. Before that we tracked reworks loosely in the ERP system, but not in a way that told us anything useful about why they were happening. We want to share what the data has shown us so far, because we think it is relevant to anyone running a digital orthotics production line.

The short version: about one in eight of our devices comes back, the majority are ankle-foot orthoses for adult patients, and the most common stated reason is pressure at a bony prominence — the lateral malleolus accounts for about 40% of those cases, the navicular for another 20%.

When we looked at the geometry of the returned devices against the original scans, a pattern became clear. Our CAD software applies a uniform 3 mm clearance offset across the entire inner surface as a default safety margin. On a flat stretch of the posterior shaft of a tibia, 3 mm of clearance is more than enough and the device can feel loose. On a malleolus with a radius of curvature of 15–20 mm, the same 3 mm offset is not sufficient to prevent contact under load — the shell flexes slightly during walking and closes that gap. We had suspected something like this for a while, but the log data made it concrete.

The rework cost per device averages €180 when you include the material, print time and orthotist labour for the refitting appointment. Over 2023, that came to a figure our finance manager would prefer we not publish, but it is large enough to justify a serious effort to fix the underlying cause.

We are currently looking for a technical partner who can help us build a smarter offset model — one that uses the local surface geometry from the scan to vary the clearance rather than applying the same value everywhere. If you work in computational geometry or medical device design and this sounds like a problem you have seen before, we would be glad to hear from you. Write to razvoj@ortoprintsolutions.rs.

title: O nama i usluge — Kovač-Metal d.o.o.
text:
Kovač-Metal d.o.o. je porodično preduzeće za obradu metala sa sedištem u Zrenjaninu, aktivno od 1987. godine. Naša osnovna delatnost je obrada čeličnih limova — rezanje, savijanje i zavarivanje — kao i izrada i montaža lakih čeličnih konstrukcija za građevinarstvo i industriju.

Raspolažemo sa dva ključna mašinska resursa: fiber laserskim rezačem formata 3000×1500 mm i CNC press-kočnicom nosivosti 250 tona. To nam omogućava da radimo serije od jednog komada do nekoliko stotina, sa tolerancijama koje zadovoljavaju zahteve mašinogradnje.

Pored toga, upravljamo sopstvenom toplom pocinkovnom linijom koja čeličnim elementima pruža dugotrajnu korozivnu zaštitu. Kapacitet linije iznosi do 1.200 kg po šarži.

Naš tim broji 47 zaposlenih, od kojih su 28 direktno angažovani u proizvodnji. Prosečan radni staž u firmi je 11 godina — stabilnost koja se odražava na kvalitet i pouzdanost isporuke.

Kupce prihvatamo iz celog regiona Vojvodine. Dugogodišnji poslovni partneri uključuju preduzeća kao što su Agrotehna Kikinda (sklopovi za berače kukuruza), Gradmont Zrenjanin (čelične konstrukcije za stambenu gradnju) i Steelform Ruma (okviri za industrijske nadstrešnice). Svaki novi narudžbeni list obrađuje naša tehnička priprema u roku od 48 sati.

title: Isporučili smo 340 okvira za prikolice Agrovetoru iz Sombora
text:
U februaru i martu 2024. godine završili smo jednu od naših najvećih pojedinačnih narudžbina u poslednjih nekoliko godina — izradu 340 čeličnih okvira za jednoosovinske prikolice za preduzeće Agrovet d.o.o. iz Sombora.

Narudžbina je podrazumevala rezanje i savijanje limova debljine 3 i 4 mm, MAG zavarivanje nosivih sklopova i finalnu obradu u našoj toplo-pocinkovnoj liniji. Svaki okvir je pre isporuke prošao vizuelni pregled i dimenzionalnu kontrolu.

Najveći tehnički izazov na ovom poslu bio je održavanje konzistentnih uglova savijanja tokom duge serije — kod 3 mm galvanizovanog lima, preskočni ugao varira u zavisnosti od temperatura hale i stepena istrošenosti alata. Naši operateri su za ovu seriju vodili dnevnik merenja i ručno korigovali parametre na press-kočnici po potrebi, što je oduzelo dosta vremena, ali je na kraju dalo rezultat.

Završena isporuka potvrđuje da je naš kapacitet press-kočnice i laserskog rezača dovoljan za serije ovakvog obima, ali smo svesni da bismo sa automatizacijom kontrole ugla mogli isti posao završiti za kraće vreme i sa manjim brojem doradnih prolaza.

Agrovet je ostao zadovoljan kvalitetom i dinamikom isporuke. Razgovaramo o nastavku saradnje za jesenju sezonu.

title: Posetili smo sajam MetalTech Beograd 2024 — utisci sa izložbe

Iz Kovač-Metala su otišli Dragan Kovač i naš tehnolog Milica Vujanović. Cilj posete bio je konkretna provera dve stvari: dostupnost sistema za automatsku kompenzaciju preskočnog ugla na press-kočnicama i rešenja za merenje potrošnje energije po zavarivačkim stanicama.

Na štandu jednog nemačkog distributera videli smo demonstraciju sistema za merenje ugla koji radi u realnom vremenu i šalje signal nazad na kontroler kočnice. Sistem izgleda obećavajuće, ali cena licenciranog rešenja za našu mašinu iznosi nešto više od 18.000 evra — to je za sada izvan našeg tekućeg budžeta, ali dobar pokazatelj tržišnih cena.

Što se tiče energetskog monitoringa, razgovarali smo sa domaćim distributerom iz Novog Sada koji nudi podmernu opremu sa daljinskim očitavanjem. Razmatramo pilot instalaciju na dve stanice.

Ukupno, sajam je potvrdio da rešenja koja tražimo postoje, ali su uglavnom dizajnirana za veće kapacitete i cenovne razrede od naših. Tražimo pristup koji bi imao smisla za firmu naše veličine.

title: What We Build — NovaByte Simulations
text:
NovaByte Simulations builds training simulators for industries where a mistake during learning is expensive or dangerous. We work with logistics operators, construction companies, and vocational training centres across the former Yugoslav states. Our clients use our simulators daily — sometimes for initial licensing preparation, sometimes for refresher training, sometimes to assess whether an operator is ready to move up to a more demanding machine class.

Our core products are StackSim Pro, a forklift and reach-truck training environment; LiftSim, which covers tower and mobile crane operation; and DigSim, for excavator and earthworks equipment. All three run on standard Windows workstations and laptops, connect to physical control hardware where clients prefer it, and log every trainee action for review.

ScenarioForge is the authoring tool we built for our own content team that we now license to training centres with large enough programme volumes to justify building custom scenarios. It does not require programming knowledge, and most instructors learn the basics in a day.

TraceBoard is our reporting layer. It aggregates session logs from all simulators into one place so that a training manager can see, at a glance, which operators have met hour requirements, where error rates are clustered by task type, and how individual trainees compare to cohort averages.

We have been at NTP Novi Sad since 2013. Most of our work is done in the building; we prefer to keep development, art, and client support in the same space. Our clients tend to stay with us: the average customer relationship is now over five years, and several of our earliest industrial clients are still running on products that have evolved continuously from the first version we delivered to them.

title: Senior Unity Engineer — Physics and Simulation Systems
text:
NovaByte Simulations is looking for a senior Unity engineer to take ownership of the physics and simulation layer across our industrial training products.

What the role involves:
You will work on the systems that make our simulators feel accurate to operators who know real machines — load dynamics on forks and rigging points, terrain interaction for earthworks equipment, and the physical feedback that comes through control hardware. You will also be the main contact for integration of new hardware peripherals such as force-feedback devices and motion platforms.

The codebase is C#, Unity 2022 LTS, with custom extensions built on top of PhysX. We use Azure DevOps for version control and task tracking. Asset production is handled by a separate team; your job is the logic and physics, not the art.

What we are looking for:
— At least four years working in Unity on projects that shipped to real users
— Solid understanding of rigid-body dynamics, constraints, and joint systems
— Experience profiling and optimising physics-heavy scenes for lower-end hardware
— Comfortable reading academic or technical papers on physical modelling and translating them into code
— Familiarity with hardware-in-the-loop setups is useful but not required

What would make you stand out:
— Any background in robotics, mechanical engineering, or industrial simulation
— Experience writing compute shaders or GPU-side physics extensions
— Previous work on simulators for professional or safety-critical contexts

The team is 67 people, with about 20 in engineering. We work in Novi Sad, on-site five days a week. Salary is competitive for the regional market and negotiable based on experience. If you have questions before applying, write to jobs@novabytesim.rs (fictional address) and someone will get back to you within two working days.

title: Data Analyst — Trainee Performance and Behavioural Data
text:
We are looking for a data analyst to join the TraceBoard product team. This is a new role created because the data we are collecting from simulators — including gaze data from eye-tracking hardware — has outgrown what our current team can process and interpret.

The work:
You will build and maintain pipelines that turn raw session logs and gaze recordings into the metrics displayed in TraceBoard. You will also take on the eye-tracking analysis work that is currently sitting in a backlog: we have approximately 340 archived sessions with matched outcome data and we need a method for scoring gaze patterns against error risk.

Day to day, this means Python, some SQL, and close collaboration with the engineers who maintain the simulator logging systems. You will not be writing game code, but you need to understand what each logged event means operationally.

What we are looking for:
— Three or more years working with time-series or event-log data in a professional context
— Python data stack: pandas, numpy, at least one visualisation library
— Ability to read a dataset critically and communicate what it does and does not support
— Comfort with ambiguity: some of our data is messy and the questions are not always well-formed when they arrive

Useful but not essential:
— Any prior work with eye-tracking data, scanpath analysis, or fixation detection
— Experience in a domain where the data is tied to safety or performance outcomes
— Familiarity with statistical testing — we do not need a statistician, but someone who knows when a result is not reliable

This is a full-time position in Novi Sad. The TraceBoard team is small — currently three people — and this hire will significantly expand its capacity. We expect the eye-tracking backlog to be the first substantial project.

title: LiftSim Adopted by Three New Training Centres in Bosnia and Herzegovina
text:
NovaByte Simulations has completed delivery of LiftSim installations at three vocational training centres in Bosnia and Herzegovina, following a procurement process that ran through the second half of 2023.

The three centres — Centar za stručno obrazovanje Tuzla, Tehnički školski centar Zenica, and Zanatski centar Mostar (all fictional) — will use LiftSim as part of initial operator preparation for tower crane licencing. Each installation includes four simulator stations running on local workstations, physical crane-control hardware with replica pendant and cab controls, and a TraceBoard licence for their training coordinators.

The procurement was coordinated through a regional vocational education initiative, and the specification required that the simulator software be available in Bosnian as well as Serbian and Croatian. NovaByte added full Bosnian-language localisation to LiftSim during the project, which is now included in the standard product.

Miloš Crnobrnja, head of product at NovaByte, said the project involved closer collaboration with the training centres than a typical software delivery. "The instructors at these centres have decades of experience with real cranes. They pointed out several places where our scenario design was not reflecting how operators actually learn the job. We revised four scenarios before final acceptance, and the product is better for it."

All three centres are expected to have trainees using the system by the end of the second quarter. NovaByte's support team will conduct on-site reviews at each location in October.

The expansion into Bosnia and Herzegovina follows existing LiftSim deployments in Serbia, Slovenia, and Croatia, and brings the total number of active LiftSim installations to 31 across the region.

title: Why We Started Logging Gaze Data — and What We Have Not Figured Out Yet
text:
About eighteen months ago we added eye-tracking hardware to several of our StackSim Pro and LiftSim simulator stations. The idea came from a conversation with an instructor at one of our long-term clients — a logistics company running a large warehouse in Vojvodina. She made the observation that experienced operators do not look at the same things novices do, and that you can sometimes predict a mistake by watching where someone is not looking, rather than where they are.

That seemed like something a simulator should be able to capture. Consumer eye-tracking hardware has become inexpensive enough that adding it to a simulator station is not a major cost, and the SDK integration took one of our engineers about two weeks.

The hardware has been running reliably. Over 340 sessions have been recorded with matched outcome data — meaning we know, for each session, whether an error event occurred and at what point. That is a reasonable dataset.

What we have not done yet is turn it into anything useful at the point of training. Currently the gaze data sits in CSV files. An instructor can watch a gaze-overlay replay if they have the time, which most do not. There is no score, no flag, nothing that surfaces automatically in TraceBoard.

We have tried a few simple approaches — fixation duration on defined areas of interest, time-to-first-fixation on safety-relevant zones before a manoeuvre. The numbers come out, but we have not been able to establish a threshold that distinguishes reliably between sessions that ended in errors and sessions that did not. It is possible we are asking the wrong question. It is also possible the method is sound but we are not applying the right analysis.

We are writing this partly to think through the problem in public, and partly because we are actively looking for someone — either a hire or an external collaborator — who has worked with this kind of data before. If that is you, get in touch.

title: We Exhibited at SPS Nürnberg 2023 — Notes from the Floor
text:
Three of us from Voltiko spent four days at SPS Nürnberg in November. It is the main industrial automation trade fair in the German-speaking market and one of the few places where we reliably meet current and potential customers in person rather than by video call.

We shared a small stand with two other Serbian technology companies from the NTP Novi Sad cluster as part of a joint representation organised through the park. The arrangement worked — it kept costs manageable and the shared space drew more foot traffic than a single small stand would have.

What we heard from integrators at the fair: demand for sub-GHz wireless nodes in industrial environments is still growing, mostly replacing wired sensor runs in retrofit projects where running new cable is expensive. Battery life and documentation quality came up repeatedly as the factors that differentiate suppliers. Several integrators mentioned that their enterprise clients are tightening supplier security requirements, which matches what we are hearing directly from two of our own German accounts.

We had productive conversations with four integrators we had not spoken to before. Two of those have since requested engineering samples.

One thing we noted: the number of Asian module vendors at the fair has increased significantly in the past two years. Most are competing on unit price. We are not going to win on unit price against a Shenzhen module manufacturer. We are going to win on reliability data, documentation, and the ability to respond quickly when an integrator has a problem in the field. That is not a new conclusion but it was reinforced.

We plan to return to SPS in 2024. If you are attending and want to schedule a meeting, contact us in advance at sales@voltiko.rs.

title: What We Build and Why
text:
Voltiko makes wireless sensor nodes and gateways for industrial IoT. That is a crowded sentence, so let us say what we actually mean by it.

A sensor node in our product line is a small sealed PCB — roughly 55 mm × 35 mm in the standard form factor — with a sensor, a sub-GHz radio, and a coin-cell battery. It wakes up on a schedule, takes a reading, transmits it, and goes back to sleep. The target battery life is five years under a defined duty cycle. We manufacture these in Novi Sad and ship them primarily to system integrators in Germany, Austria, and the Czech Republic.

A gateway in our line is a DIN-rail-mounted device that collects data from up to 200 nodes in a mesh network and pushes it over TLS to a cloud endpoint chosen by the integrator. The VG-10 runs on 24 V DC, has a local Ethernet port, and is designed to run unattended in an industrial cabinet for years.

We do not license reference designs and we do not sell chipsets. Everything — the PCB layout, the antenna matching, the firmware, the mechanical enclosure specification — comes from our team in Novi Sad. We have 34 people. We do our own SMT assembly on-site.

Why does that matter to an integrator? Because when a unit in the field behaves unexpectedly, we can look at the production record for that specific board and at the firmware version running on it. We are not pointing at a module supplier. The accountability is ours.

If you are an integrator evaluating sensor hardware for a new deployment, we are willing to provide engineering samples, field trial support, and a data sheet that reflects measured performance rather than typical-condition marketing numbers. Contact our technical sales team to start a conversation.

title: Firmware Engineer – Wireless Protocols and Power Management
text:
Voltiko is looking for a firmware engineer to join our team in Novi Sad. We have two firmware engineers today; this would be the third.

The work is embedded C on ARM Cortex-M0+ and M4 targets, a tickless RTOS environment, and a lot of attention to power consumption. Our nodes run from coin cells for years, so every peripheral enable, every polling interval, and every radio wake-up has a cost that has to be justified.

On the radio side, we currently ship products using a proprietary sub-GHz mesh stack and are evaluating LoRa as an optional physical layer for some customers. You do not need to have built a radio stack from scratch, but you should be comfortable reading a radio module datasheet, understanding duty cycle restrictions under CE RED, and writing MAC-layer logic that handles retries, collision avoidance, and low-power sleep scheduling.

The gateway side runs on a more capable processor and handles TLS 1.2 over MQTT, certificate management, and OTA firmware update signing. Experience with embedded TLS libraries — mbedTLS specifically — is useful.

We use Git, review every pull request before merge, and keep a hardware-in-the-loop test bench for regression testing. We do not have a formal CI pipeline yet; building one is on the list and you would be involved in that.

We are not looking for someone who wants to move into management quickly. This is a hands-on engineering role. The team is small, decisions are made close to the work, and the products go into real industrial environments where reliability matters.

Salary is negotiable based on experience. The position is on-site in Novi Sad. Send a CV and a short note about a firmware problem you found interesting to jobs@voltiko.rs.

title: Voltiko Completes Delivery of 4,200 Sensor Nodes for Cold-Chain Project in Bavaria
text:
Voltiko has completed delivery and commissioning support for a 4,200-unit deployment of VN-4x sensor nodes integrated by Reismann Industrielösungen, a Munich-based system integrator specialising in food logistics infrastructure.

The deployment monitors temperature and humidity across 14 cold-storage facilities in Bavaria operated by a regional food distribution company. Reismann selected our VN-4x-T (temperature variant) and VN-4x-TH (combined temperature and humidity) nodes, paired with four VG-10 gateways per site, each pushing data to Reismann's own cloud platform over TLS.

The project ran from initial sample evaluation in April 2023 to final site commissioning in February 2024. A batch of 600 units was delivered as a pilot in June 2023, ran through the summer without reported issues, and Reismann placed the main production order in September.

Martin Holec, our technical sales lead, said the project was straightforward partly because Reismann had clear documentation requirements from the start. They provided a full interface specification for the MQTT topic structure and certificate management procedure before we wrote a line of gateway firmware for their integration, which is not always the case.

For us the project is a reference point for cold-chain deployments at this scale. We now have field data from 4,200 nodes in low-temperature environments running our Q4 2023 firmware build, which will inform how we tune the power management defaults for the next hardware revision.

If you are an integrator evaluating sensor hardware for a similar application, contact us at sales@voltiko.rs.

title: Production Test Technician – Electronics Assembly
text:
We are hiring a production test technician for our electronics assembly floor in Novi Sad.

Voltiko manufactures wireless sensor nodes and gateway boards in-house. Final functional testing is done on a custom jig that checks power rails, communication buses, and radio carrier detect for each board before it is packaged. The technician in this role operates that jig, records pass/fail results in our production tracking system, flags anomalous readings, and escalates boards that show anything outside tolerance.

Currently one experienced technician runs roughly 180 boards per shift on the jig. We want a second person so that we can split shifts and increase throughput, and also so we are not dependent on a single person's knowledge of how the jig behaves.

What we are looking for: someone with a technical secondary school background in electronics or electrotechnics, basic familiarity with reading a multimeter and understanding what voltage and current measurements mean in the context of a functioning circuit, and a methodical approach to repetitive work. You do not need to be a design engineer. You do need to notice when something looks wrong and say so.

We will train you on the jig and on our production tracking software. Over time, we expect this person to be involved in jig maintenance and potentially in the development of improved test procedures — we are actively working on upgrading our test coverage and want someone on the production floor who can give practical input on what is and is not feasible.

The position is full-time, on-site. Working hours are fixed shift. We provide a standard Serbian employment contract with health and pension contributions. Send a CV to jobs@voltiko.rs.

title: Why We Moved Final Assembly In-House in 2018 and What We Learned
text:
When Voltiko was smaller, we subcontracted PCB assembly to a contract manufacturer in Subotica. It was a reasonable decision at the time — we did not have the capital for an SMT line and our volumes were too low to justify it. The arrangement worked until it did not.

The problem was not quality, exactly. The contract manufacturer was competent. The problem was feedback latency. When a batch came back and we found a pattern of solder defects on a specific footprint, we were looking at a process that had already run 1,200 boards. Changing something meant negotiating a process change with a supplier, waiting for the next run, and hoping the change held. By the time we had data confirming the fix, months had passed.

In 2018 we decided to bring assembly in-house. We purchased a used reflow oven and pick-and-place machine, hired two technicians, and moved everything into our own space at NTP. The first six months were slower and messier than outsourcing had been. We were learning SMT process management while also trying to hit delivery commitments.

Four years later, the decision looks correct. When we see a solder joint pattern we do not like, we can change the stencil aperture and run a test panel the same day. Our process engineers — which at our scale means our most experienced production technician — can walk over to the reflow oven and look at a profile. The feedback loop is hours, not weeks.

We still have gaps. Our functional test coverage is not as thorough as we would like. We catch most faults on the jig but we know we are missing some intermittent failures that only appear under thermal stress. That is the problem we are working on next. Solving it will probably require a combination of better test fixture design and a more systematic analysis of where our current jig leaves coverage gaps. We are looking for people to help with that.

title: We Received a Creative Industries Development Grant
text:
We found out in October that Subotica Interactive has been awarded a development grant from the Fond za Kreativne Industrije Srbije — one of a small number of grants given to game development projects this cycle.

The amount is modest: enough to cover part of Ervin's contract through the first half of 2024 and to pay for professional audio mixing on the first chapter of the game. It does not change the fundamental situation, which is that we are still a micro studio working on a tight budget. But it covers a gap that would have meant slower progress or compromises we did not want to make.

The application process asked us to describe our cultural angle, our market, and our plan for reaching players outside Serbia. We wrote honestly about what we are building and why, and apparently that was enough. We are grateful.

What this means in practical terms: the game stays on track for an Early Access release in 2025. The audio work can start this winter rather than being pushed back. And we have a small amount of room to bring in short-term help for specific problems — the language work and the architectural reference research being the two we feel most acutely right now.

If you have been following development for a while, thank you. The log has been quiet lately because we have been heads down on the second chapter. More updates coming before the end of the year.

title: About Subotica Interactive
text:
Subotica Interactive started because Milovan Fekete could not find the game he wanted to play.

He grew up in Subotica surrounded by a culture that does not appear in mainstream games — the flatlands, the mixed-language households, the folk stories that are neither quite Slavic nor quite Central European but somewhere in between. In 2021 he registered as a sole trader and started building it himself.

The studio now has five people working on its first title, a narrative RPG set in 1920s Vojvodina. The team is fully remote, spread across Subotica and Novi Sad, meeting in person a few times a year.

We do not have a publisher. We fund development through a combination of personal savings, a small grant from a Serbian creative industries fund, and modest revenue from an asset pack sold to other developers. That independence means we move slowly, but it also means no one is telling us to make the folklore more accessible or to replace the Hungarian dialogue with English.

Our players are people who have played a lot of games and want something located somewhere real. They notice when period detail is wrong. We try to make sure it is not.

If you want to follow development, we post irregular updates on our development log. If you are a developer interested in licensing our Pannonian environment assets, the pack is available on our itch.io page. If you are a historian, linguist, or architect with knowledge of interwar Vojvodina, we are genuinely interested in talking to you — our contact form is always open.

title: What We Know and Do Not Know About Vojvodina Manor Houses
text:
One of the first environments the player spends serious time in is a manor house on a working agricultural estate somewhere between Subotica and Sombor. We have been working on it for longer than we planned, and I want to write about why.

The problem is not imagination. Ervin is a capable artist and he knows what the space should feel like. The problem is that we do not actually know what these buildings looked like inside.

We have photographs of the exterior of a handful of manor houses from the period — some from archives, some from a collection shared with us by Panonska Baština in Subotica. They show us rooflines, window proportions, entrance porches. They tell us almost nothing about interior layouts, room heights, stair placement, or the smaller material details that make a space feel inhabited rather than dressed.

Ervin has modelled the main hall three times. Each version looks plausible. None of them is grounded in anything we can verify. Playtesters who grew up in the region have not flagged specific errors — but they have also said things like 'it feels a bit off' without being able to explain why.

We have looked at regional museum catalogues, local history publications, a couple of academic papers on Vojvodina architectural heritage. These are useful for context but not for production. We need measured drawings, floor plans, or someone who has documented these buildings in detail.

If you know of relevant sources — archives, surveys, researchers who work on this material — we would genuinely like to hear from you. This is not a rhetorical question. We are stuck on something that matters to the quality of the work.

title: Part-Time Narrative Consultant — Historical Languages (Serbian / Hungarian)
text:
Subotica Interactive is looking for a part-time consultant to review and improve dialogue scripts for our game in development, *Lodgings on the Near Shore*.

The game is set in Vojvodina between 1922 and 1929. Characters speak Serbian and Hungarian, occasionally mixing both depending on context and social background. We have a working script of approximately 18,000 words in Serbian and 9,000 words in Hungarian. Both are written first in contemporary language and need to be revised toward registers and vocabulary appropriate to the period.

What we need:
- Review of existing dialogue for anachronistic phrasing in both languages
- Suggestions for period-appropriate replacements, with brief notes on why
- A short style reference we can apply ourselves to new scenes going forward
- Availability for occasional short questions during production (a few hours per month)

This is a paid contract role. Budget is limited — we are a five-person micro studio — and we will be transparent about figures in the first conversation. We expect the initial review to take fifteen to twenty hours spread over six to eight weeks.

You do not need to have worked on games before. You do need to have a practical working knowledge of historical Serbian and/or Hungarian language, ideally with some familiarity with the Vojvodina region or early twentieth-century Balkan context.

To apply, send a short message and any relevant background to the address below. We are not asking for a formal CV unless you want to send one.

title: 3D Environment Artist — Freelance Contract (Short-Term)
text:
We are looking for a second environment artist to support Ervin Molnár on background and secondary interior environments for *Lodgings on the Near Shore*.

Our pipeline is Blender to Godot 4. Assets are baked low-poly with hand-painted texture elements in Krita. Style reference will be provided. We are aiming for a visual approach that reads clearly at medium camera distances without photorealism.

The contract is for three to five secondary environments — a village inn interior, a railway waiting room, a mill interior, and one or two smaller spaces depending on time. We have partial photographic reference for some of these and almost none for others. Ervin will provide briefs and do a first technical review of each asset; Milovan will give final sign-off.

This is a paid freelance contract. Rate is negotiable based on experience; we will not waste your time with an unpaid test.

Required:
- Solid Blender skills, comfortable with low-to-mid poly modelling
- Experience with PBR or hand-painted texturing pipelines
- Ability to work from incomplete reference and ask sensible questions
- Some familiarity with or willingness to research vernacular Central European architecture

Nice to have:
- Previous game environment work in Godot
- Interest in the historical subject matter

Please send a portfolio link and a short note. We do not need cover letters but we do read every message we receive.

title: We Will Be at Indie Dev Beograd 2024 — Come Find Us
text:
We will be attending Indie Dev Beograd 2024 on the 12th and 13th of April. We will have a short playable slice of *Lodgings on the Near Shore* — the opening chapter, around forty minutes — running on a laptop at our table.

This is the first time the game has been playable by anyone outside the immediate team and a small group of trusted playtesters. We are nervous about it in the way you are nervous about anything that has mostly existed inside your own head for two years.

What the demo includes: the arrival sequence, the first two conversations in the inn, and the initial exploration of the estate grounds. It is in Serbian with Hungarian dialogue where appropriate; there are no translations currently in the build. The UI is functional but not final.

What we are hoping to hear from people who play it: whether the atmosphere lands, whether the pacing of the opening feels right, and — for anyone who speaks Hungarian — whether the language sounds like it belongs to the time and place.

We are also going to the event to meet other developers and to have honest conversations about the specific problems we are stuck on. If you work on games, know someone who knows historical languages, or have any connection to Vojvodina architectural history, please come and talk to us.

The event is free to attend. More details on the Indie Dev Beograd website.

title: Šta radimo — Vertigo Labs a.d.
text:
Vertigo Labs razvija i licencira CXCore — platformu za analitiku korisničkog iskustva namenjenu telekomunikacionim operaterima i maloprodajnim lancima. Platforma se isporučuje kao white-label rešenje: svaki klijent je postavlja pod sopstvenim imenom i brendom, integriše je u postojeću infrastrukturu i koristi direktno unutar svojih internih sistema.

CXCore prikuplja podatke iz više izvora: clickstream podatke s digitalnih kanala, podatke iz senzora i kamera u fizičkim prodavnicama, kao i podatke iz klijentskih CRM i billing sistema. Na osnovu tih podataka platforma u realnom vremenu generiše uvide o ponašanju korisnika — od kretanja unutar prodavnice do verovatnoće da će pretplatnik raskinuti ugovor.

Naši klijenti nisu kompanije koje traže konsultante da im objasne šta znači 'digitalna transformacija'. To su operativne organizacije s jasnim KPI-jevima, koje žele pouzdan alat koji radi i koji mogu da konfigurišu bez dugih implementacionih projekata. Upravo zbog toga je naš model licenciranja izgrađen tako da nova instalacija bude živa za četiri do osam sedmica.

Naš tim od 155 zaposlenih podeljen je na inženjering, R&D, DevOps, podršku klijentima i prodaju. Sedište kompanije je u Novom Sadu, a prodajna kancelarija u Briselu pokriva klijente u zapadnoj i centralnoj Evropi.

Ukoliko ste telekomunikacioni operater ili maloprodajni lanac i tražite analitičku platformu koja nije prototip nego proizvod koji radi u produkciji kod stvarnih klijenata, kontaktirajte naš tim.

title: CXCore platforma implementirana kod lanca Frontiera Retail u Rumuniji
text:
Vertigo Labs potpisao je ugovor o licenciranju CXCore platforme s rumunskim maloprodajnim lancem Frontiera Retail, koji trenutno posluje s 61 prodavnicom u šest rumunskih gradova.

Implementacija je počela u oktobru prošle godine i obuhvata integraciju s postojećim POS sistemom klijenta, postavljanje senzorske infrastrukture u 12 pilot prodavnica i prilagođavanje korisničkog interfejsa platforme prema vizuelnom identitetu kompanije Frontiera Retail.

Direktor proizvoda kompanije Vertigo Labs, Milena Đorđević, izjavila je: 'Implementacija u Rumuniji bila je za nas i tehnički izazov i dobra lekcija. Svako novo tržište nosi podatke koji ne izgledaju sasvim isto kao ono na čemu smo model gradili. Radimo aktivno na tome da proces adaptacije bude brži i manje zahtevan za svaki naredni klijent.'

Prva faza ugovora pokriva period od 18 meseci i uključuje upravljani hosting, SLA podršku i pristup svim ažuriranjima platforme. U drugoj fazi planira se proširenje na preostalih 49 prodavnica ukoliko pilot pokaže zadovoljavajuće rezultate.

Frontiera Retail je drugi rumunski klijent kompanije Vertigo Labs; prvi, operater mobilne telefonije Colibri Mobile, koristi platformu od 2021. godine za praćenje satisfakcije pretplatnika.

Kompanija planira da u toku 2024. godine objavi detalje o narednom koraku ekspanzije.

title: Oglas za posao: Senior ML Inženjer — adaptacija modela i transfer učenje
text:
Vertigo Labs traži iskusnog ML inženjera koji će se priključiti internom R&D timu i raditi na poboljšanju i adaptaciji modela za predviđanje ponašanja korisnika u različitim tržišnim okruženjima.

Šta ćeš raditi:
— Analizirati performanse postojećih modela kada se primenjuju na nove klijente i geografska tržišta
— Istraživati i implementirati tehnike prilagođavanja modela s ograničenim podacima (fine-tuning, domain adaptation, few-shot pristupi)
— Sarađivati s timovima koji rade na integraciji podataka iz senzora i kamera
— Dokumentovati metodologiju i rezultate na način razumljiv i tehničkim i poslovnim kolegama

Šta tražimo:
— Minimum tri godine iskustva u radu s PyTorch ili TensorFlow okvirom
— Razumevanje problema distribucijskog pomaka između skupova podataka za treniranje i produkciju
— Iskustvo s anotacijom i balansiranjem skupova podataka
— Poznavanje scikit-learn ekosistema
— Iskustvo s radom na streaming podacima je prednost (Kafka, Flink)

Šta nudimo:
— Rad na stvarnim poslovnim problemima, ne na igračkim skupovima podataka
— Tim koji je mali dovoljno da svako ima uticaj na arhitekturalne odluke
— Fleksibilan rad (hibridni model, sedište Novi Sad)

title: Zašto smo počeli ozbiljno da razmišljamo o EU AI Aktu — i šta smo naučili do sada
text:
Pre nekoliko meseci jedan od naših telekomunikacionih klijenata u Belgiji postavio nam je pitanje koje nismo očekivali: 'Možete li nam dati dokumentaciju o tome kako vaš model donosi odluke, u formatu koji naš pravni tim može da pročita?'

Prvotna reakcija našeg tehničkog tima bila je da to nije teško — imamo SHAP vrednosti, imamo metrike, imamo validation report. Problem je nastao kada smo pokušali da sve to prevedemo u nešto što osoba bez ML pozadine može da prati i što zadovoljava zahteve koji se pominju u EU AI Aktu u kontekstu sistema koji donosi odluke koje utiču na prava korisnika.

Proveli smo nekoliko sedmica analizirajući šta zapravo Akt zahteva za sisteme poput našeg churn-prediction modula. Razlika između tehničke eksplanabilnosti modela i onoga što se traži u dokumentu za regulatornu usaglašenost je veća nego što smo mislili.

Do sada smo naučili sledeće: SHAP nam daje korisnu osnovu, ali nije dovoljan sam po sebi. Potrebno je prevesti ono što SHAP pokazuje u narativ koji opisuje logiku odluke na način koji ima smisla za konkretnog korisnika. Pored toga, dokumentacija mora da prati i procenu rizika — ko može da bude pogođen i na koji način, i koje mere su preduzete.

Nismo još završili ovaj proces. Radi se o ugovoru koji ima realan rok i koji je za nas finansijski značajan. Ako neko od čitalaca ima iskustvo s pisanjem ovakvog tipa dokumentacije u okviru EU regulatornog konteksta, rado bismo razgovarali — kontaktirajte nas na info@vertigolabs.rs.

title: What We Do — GeoStruct Inženjering
text:
GeoStruct Inženjering has been delivering geospatial and structural engineering services to public clients in Serbia and the Western Balkans since 2008. Our office is in Novi Sad, inside the Science Technology Park, and most of our fieldwork takes place across Vojvodina, Šumadija and the Srem and Banat regions.

We operate in three connected areas.

The first is infrastructure inspection and documentation. We fly drone-LiDAR surveys over bridges, overpasses and retaining structures, process the resulting point clouds and produce BIM models and condition reports that road agencies and municipalities use for maintenance planning and investment decisions. We have completed surveys on more than 60 structures to date.

The second is geotechnical investigation. For road corridors, building foundations and flood-defence works, we design and supervise borehole campaigns, interpret the logs and produce subsurface models in PLAXIS that feed directly into design and risk assessments. We take care to be clear about where our data is dense and where it is not.

The third is KatastarVid, a web platform we built and now maintain for municipal governments. It pulls together cadastral parcel data and underground utility records into a single browser-based map that planning officers, permit desks and utility crews can consult without specialist GIS software. Three municipalities in Vojvodina are currently live on the platform.

Our clients include the Vojvodina Roads Directorate, the City of Zrenjanin Utility Service, Srem Regional Development Agency and a number of municipal public enterprises. We work mostly on fixed-price contracts with clearly defined deliverable sets. If you are looking for a subcontractor that will give you a point cloud and leave you to deal with it, we are probably not the right fit. If you want a team that will stay on until the model is useful, get in touch.

title: GeoStruct Completes Inspection of 14 Structures on the Vojvodina Secondary Road Network
text:
GeoStruct Inženjering has completed the field survey phase of a contract with the Vojvodina Roads Directorate covering 14 bridges and box culverts on secondary roads in Bačka and Banat.

The contract, awarded in late 2023, required drone-LiDAR survey, close-visual inspection and delivery of BIM-linked condition reports for each structure. Field work ran from February to April 2024, with survey flights completed in 22 days across sites between Kikinda in the north and Bač in the south.

The resulting point clouds are currently in processing at our Novi Sad office. Structural condition reports for the first six structures have been submitted to the client for review. Final deliverables for all 14 structures are due by the end of July 2024.

Dragan Stanković, our lead structural engineer, noted that three of the structures showed unexpected soffit cracking that had not been flagged in the previous visual inspection cycle, which was completed without drone access. The LiDAR data allowed the team to map crack patterns across the full underside of the decks and correlate them with deflection estimates, something that would have required scaffolding under the previous method.

This contract follows two earlier framework agreements with the same client and represents the largest single batch of structures we have processed in one campaign. The Vojvodina Roads Directorate has indicated it plans to extend the inspection programme to a further 20 structures in 2025, for which a new tender is expected in the autumn.

For enquiries about bridge inspection or infrastructure documentation services, contact us at office@geostruct.rs.

title: What We Learned Deploying KatastarVid in Three Small Municipalities
text:
We have been running KatastarVid in pilot with three Vojvodina municipalities since mid-2023. Inđija, Srbobran and Bač have different sizes, different levels of internal GIS capacity and different expectations of what the platform should do. After a year, here is an honest account of what has worked and what has not.

What has worked: the basic proposition. Planning officers in all three municipalities are using the platform to cross-reference cadastral parcels with utility corridor data before issuing construction permits. Before KatastarVid, that check involved a phone call to the utility company and a wait. Now it is a map query. The time saving is real and the users notice it.

Also working: the data update pipeline. We built a semi-automated import process that pulls fresh cadastral data from the Republic Geodetic Authority's public WFS feed and merges it with the municipality's own utility records. In Inđija the planning desk runs the update monthly without involving us, which is what we wanted.

What has not worked: performance at scale. When a user queries a large area — anything covering a dense part of the urban zone — load times stretch past what is acceptable. We know the cause is in the database layer, not the front-end. We have partial fixes in place but not a full solution. This is the thing we are working hardest on right now.

Also harder than expected: data quality on the utility side. Each municipality holds its utility records differently. One uses a reasonably clean CAD export, one has a hybrid of paper records and GPS tracks, and one has a spreadsheet with coordinates that do not match the cadastral geometry within any useful tolerance. Onboarding new municipalities will always involve a data-cleaning phase that is difficult to price upfront.

Our plan for the next twelve months is to resolve the performance issue and then pitch the platform to three or four larger cities. We think the product is ready for that conversation once the query times are fixed. If you work in municipal planning and want to see a demonstration, contact Milena Vukić at m.vukic@geostruct.rs.

title: Job Opening: Backend / Spatial Database Developer (KatastarVid Platform)
text:
GeoStruct Inženjering is looking for a developer to join the small team maintaining and improving KatastarVid, our municipal cadastral and utility-network web platform.

The role is based in Novi Sad with some flexibility for remote work. It is a full-time position.

What the platform looks like today: a PostGIS database holding cadastral geometry and utility-network attributes, a Python/Flask API layer, and a front-end built in Mapbox GL JS. We switched to vector tiles last year for the map rendering and it helped, but we have a known performance problem with large bounding-box queries that we need to solve properly.

What you will work on:
— Diagnosing and resolving slow query performance on large spatial datasets (50,000+ parcels in a single request)
— Redesigning the API layer to support more granular, cacheable requests
— Setting up proper database partitioning and query planning
— Working with our GIS analysts to improve how cadastral and utility data are joined and pre-aggregated
— Helping us plan the infrastructure changes needed to onboard larger municipalities

We are not looking for someone who only knows desktop GIS tools. You need to be comfortable with SQL at a level where reading and writing a complex PostGIS query is routine. Experience with vector tile generation (tippecanoe or pg_tileserv) is a plus. Python is the backend language; experience with other languages is welcome but Python is what we use.

The team you would join is small — currently one GIS analyst and one part-time contractor. You would have a direct line to Milena Vukić, our chief geodesist, and to Branimir Ostojić for anything commercial.

Salary is negotiable depending on experience. Applications should include a CV and a short note — one paragraph is enough — describing a database performance problem you have worked on and how you approached it. Send to posao@geostruct.rs.

title: Job Opening: Point-Cloud Processing Engineer (BIM Modelling, Infrastructure)
text:
We are a Novi Sad engineering consultancy and we need someone who can work with large LiDAR point clouds and turn them into structural BIM models.

Right now this pipeline takes too long and relies too heavily on manual work. We want to improve it and we are looking for a person who can both do the immediate processing work and help us build a better workflow.

Your main responsibilities:

Nice to have: experience with bridge or civil infrastructure specifically; familiarity with IFC schema; any scripting in Python or C#.

This is a full-time position based in Novi Sad. We survey mostly in the field between April and October and process through the winter, so some seasonal variation in travel is expected.

title: Voltmreža completes 6,200-meter rollout for Banat utility — project delivered on schedule
text:
Voltmreža a.d. has completed the second phase of a smart metering deployment for a distribution network operator serving rural municipalities in the Banat region. The project covered 6,200 meter points across 41 settlements, including 18 locations with fewer than 30 consumers where communication backhaul options were limited.

The contract, awarded in the third quarter of 2023, required installation of single- and three-phase meters compliant with current Serbian technical requirements for smart metering, configuration of data concentrators and radio-frequency mesh communication nodes, and full integration with the utility's existing head-end system. Voltmreža's metering team, led by site coordinator Bojan Tadić, completed all installations and acceptance tests within the agreed 22-week schedule.

A particular challenge on this project was communication coverage in three settlements where building density and terrain made the standard RF mesh topology unreliable. The team deployed additional relay nodes and adjusted channel configurations to achieve the data retrieval rates specified in the contract. All 6,200 points are now reporting within the required daily read-success threshold.

Predrag Kukić, managing director, noted: "This project adds to a metering portfolio that now covers over 24,000 points in Vojvodina. The team handled the communication problems in the outlying settlements without requesting a schedule extension, which reflects well on the planning work done before mobilisation."

The utility has indicated it will issue a further tender for a third phase covering approximately 4,000 additional meter points later this year. Voltmreža has submitted an expression of interest.

title: What we learned from two cable strikes in one year
text:
Last year was a difficult one for our civil teams in two specific incidents that we have spent several months reviewing. In both cases, underground cables were struck during excavation on streets where our cable locator showed clear signals but the actual cable position differed from both the signal reading and the as-built drawing. The combined repair and delay cost was around 340,000 dinars — not a figure that ends a business, but enough to get everyone's attention.

We have been using a Radiodetection RD8100 since 2017 and our operators are experienced with it. The problem in both incidents was not operator error in the straightforward sense. One site had four parallel LV cables installed over a period of twenty years, and the signals overlapped. The other site had a cable routed at an unexpected depth after a previous repair that was never documented. In both cases, the as-built drawings from the 1980s were off by more than three metres.

After the second incident we set up an internal review group. The conclusions were uncomfortable but not surprising. Our QGIS asset registry is accurate for infrastructure installed or touched since about 2015, because we made systematic recording part of every job at that point. For older cable runs that we have not excavated recently, the registry is essentially a cleaned-up scan of the original paper drawings, and those drawings were always approximate.

We have now made pre-excavation exploratory pitting mandatory for any street where the last confirmed survey is more than eight years old. That reduces the strike risk but adds cost and time to every job in those areas, and it does not solve the underlying data quality problem.

We are currently looking at approaches that could improve positional confidence without requiring us to re-survey every kilometre of old network from scratch. If anyone is working in this area and wants to discuss it in a practical context, we are interested in talking.

title: What UrbanVizion Does — Platform Overview
text:
Urban planning produces decisions that shape a city for decades. The tools planners use to make those decisions should be as serious as the decisions themselves.

UrbanVizion is a software platform for municipalities, regional agencies, and urban planning practices. It covers the core workflow of spatial plan development: loading and validating spatial data, building scenario models, visualising proposals in three dimensions, and collecting structured feedback from residents and stakeholders.

ZoneSim lets a planner define land-use zones, set building parameters, and compare up to four scenarios side by side. Changes to one scenario do not affect the others, and every version is stored so the decision trail is visible after the project closes.

CityView 3D renders those scenarios as navigable three-dimensional models in the browser. No plugin, no desktop install. A resident attending a public consultation session can walk through a proposed neighbourhood on a tablet they brought from home.

PublicVoice replaces comment boxes and public meeting sign-up sheets with a structured form that ties each comment to a specific parcel, zone, or street segment. Planners get a map of where concerns are concentrated, not a stack of unindexed PDFs.

DataBridge handles the part nobody enjoys: taking cadastral data in half a dozen source formats, checking it for geometry errors, resolving coordinate reference system differences, and delivering clean layers that the rest of the platform can use.

We work with cities that have between 30,000 and 500,000 residents. Our clients are mostly in Austria, Slovenia, and Serbia. We speak the language of spatial planning — zone categories, floor-area ratios, setback rules — because our founding team includes people who spent years doing that work before they started writing software.

title: UrbanVizion Signs Agreement with Municipal Planning Office of Feldkirchen an der Mur
text:
UrbanVizion has signed a two-year service agreement with the municipal planning office of Feldkirchen an der Mur, a town of approximately 14,000 residents in the Austrian state of Styria. The agreement covers a full deployment of the ZoneSim and PublicVoice modules for an ongoing revision of the town's spatial development plan.

The Feldkirchen project is the fourth active deployment UrbanVizion has in Austria and the first in Styria. The planning office will use ZoneSim to model three alternative development scenarios for a mixed-use expansion area on the southern edge of the town centre, and will use PublicVoice to run two rounds of structured public consultation before the plan is submitted to the regional authority for approval.

Marija Vukić, head of product at UrbanVizion, said the Feldkirchen project presented a specific technical requirement: a significant portion of the expansion area borders a block of nineteenth-century residential buildings, which means the 3-D visualisation will need to represent older roof forms accurately enough for residents to recognise their neighbourhood. The team is treating this project as a practical test of improvements currently in development.

The agreement was facilitated in part by a referral from an existing client, the planning office of Wolfsberg, which has used UrbanVizion's platform since 2022.

UrbanVizion currently has active deployments in four municipalities across Austria and Slovenia, and one pilot project with a planning agency in Novi Sad. The company is based at NTP Novi Sad and has nineteen employees.

title: Computational Geometry Engineer (Mid–Senior)
text:
UrbanVizion is looking for an engineer with a strong background in 3-D geometry processing to join the CityView team in Novi Sad.

The core problem you will work on: we generate city-scale building models from cadastral footprints and height attributes. The pipeline works well for simple geometries but produces obviously wrong results for historic buildings with complex roof forms. We want to improve the quality of generated models using whatever combination of procedural rules, point-cloud processing, and data-driven approaches makes sense technically.

What the role involves day to day:
— Writing and maintaining Python and C++ geometry processing code in our spatial pipeline
— Working with GDAL, CGAL, and Open3D (or equivalent libraries you bring)
— Evaluating lidar point-cloud datasets and building workflows to extract roof geometry where coverage exists
— Designing fallback procedural rules for areas without lidar
— Collaborating with our GIS specialist on data quality and with our frontend team on how models are delivered to CesiumJS

What we are looking for:
— Solid understanding of 3-D mesh generation and repair
— Experience processing point-cloud data (lidar or photogrammetry) — any toolchain
— Comfort with PostGIS for spatial queries
— Some exposure to urban or architectural geometry is a plus but not required
— Serbian or English; German is a bonus

We are a team of nineteen people in a single office at NTP Novi Sad. The role is on-site with flexibility. Salary range is 2,400–3,200 EUR gross depending on experience, plus equipment budget. We do not offer equity at this stage but expect to revisit that after the Series A closes.

To apply, send a CV and a short note (half a page is enough) describing a geometry problem you have solved and what made it hard. We do not use automated screening.

title: What We Learned Showing Our Platform to Planners in Three Countries
text:
In January we attended the Central European Urban Planning Technology Exchange in Ljubljana — a two-day event that brings together municipal planning staff, software vendors, and regional policy people from Austria, Slovenia, Croatia, and Hungary. We brought a working demo and talked to around thirty planners over two days. Here is what we actually heard.

The 3-D model problem is real. We knew our procedural building models looked rough in historic areas. We did not fully appreciate how much it matters in a public consultation context. Two separate planners told us, independently, that when residents see a building that looks nothing like the one they live in, they stop listening to everything else. The model breaks the trust the consultation is supposed to build. This is now the top engineering priority for the first half of 2024.

Planners want comfort data but are realistic about precision. Several people asked whether we could show wind or shadow effects at street level. When we explained the computational difficulty, the most common response was not disappointment but a practical question: would a rough estimate that runs fast be useful, or is it better to have nothing than something that might mislead? Most of them said a fast rough estimate would be useful if it was clearly labelled as indicative. That framing helps us define what we actually need to build.

Coordinate misalignment is a known frustration. We were not the only vendor at the event dealing with datum transformation issues. A planner from a Slovenian city showed us a printed overlay where building outlines from two official datasets were offset by about two metres. She said she had learned to live with it. We told her we were actively working on it. She looked moderately hopeful.

The event reinforced that the problems we are working on are real product problems, not edge cases. We will be back next year, and hopefully with better roofs.

title: Junior GIS and Data Integration Specialist
text:
We are expanding the DataBridge team and looking for someone who understands spatial data formats, coordinate reference systems, and data quality well enough to build and maintain import pipelines for municipal clients.

This is a junior-to-mid role. We will teach you our systems; you need to bring solid fundamentals.

Day-to-day responsibilities:
— Ingesting client spatial data (Shapefile, GeoJSON, GML, DXF, national exchange formats) and identifying quality issues
— Writing and maintaining GDAL-based transformation pipelines in Python
— Investigating coordinate reference system mismatches — we work across MGI 1901, ETRS89, and local projections and the differences matter
— Documenting data sources and transformation parameters for client deliveries
— Supporting the GIS specialist on validation checks before data reaches the platform

What you should know:
— EPSG codes, datum transformations, and why they sometimes go wrong
— GDAL / OGR command-line tools and the Python bindings
— PostGIS at a working level
— Basic Python scripting — you do not need to be a software engineer but you need to read and write scripts without help

Nice to have:
— Familiarity with Serbian or Austrian cadastral data formats
— Experience with Proj grid shift files
— Any exposure to QGIS plugin development

This is a full-time on-site position at NTP Novi Sad. Salary range 1,400–1,800 EUR gross. We are a small company and you will be working directly with the people making product decisions from day one. Application: CV and one paragraph explaining why coordinate reference systems are harder than they look.

title: UrbanVizion Open Demo Day — NTP Novi Sad
text:

We are hosting this event partly because we believe in showing work in progress rather than finished demos, and partly because we are genuinely looking for people who might want to work on these problems with us — whether as future employees, as collaborators from another organisation, or simply as people who know something we do not.

title: Šta radimo i kako radimo
text:
RoboFleks projektuje, gradi i pušta u rad robotske radne ćelije prilagođene pogonima u kojima ne postoji IT odeljenje sa deset ljudi i budžet kakav imaju multinacionalne kompanije. Naši klijenti su fabrike sa 20 do 300 zaposlenih, koje imaju konkretne probleme: sporu paletizaciju, neujednačen kvalitet zavara, visoku stopu grešaka pri ručnom rukovanju delovima.

Proces počinje obilaskom pogona. Naš inženjer dolazi, meri taktove, razgovara sa poslovođom i snima raspored. Tek posle toga predlažemo rešenje — ponekad je to kobot na postolju sa pneumatskim hvatačem, ponekad je to kompletna integracija sa postojećim konvejerom i PLC-om koji klijent već ima. Ne prodajemo robote kao robu; prodajemo funkcionalnu ćeliju koja radi od prvog dana.

Koristimo Universal Robots platformu za kobot aplikacije jer je programibilna bez specijalnog znanja, što znači da klijent može sam da prilagodi putanje posle naše instalacije. Za teže aplikacije, poput zavarivanja i rukovanja teškim teretom, radimo sa Mitsubishi MELFA industrijskim robotima. Upravljački ormari su bazirani na Siemens S7-1500 sa standardizovanim SCADA interfejsom koji svaki operater može da nauči za pola dana.

Nakon puštanja u rad, nudimo ugovor o servisnoj podršci koji uključuje dve preventivne posete godišnje i telefonsku dostupnost inženjera radnim danima. Naš prosečni odziv na kvar je ispod četiri sata za klijente u Vojvodini.

Trenutno sarađujemo sa više od 30 aktivnih klijenata u Srbiji, Bosni i Hercegovini i Severnoj Makedoniji. Svaki novi projekat vodi imenovani inženjer koji ostaje kontakt osoba tokom celог životnog ciklusa ćelije.

title: Završena instalacija paletizacione linije za Palić Pakovanje
text:
Početkom februara 2024. naš tim je završio puštanje u rad automatizovane paletizacione linije u pogonu kompanije Palić Pakovanje d.o.o. u Subotici. Linija radi sa UR16e kobotom koji slaže kutije od 8 do 22 kilograma na euro palete u četiri različita uzorka slaganja, u zavisnosti od aktivnog naloga.

Projektat je trajao ukupno sedam nedelja od prve posete pogonu do predaje dokumentacije. Centralni deo instalacije je prilagođeni vakuumski hvatač koji smo projektovali interno jer standardni hvatač iz kataloga nije mogao da prihvati sve formate ambalaže koje klijent koristi. Hvatač je napravljen kod kooperanta u Novom Sadu prema našim crtežima.

Klijent je pre ove instalacije imao dvoje radnika koji su ručno paletizirali smenu od osam sati. Novi sistem radi u kontinuitetu bez paletizacionih zastoja. Takt od 420 kutija po satu zadovoljen je već u prvoj nedelji rada.

Direktor pogona Palić Pakovanja, gospodin Ištvan Feješ, izjavio je da je ekipa bila profesionalna tokom celog projekta i da su eventualne sitne prilagodbe rešavali odmah na licu mesta, bez čekanja.

Ova instalacija je naš deveti završeni projekat u prehrambenom i ambalažnom sektoru. Dokumentacija je pripremljena za srpsku CE proceduru i predata klijentu u punom obimu.

title: Tražimo: Integracioni inženjer robotike (srednji nivo)
text:
RoboFleks d.o.o. traži integracionog inženjera za rad na instalaciji i puštanju u rad robotskih ćelija kod naših klijenata u Vojvodini i regionu.

Šta radite na ovom poslu:
- Programiranje kobot aplikacija na Universal Robots platformi (URScript i PolyScope)
- Električno povezivanje i testiranje sigurnosnih kola prema SIL/PL zahtevima
- Izrada tehničke dokumentacije za CE prijem
- Komunikacija sa klijentom tokom puštanja u rad
- Povremeni servisni izlasci za klijente u regionu

Šta tražimo:
- Završene studije mašinskog ili elektrotehničkog inženjerstva
- Iskustvo sa PLC programiranjem (Siemens Step 7 ili TIA Portal)
- Osnovno znanje o industrijskim komunikacionim protokolima (Profinet, Modbus TCP)
- Vozačka dozvola B kategorije obavezna
- Poznavanje engleskog na nivou čitanja tehničke dokumentacije

Šta je prednost:
- Rad sa Universal Robots ili sličnim kobot platformama
- Iskustvo sa Sick ili Pilz sigurnosnim komponentama
- Poznavanje ROS okruženja (nije obavezno, ali korisno za razvojne projekte)

Nudimo:
- Ugovor na neodređeno vreme
- Terenski dodatak za svaki dan van Novog Sada
- Obuku kod proizvođača robota u prvoj godini
- Tim koji nema nepotrebne sastanke

Molbe slati na karijere@robofleks.rs do 10. aprila 2024.

title: Tražimo: Junior softverski inženjer — upravljački sistemi i vizija
text:
Otvaramo poziciju za mlađeg inženjera koji bi radio na razvoju internih softverskih alata i integraciji vizijskih sistema u naše robotske ćelije. Ovo nije tipičan web ili aplikativni razvoj — radite na softveru koji direktno kontroliše mašine u pogonu.

Šta biste radili:
- Razvoj Python skripti za automatizovano testiranje i kalibraciju vizijskih kamera Keyence IV3
- Podrška starijim inženjerima u strukturiranju URScript koda za ponovnu upotrebu
- Pisanje internih alata za generisanje PLC parametarskih blokova iz Excel unosa (proof of concept koji interno koristimo treba da postane stabilan alat)
- Dokumentovanje softverskih rešenja koja razvijamo

Šta tražimo:
- Završene ili poslednje godine studija elektrotehnike, računarstva ili srodnih oblasti
- Solidno znanje Pythona; iskustvo sa NumPy i OpenCV je prednost
- Razumevanje osnova digitalnih I/O sistema
- Preciznost u pisanju dokumentacije

Napominjemo direktno: imamo alat za upravljanje tipskim konfiguracijama ćelija koji je počeo kao Excel tabela i malo izmakao kontroli. Jedna od prvih zadataka biće rad na tome da ga učinimo upotrebljivim. Tražimo nekoga kome ovakav zadatak izgleda kao izazov, ne kao kazna.

Radno mesto je u Novom Sadu, u NTP kampusu. Povremeni izlasci na terene su mogući ali nisu dominantni deo posla. Zainteresovani kandidati mogu poslati kratak opis svog tehničkog iskustva i primere koda (GitHub link ili prilog) na karijere@robofleks.rs.

title: Tehnički dan u NTP Novi Sad: Robotika za srednja preduzeća
text:
RoboFleks organizuje otvoreni tehnički dan u prostoru Naučno-tehnološkog parka Novi Sad u sredu, 15. maja 2024. od 10 do 16 časova.

Program je namenjen tehničkim direktorima, poslovođama i vlasnicima malih i srednje velikih pogona koji razmatraju uvođenje robota ili kobota, ali nisu sigurni gde da počnu i koliko to zaista košta.
