title: PrintMetal 3D Completes First Delivery for Fluid-Control Customer Radovan Group
text:
In January 2024, PrintMetal 3D completed its first production delivery for Radovan Group, a manufacturer of industrial valve bodies and actuator housings based in Zrenjanin. The order covered fourteen 316L stainless valve seat inserts that Radovan Group needed to replace a discontinued casting that their usual supplier had stopped producing.

The parts went through our full production process: build preparation in Materialise Magics, printing on our SLM 280, stress relief, and CNC finishing to bring sealing surfaces to the specified Ra and dimensional tolerances. All fourteen parts were measured on our Zeiss CMM before dispatch. Radovan Group's own quality team conducted a pressure test at 240 bar on a representative sample, and all tested parts passed on the first attempt.

For us this job was notable for a couple of reasons. First, the valve seat geometry had internal features that made conventional re-machining from billet difficult and slow. Additive manufacturing was not chosen because it was fashionable — it was chosen because it was the practical answer. Second, the order arrived on a Wednesday with a ten-day deadline. We were able to nest the parts alongside another customer's brackets in a single build, which kept the per-part cost reasonable for Radovan Group without pushing back any existing orders.

Radovan Group's production engineer, Milena Stojanović, noted that the main concern going in was whether the density and surface integrity of the printed parts would hold up under pressure cycling. We are glad the results answered that question directly.

We are not announcing a long-term supply agreement here — that is for Radovan Group to decide based on their ongoing requirements. What we can say is that the technical path is proven, and we are ready to repeat it.

title: Job Opening: SLM Machine Operator / Process Technician
text:
PrintMetal 3D is a small metal additive manufacturing company based at NTP Novi Sad. We currently operate four SLM machines and a post-processing line, and we are looking for a hands-on operator and process technician to join our production floor.

What the role involves:

- Running build preparation tasks in Materialise Magics under supervision of our application engineers
- Operating the shot-peening cabinet and supporting CNC finishing work
- Conducting Archimedes density measurements and logging results
- Keeping machine maintenance logs up to date and flagging issues early

What we are looking for:
- A background in mechanical engineering, materials, or a related technical field — a degree is helpful but not required if you have workshop experience
- Comfort working with metal powders and following strict handling and safety procedures
- Some exposure to CAD or metrology software is a plus
- Attention to detail: our customers test their parts, and a mistake in powder handling or build setup shows up in their results

What we offer:
- Full-time position, Monday to Friday, occasional Saturday when lead times are tight
- On-the-job training on SLM machines and Magics
- A small team where you can see the full production process rather than one small corner of it
- Salary in line with the Novi Sad manufacturing market, reviewed after six months

We are not looking for someone who wants to manage from a distance. This is a floor role. If you like working with machines, solving small problems every day, and being part of something that is growing steadily, we would like to hear from you.

Send a CV and a short note about your relevant experience to the address on our contact page. Applications are open until the position is filled.

title: Services — PrintMetal 3D
text:
We print metal parts. That sounds simple because the core of what we do is straightforward: a customer sends us a CAD file or a worn-out original, and we send back a dimensionally accurate metal part, usually within five to eight working days. What is less simple is making that happen reliably across four machines, a dozen active materials on the market, and customers whose tolerances and surface requirements are all different.

Our standard materials are 316L stainless steel, AlSi10Mg aluminium alloy, and 17-4 PH stainless. We take on Ti-6Al-4V jobs for established customers on a case-by-case basis. Every build is accompanied by a density coupon measured by the Archimedes method, and critical parts get a dimensional report from our Zeiss CMM before they leave the building.

Post-processing is handled in-house: we do stress relief and age hardening in our induction furnace, shot peening for surface compression, and CNC finishing where Ra values below 1.6 µm are required. We do not offer painting or electroplating.

For customers who do not have print-ready files, our application engineers can work from a technical drawing, a STEP file, or a physical sample. Reverse engineering from a sample adds two to three days to the lead time depending on complexity.

We serve customers across the Vojvodina automotive supply chain, fluid-control equipment producers, and toolmakers who need inserts or conformal-cooling cores faster than a conventional machining house can deliver. Our minimum order is one part. We do not have a maximum — we have run batches of 200 bracket assemblies for a single customer.

If you have a part that has failed pressure testing, broken in service, or simply costs too much to source, send us the drawing. We will give you a straight answer about whether additive manufacturing is the right process, and a quote within 24 hours.

title: Why Our Build Schedule Lives in a Spreadsheet — and Why That Has to Change
text:
Every Monday morning, one of our application engineers — usually Tomislav Horvat — sits down with a list of open orders and spends two to three hours working out what goes into which machine that week. He looks at materials, deadlines, part sizes, and which jobs can share a build without contaminating each other's powder. Then he opens Materialise Magics, tries a few nesting arrangements, estimates platform fill, and writes the result into a spreadsheet that the rest of the team works from.

This process works. We have been doing it for five years and we have not missed a deadline that was actually achievable. But it has three problems that are getting harder to ignore as our order volume grows.

The first is time. Two to three hours of Tomislav's Monday is two to three hours he is not doing application engineering, parameter testing, or anything else. When rush orders come in mid-week, the process repeats in a compressed and more stressful form.

The second is utilization. We track platform fill after each build, and our average over 2023 was 61.4 percent. We believe 75 percent or above is achievable without adding machine time, simply through better nesting decisions. At our throughput, that difference is meaningful.

The third is that the knowledge is in Tomislav's head. He knows which materials cross-contaminate, which customers are flexible on scheduling, and which part geometries nest poorly. None of that is written down in a way that a tool — or a new colleague — could use.

We are not describing this as a crisis. It is an inefficiency we have been aware of for a while, and we are now actively looking for help to address it. If you have worked on scheduling or nesting problems in a manufacturing context and want to talk about what an approach might look like for a four-machine shop with varied small orders, we are interested in hearing from you. Our contact details are on this site.

title: Part-Time Opening: Data & Process Analyst (6-Month Contract)
text:
PrintMetal 3D is looking for someone to help us make better use of the process data we collect across our four SLM machines. This is a part-time, six-month contract — roughly two to three days per week — based at NTP Novi Sad with some flexibility on hours.

The context: we have kept detailed records of every build we have run since mid-2019. Each record includes the material, machine ID, laser parameters used, coupon density measurement, and the pass/fail result from customer pressure testing or our own dimensional inspection. We also have metallographic cross-section images for a subset of builds. We believe there is useful information in this dataset that we have not been able to extract with the time and tools we currently have.

What the work involves:
- Cleaning and structuring our existing build log data (mostly in Excel, some in PDF reports)
- Exploring correlations between parameters and quality outcomes
- Building a practical, readable summary of findings — not an academic report, something our engineers can act on
- If findings support it, helping us set up a simple decision-support tool for parameter selection

What we need from you:
- Solid practical skills in data analysis — Python or R preferred, Excel acceptable for simpler work
- The ability to understand a manufacturing process quickly without needing everything explained twice
- No requirement for a specific academic background; results matter more than credentials

What we do not need:
- A consultant who will tell us to buy expensive software
- Someone who will be here for two weeks and then disappear

We are a team of thirteen people making metal parts. If you can help us reduce our build failure rate with the data we already have, that is worth a great deal to us. Interested? Send a short message explaining what similar work you have done.

title: What We Do — HempTex Vojvodina
text:
HempTex Vojvodina grows industrial hemp and turns it into usable textile raw material. That is the whole business. We are not a fashion brand and we are not a cosmetics company. We are a fibre producer.

We farm on our own land near Bačka Palanka in the Vojvodina plain. The soil here is well-suited to hemp — flat, reasonably fertile, easy to manage mechanically. We plant approved low-THC varieties, typically a French long-straw cultivar that gives us a good bast yield, and we harvest by the end of August. After cutting, the stems are left to rett in the field or moved to our water-retting pond depending on the season and the weather forecast.

Once retted and dried, the stems go through our decorticator, which separates the woody hurds from the bast fibre. The bast is then scutched, graded by hand on a long grading table, and packed for dispatch. Long-line fibre goes to textile converters. Short-fibre tow goes to non-woven and insulation customers. We also run a carding and light spinning operation that produces yarn on cones for smaller textile workshops.

Our non-woven mat line uses a needle-punch process. The mats are used mainly as horticultural grow mats and as acoustic insulation panels by a building-products customer in Novi Sad.

We do not promise things we cannot deliver. Lead times are seasonal. We can usually confirm fibre specifications before an order is placed, and we keep samples from each graded batch for six months. If you are a buyer who needs consistent quality and honest communication, we are worth talking to. If you need year-round guaranteed supply of a very tightly specified yarn count, we are probably not the right supplier yet.

Contact Dragana Bačić at the number below for commercial enquiries.

title: First Delivery to Slovenian Converter Completed
text:
We completed our first full commercial delivery to Kovaček Technical Textiles in Slovenia at the end of April. The order was for 2.4 tonnes of long-line bast fibre, graded to their specification of minimum 45 cm average fibre length with a shive content below 4%.

This took longer to set up than we expected. Kovaček's technical buyer, a man named Tomaž Prezelj, visited us twice before he was satisfied with our grading consistency. His main concern was that our grading was done by eye and by hand, and he wanted to understand how repeatable it was from batch to batch. We agreed to provide a sample from each half-tonne lot before the full lot was packed, which added time to the process but gave him confidence.

Of the 2.4 tonnes delivered, 2.1 tonnes met the long-fibre specification. The remaining 0.3 tonnes fell just below the length threshold and was downgraded to tow price. That is not a result we are happy with, but it is honest. We told Kovaček what happened and they appreciated that.

The relationship is now ongoing. We have an informal agreement to supply at least 5 tonnes in the 2024 harvest season, subject to quality. For us this is the most significant customer development since we started. Long-fibre sales at the price Kovaček pays are substantially better for the business than selling everything as tow.

The main thing we learned from this process is that our fibre-length consistency needs to improve. We are looking at where in the line the variation is coming from. We will write more about that when we have something concrete to say.

title: Why Our Decorticator Is the Thing We Talk About Most
text:
Anyone who visits us and asks about production challenges will hear about the decorticator within about three minutes. We are slightly embarrassed by how often we bring it up, but it is genuinely the central technical problem in our business right now, so here is a straightforward explanation of what it does and why it matters.

Decortication is the step where you separate the hemp stem into two parts: the woody inner core, called hurds or shives, and the outer bast fibre, which is what goes into textiles. Getting those two apart cleanly, without breaking the long bast fibres, is harder than it sounds.

Our machine is a hammer-mill type. Rotating hammers break the woody core and the action of the machine pulls the fibre through. The problem is that the hammers do not distinguish between hurds and fibre. They break what they hit. Long fibres that get caught in the wrong place get shortened.

We have experimented with feed rate — slower is better but reduces throughput significantly. We have adjusted the clearance between the rotor and the housing. Both changes helped at the margins. Neither solved the core problem.

What we do not know is exactly where in the line the breakage is concentrated. It could be at the in-feed. It could be at the hammers themselves. It could be at the exit, where fibre bundles can catch on the housing. We have watched the line running and formed opinions, but opinions are not measurements.

If we could get someone with real process knowledge to look at this with us — measure what is happening, propose specific modifications or settings, and help us test them — we think there is a realistic path to recovering a meaningful share of that long-fibre yield. That is the outcome we are working toward.

title: Small Grant Approved for Equipment Assessment
text:
We received confirmation in late August that a small grant application we submitted to the Vojvodina Development Fund earlier this year has been approved. The grant is for 4,200 euros and is designated for technical consultancy related to our decortication line.

This does not solve the problem, but it gives us a defined budget to start working on it properly. Until now, any time we spent on diagnostics came directly out of operating time and cost us in other ways. With a ring-fenced amount, we can engage someone with process knowledge on a structured basis rather than asking for informal opinions at trade fairs.

We are now in the process of identifying who that might be. We have spoken informally to one person with flax-processing experience, but flax and hemp decorticators are not identical machines and we want to be careful about assuming the same solutions apply.

The grant has a spending deadline of June 2025, which means any consultancy work needs to be completed and documented before the 2025 harvest season ends. That is actually a useful pressure. We want to test any proposed changes during the 2025 processing run while the conditions are comparable to this year.

We will post an update once we have a clearer plan. If you have worked on hammer-mill bast-fibre lines and you are reading this, contact Miroslav directly.

title: First External Clinic Pilot Completed: Eight Patients, Eight Weeks
text:
We finished our first pilot outside our own practice in January. Eight patients recovering from total knee replacement at a private outpatient centre in Novi Sad used VitaMonitor for their full eight-week home-rehabilitation programme. Here is what we found.

Adherence: patients completed sixty-eight percent of scheduled sessions, compared to a historical average of around forty percent for paper-based home programmes at the same centre. We are cautious about reading too much into that number — the population was small and patients in a technology pilot may behave differently — but it is an encouraging direction.

Accuracy issues: the pilot confirmed what we already suspected. In about one in five sessions the app produced joint-angle readings our physiotherapists judged to be unreliable. In almost every case the cause was poor home lighting or a background that confused the pose-estimation model. We are now treating this as our primary technical problem and are actively looking for collaborators with computer vision expertise.

Physiotherapist time: the supervising physiotherapist at the external centre reported spending an average of thirty minutes per week reviewing flagged sessions for all eight patients combined, compared to an estimated four to five hours for phone-call-based follow-up she had used previously. She described this as the most practically useful aspect of the platform.

Patient feedback: collected via a simple five-question form at the end of the programme. The aspect rated most positively was the spoken feedback during sessions. The most common complaint was that the app sometimes asked patients to reposition their phone mid-exercise, which they found disruptive.

We are using these results to prioritise our development roadmap for the rest of 2024 and to prepare a larger pilot proposal. Thank you to the team at the external centre for their time and honest feedback.

title: How VitaMonitor Works
text:
After orthopaedic surgery, the hardest part of recovery often happens at home, far from the clinic, with a printed sheet of exercises and nobody to tell you whether you are doing them correctly. VitaMonitor was built to change that.

The patient downloads our mobile app before leaving the hospital. Their physiotherapist sets up a weekly exercise schedule — the number of sets, the target range of motion, the pace — using our web dashboard. Each day, the patient opens the app, stands in front of their phone, and works through the assigned exercises. The camera watches the movement in real time, calculates the angle at the relevant joint, and gives simple spoken and visual feedback: go a little further, slow down, straighten your leg.

At the end of each session the app sends a summary to the physiotherapist's dashboard. Sessions that look normal are filed automatically. Sessions where the movement pattern falls outside the expected range are flagged for review. The physiotherapist decides whether to call the patient, adjust the protocol, or simply note the deviation.

Surgeons who refer patients to us receive a one-page progress PDF at the four-week and eight-week mark, formatted to match the outcome measures they already use.

We support knee and hip replacement rehabilitation protocols today. Shoulder and Achilles protocols are in development. The app runs on any Android or iOS smartphone made in the last five years and does not require any wearable sensor or additional hardware.

Our team is based at NTP Novi Sad. If you are a physiotherapist, clinic manager, or orthopaedic surgeon and want to discuss a pilot, write to us at info@vitamonitor.rs.

title: Junior Computer Vision Engineer (part-time, on-site Novi Sad)
text:
VitaMonitor is a small team building a smartphone rehabilitation platform for patients recovering from orthopaedic surgery. We are looking for a junior computer vision engineer to join us part-time, three days a week, on-site at NTP Novi Sad.

What you will work on:
Our current pose-estimation pipeline uses MediaPipe Pose running on-device. The core problem we are trying to solve is that the pipeline is accurate in controlled lighting but loses reliability in typical home environments — cluttered rooms, varied lighting, loose clothing. Your main task will be to investigate and improve the robustness of joint-angle extraction under these real-world conditions.

Day-to-day work will include:
- Analysing our existing dataset of session videos labelled with ground-truth joint angles
- Testing preprocessing steps — adaptive histogram equalisation, background subtraction, confidence-weighted smoothing — and measuring their effect on angle error
- Exploring whether a lightweight correction model trained on our data can reduce systematic errors from the raw MediaPipe keypoints
- Writing clean Python code that can be integrated into our Django backend or compiled for on-device use

Stack we use: Python, OpenCV, MediaPipe, scikit-learn, Label Studio, Django, PostgreSQL, React Native.

What we are looking for:
- Solid Python and basic OpenCV experience
- Familiarity with body-pose estimation (MediaPipe, OpenPose, or similar)
- Comfortable working with small datasets and understanding why that is a constraint
- Interest in the medical context — you do not need a clinical background but you need to care about accuracy

We cannot offer a large salary at this stage. We offer a real problem, direct access to the clinical team, and the chance to see your code used by actual patients within weeks of writing it. Send a CV and two or three lines about a computer vision project you have worked on to posao@vitamonitor.rs.

title: Why 34 Annotated Sessions Are Not Enough (and What We Are Doing About It)
text:
We want to be straightforward about something that has been the main bottleneck in our technical development for the past few months.

Our platform now has thirty-four patients who use it regularly. That is thirty-four people doing daily exercises, which adds up to a few hundred video sessions every week. We have always wanted to build an automated quality-scoring system so that our physiotherapists do not have to watch every session — just the ones that need attention. Sounds reasonable. The problem is that we have only managed to annotate thirty-four sessions in full. That is one per patient, done by Dragana and Nikola working through lunch breaks and early mornings with Label Studio open on a second screen.

We tried training a classifier on those thirty-four examples. A simple decision tree on the joint-angle time-series. A slightly less simple LSTM. The results were the same each time: the model learned the training examples almost perfectly and then performed at roughly chance level on held-out sessions. This is a textbook small-data overfitting problem and we are not embarrassed to name it directly.

Annotating faster is not straightforward. A single session takes twenty to twenty-five minutes to label properly, because the annotator has to watch the video multiple times, mark specific frames, and write a short note on anything unusual. We cannot cut corners on annotation quality — the labels are clinical judgements, and a bad label is worse than no label.

We have been reading about semi-supervised learning, self-training, and contrastive methods that can make use of unlabelled data. We have also looked at simple rule-based baselines — if the knee angle does not reach the protocol target for more than half the repetitions, flag the session — which might be good enough for a first version even if they are not elegant.

If you work on this kind of problem — small labelled datasets, time-series data from video, healthcare constraints — we would genuinely like to talk. We are at NTP Novi Sad and we have the raw video, the annotation tooling, and a clinical team who can explain what a good session looks like.

title: What We Do — Kognitiva a.d.
text:
Kognitiva builds analytics platforms that financial institutions and public bodies in South-East Europe use to make faster, better-documented decisions.

We have been doing this since 2008, when two of our founders left positions at a Serbian retail bank frustrated by the gap between what the data showed and what the business was able to act on. The original product was a credit-scoring module that sat on top of a core banking system and produced a structured report a loan officer could sign. That product is still running, much changed, at three clients today.

Today our work spans the full lifecycle of a data product. We connect to a client's source systems — core banking platforms, claims management software, government registries — clean and govern the incoming data, build or refine scoring and detection models, and operate those models in production. We run monitoring dashboards so clients can see model drift before it becomes a business problem, and we produce audit-ready output so that compliance teams have what they need without calling our engineers.

Our clients range from a retail bank with four branches to an insurance group operating in six countries. What they share is that they make a large number of structured decisions every day — credit, claims, underwriting, benefit eligibility — and those decisions need to be fast, consistent and explainable to someone outside the organisation.

We are not a general-purpose software house and we do not take on projects outside financial services and closely related public-sector work. That focus means our team understands the regulatory environment, the data formats and the business constraints without a lengthy discovery phase.

Our headquarters are in Novi Sad, at the NTP Novi Sad campus, with offices in Zagreb and Bucharest. Client-facing staff travel regularly; engineering teams are mostly office-based in Novi Sad.

title: What we learned running SHAP explanations in a 400-millisecond window
text:
We have been using SHAP values to explain our scoring model outputs for about two years. When we started, the primary audience was our own data scientists — a way to sanity-check that a model was using features sensibly. Over the past year, the audience has changed. Compliance officers, auditors and, in one case, a national insurance regulator have started asking to see these explanations as part of formal reviews.

That shift changed our requirements considerably. An explanation that satisfies a data scientist is not always one that satisfies an auditor. We learned this the hard way during a regulatory review last autumn, when a compliance team reviewed a sample of 200 declined applications and found that our explanations were internally consistent but not always meaningful in plain language. A feature named 'ratio_claims_36m' appearing as the top contributor does not tell an underwriter or an applicant much without additional context.

The second problem was latency. Our scoring pipeline is required to return a response within 400 milliseconds end-to-end for the majority of requests. Full TreeExplainer SHAP on our largest model added between 80 and 140 milliseconds per call depending on the record. In testing that was acceptable. In production, where we run several hundred concurrent requests during morning peaks, it pushed us over threshold on roughly 6% of calls.

We addressed the latency issue by caching background dataset summaries and running SHAP computation asynchronously for calls that were not in the critical response path, attaching the explanation to the stored decision record rather than the live API response. This brought the synchronous overhead down to around 18 milliseconds.

The plain-language problem is harder. We built a template layer that maps feature names to human-readable phrases and constructs a ranked list of contributing factors. It works for the common cases. It does not work well when the top contributors are interaction terms or when a combination of moderate factors — none dominant — drives the score. That is the problem we are still working on, and it is the reason we have started talking to external research groups who work on explanation methods.

We do not think this is a niche problem. Any scoring system operating under the EU's consumer-credit or insurance regulations faces the same requirement. If you have worked on this and want to compare notes, our research team is reachable at research@kognitiva.rs.

title: Products and Services — Polje360 d.o.o.
text:
Polje360 makes the hardware and software that goes between a farm's soil data and the machine that applies fertiliser. Our two core products are the VRS-7 controller and the FieldDesk cab terminal. Together they form a closed loop: the agronomist uploads a prescription map through the Farm Portal, the operator loads it on the terminal in the cab, and the VRS-7 adjusts the applicator rate automatically as the machine moves across the field.

VRS-7 Variable-Rate Controller
The VRS-7 mounts directly on solid and liquid fertiliser applicators. It reads GPS position and matches it to the prescription map in real time, sending control signals to the section valves or the metering drive. It logs every application event with position, rate, and timestamp. Output can be adjusted between 20 and 400 percent of the base rate without stopping. The unit is sealed to IP67 and rated for operating temperatures from -20 to +55 degrees Celsius.

FieldDesk ISOBUS Terminal
The FieldDesk is a 10-inch capacitive touchscreen terminal that mounts in the cab and communicates with the VRS-7 and compatible implements over the ISOBUS network. The operator sees the field map, current rate, coverage progress, and any active alarms. No laptop is needed in the field. The terminal stores maps locally so it works without a data connection.

Farm Portal
The Farm Portal is our annual software licence. It runs in a browser and handles prescription map creation from soil sample imports, operation records, application totals by field and season, and fleet status across all registered terminals. Customers with multiple farms or cooperative members can manage separate access levels within a single account.

Dealer Support
We supply dealers with installation kits, documentation, and direct telephone support from our team in Novi Sad. We train dealer technicians at our facility twice a year. Dealers can order CAN bus adapters for supported tractor models directly through the portal.

The cooperative's member farms grow wheat, sunflower, and corn on a combined area of roughly 8,400 hectares. For Polje360, this deployment is the first step in a planned expansion into North Macedonia and Kosovo. Agromehanika Skopje has agreed to carry the full product range and will send two technicians to Novi Sad for dealer training in May.

Sales director Branko Ilić said: "The Western Balkans market is more connected than it sometimes looks from outside. A dealer in Skopje talks to dealers in Priština and Sarajevo. Getting one credible reference deployment in a new country matters more than any brochure."

title: Note on spring season: flow sensor alert limitations
text:
During the spring 2024 application season we identified an issue that we want to be transparent about with our customers and dealers.

In April, a customer in Srem contacted our support team after noticing that his fertiliser totals for the season were lower than expected. After investigating the terminal logs, our support team found that the flow sensor on his applicator had been reading approximately 11 percent below actual flow since early March — a drift that had developed gradually and had not triggered any alarm because the reading never crossed the fixed threshold our software uses for fault detection.

The under-application affected roughly 420 hectares of wheat during the tillering and stem elongation applications. The customer has applied a corrective top-dressing where agronomically appropriate. We have covered the cost of the recalibration visit and the additional support time.

Our current alert system catches sensor failures — readings that go to zero or exceed a plausible ceiling. It does not catch gradual drift. This is a known limitation that we have discussed internally for some time. It became concrete this season.

We are now treating the development of a drift detection capability as a priority project. We are looking at whether our historical terminal data — which goes back several years for most active units — contains patterns that could be used to identify sensors drifting before they cause application errors.

If you have any questions about your terminal's sensor calibration status, please contact our support team. We recommend that dealers include a flow sensor check in all pre-season service visits as standard practice until we have a better automated solution in place.

title: O nama i uslugama — Solareks d.o.o.
text:
Solareks d.o.o. projektuje, gradi i prati fotonaponske sisteme za industrijske i poljoprivredne klijente u Vojvodini i šire. Od osnivanja 2014. godine realizovali smo više od 180 projekata, a trenutno aktivno upravljamo sa 140 lokacija ukupne snage oko 18 MW.

Naše usluge obuhvataju celokupan proces: procenu lokacije i procenu godišnjeg prinosa, izradu tehničke dokumentacije za mrežno priključenje, nabavku opreme, montažu i puštanje u rad, kao i dugoročno daljinsko praćenje i servisiranje. Za klijente koji žele da znaju tačno šta im sistem radi svakog dana, nudimo pristup našoj platformi za nadzor sa prikazom produkcije u realnom vremenu i mesečnim izveštajima.

Agri-FN instalacije — sistemi postavljeni iznad aktivnih njiva i staklenika — poseban su deo našeg portfelja. Radi se o tehnički zahtevnijim projektima koji moraju da uzmu u obzir potrebe biljaka za svetlošću, logistiku mehanizacije i sezonske varijacije. Do danas smo realizovali sedam takvih sistema u opštinama Bečej, Vrbas i Sombor.

Klijente ne obećavamo brojeve koji nisu potkrepljeni merenjima. Svaki naš ponudbeni proračun prinosa rađen je u PVsystu na osnovu stvarnih meteoroloških podataka za lokaciju, a ne generičkih tabela. Posle puštanja u rad pratimo da li sistem zaista dostiže projektovane vrednosti i o tome izveštavamo klijenta.

Ekipa broji 34 zaposlenih, od kojih je šesnaest na tehničkim pozicijama. Sedište nam je u Naučno-tehnološkom parku Novi Sad, odakle koordinišemo projekte i daljinski nadzor, dok montažni timovi rade na terenu širom Vojvodine i povremeno u inostranstvu.

title: Tražimo: Inženjer za daljinski nadzor i analizu podataka FN sistema
text:
Solareks d.o.o. traži inženjera koji će se pridružiti timu za daljinski nadzor i preuzeti odgovornost za analizu performansi naših 140 aktivnih lokacija.

Šta ćete raditi:
— Pratiti svakodnevnu produkciju sistema putem naše SCADA platforme (InfluxDB + Grafana)
— Analizirati 5-minutne podatke i identifikovati lokacije sa odstupanjem od očekivane produkcije
— Pisati Python skripte za automatizaciju redovnih izveštaja i detekciju anomalija
— Koordinirati sa montažnim timovima kada analiza ukaže na potrebu za fizičkim pregledom
— Pripremati mesečne izveštaje o performansama za klijente u Srbiji i inostranstvu

title: Potpisali smo O&M ugovor sa Feldmann Agrarenergie GmbH za tri lokacije u Bavarskoj
text:
Solareks d.o.o. i Feldmann Agrarenergie GmbH iz Landshuta potpisali su u maju 2024. ugovor o daljinskom upravljanju i održavanju za tri agri-FN lokacije u Bavarskoj ukupne snage 2,4 MW. Ugovor je na dve godine sa opcijom produženja.

Feldmann Agrarenergie je porodična kompanija koja upravlja sopstvenim sistemima na tri farme i do sada je koristila servis lokalnog nemačkog instalatera. Nakon preporuke jednog zajedničkog dobavljača opreme, kontaktirali su nas krajem 2023. godine jer su tražili partnera koji ima iskustvo upravo sa agri-FN konfiguracijom i koji nudi nadzor sa podacima na nivou stringa, a ne samo na nivou celog postrojenja.

Naš tim je u prvoj fazi postavio komunikaciju između njihovih postojećih invertera i naše platforme, uključujući VPN pristup. Ugovor pokriva mesečne izveštaje o performansama, obaveštenja o greškama u roku od četiri sata i jednu godišnju posetu terenu sa termovizijskom inspekcijom dronovima.

Ovaj ugovor je za nas važan korak u proširenju usluga izvan Srbije i prvi formalni višegodišnji O&M ugovor sa klijentom u Nemačkoj. Direktor Miloš Stanković komentarisao je: 'Feldmann tim je bio veoma direktan u pogledu zahteva — ne prihvataju nejasne izveštaje i žele da znaju tačno šta se desilo kada i zašto. To nam odgovara jer na isti način i mi pratimo naše lokacije ovde u Vojvodini.'

Paralelno sa tehničkim uvođenjem sistema radimo na usklađivanju naše platforme sa regulatornim zahtevima koje nam klijenti u Nemačkoj i Austriji postavljaju kao uslov za dugoročnu saradnju.

title: Šta smo naučili posle tri godine prikupljanja 5-minutnih podataka sa 140 lokacija
text:
Kada smo pre tri godine počeli da beležimo podatke na svakih pet minuta sa svih naših aktivnih instalacija, nismo imali jasan plan šta ćemo tačno sa tim podacima. Znali smo da su korisni, ali ih nismo sistematično koristili. Sada imamo bazu od otprilike 140 lokacija, svaka sa podacima o naponu, struji, snazi i temperaturi invertera, i tek sada počinjemo da razumemo koliko informacija se tamo krije — i koliko ih nismo koristili.

Najveća stvar koju smo naučili: alarm invertera je kasna vest. Do trenutka kada sistem sam javi grešku, kvar je već tu. Gledajući podatke unazad, u skoro svim slučajevima koji su rezultirali fizičkom intervencijom možemo da vidimo da je sistem počeo da 'čudno' radi dve do četiri nedelje ranije — blago niža produkcija u određenim satima, nešto veće oscilacije, asimetrija između stringova. Mi smo to videli tek nakon kvara, gledajući unazad.

Drugo što smo primetili: poređenje lokacija slične snage i orijentacije koje su u istoj oblasti daje iznenađujuće pouzdan signal. Kada jedna lokacija pravi šest posto manje od susedne u istim vremenskim uslovima tri dana za redom, nešto nije u redu. Ta logika je jednostavna ali zahteva automatizaciju — ne može čovek da gleda 140 grafika svako jutro.

Treće: podaci o temperaturi invertera su podcenjeni. Korelacija između dugotrajno povišene temperature invertera i kasnijeg kvara je nešto što smo tek počeli da istražujemo, ali preliminarni uvid izgleda obećavajuće.

Na ovim iskustvima gradimo sledeći korak — sistem koji će automatski proći kroz podatke svakog jutra i označiti lokacije koje odstupaju od očekivanog ponašanja. Još nismo tu, ali smer je jasan.

title: O nama i usluge — Voltex Solutions d.o.o.
text:
Voltex Solutions postoji od 2009. godine i za to vreme isporučili smo više od sto dvadeset projekata integracije i analitike za klijente u prerađivačkoj industriji širom DACH regiona i Holandije. Nismo agencija koja radi sve za svakoga — specijalizovani smo za slučajeve kada kompanija ima više poslovnih sistema koji moraju da razmenjuju podatke u realnom vremenu, a standardna rešenja nisu dovoljna.

Naše usluge obuhvataju projektovanje i implementaciju integracija između ERP sistema (pretežno SAP i Microsoft Dynamics), razvoj dashboard-ova za praćenje produkcije, nabavke i logistike, te dugotrajnu podršku i monitoring u produkciji. Svaki projekat pokrećemo fazom analize gde naš tim prolazi kroz postojeće tokove podataka zajedno sa IT timom klijenta, kako bismo razumeli gde nastaju greške i gde se gubi vreme.

Tim čine inženjeri sa iskustvom u industrijskom softveru, a ne u e-trgovini ili startap projektima — to znači da razumemo šta znači zastoj linije od sat vremena. Naš prosečan projekat traje između četiri i devet meseci, a prosečan klijent sarađuje sa nama duže od tri godine.

Za nove klijente nudimo besplatnu tehničku analizu u trajanju od dva dana, nakon koje dajemo pisanu procenu obima posla i predlog arhitekture. Kontaktirajte nas putem forme ili direktno na adresu info@voltex-solutions.rs.

title: Voltex Solutions potpisao trogodišnji ugovor sa Kessler Automotive Parts GmbH
text:
Voltex Solutions potpisao je trogodišnji ugovor sa Kessler Automotive Parts GmbH iz Štutgarta o razvoju i održavanju integracionog sloja između SAP S/4HANA instance i njihovog internog sistema za praćenje kvaliteta delova.

Kessler Automotive Parts proizvodi metalne komponente za automobilsku industriju i ima oko 1.400 zaposlenih. Njihov IT tim bio je suočen s problemom da podaci o greškama na liniji nisu stizali u SAP na vreme, što je otežavalo finansijsko izveštavanje i planiranje servisnih intervencija.

Nakon dvomesečne faze analize i proof-of-concept testa, Voltex-ov tim je predložio arhitekturu zasnovanu na event streaming-u koji smo implementirali koristeći Apache Kafka, uz FastAPI servis koji normalizuje podatke pre unosa u SAP. Pilot je završen za šest nedelja, a klijent je odlučio da produži saradnju na pun trogodišnji angažman koji uključuje razvoj, hosting i 24/5 monitoring.

'Ono što nas je ubedilo bila je faza analize — tim iz Voltex-a je razumeo naš problem pre nego što su predložili bilo šta tehničko', rekao je Gerhard Steinhoff, IT direktor kompanije Kessler Automotive Parts.

Ovaj ugovor je najveći jednokratni angažman koji je Voltex Solutions potpisao od osnivanja i označava ulazak kompanije u segment integracija u automobilskoj industriji. Projekat vodi Nikola Stanković, vođa projekta sa šest godina iskustva na SAP integracijama.

title: Šta smo naučili na Hannover Messe 2024 — beleška s terena
text:
Početkom aprila, dvojica naših kolega — Marko Ilić i Ana Petrović — posetili su Hannover Messe, jedan od većih industrijskih sajmova u Evropi. Ovde je kratki pregled onoga što su primetili, bez velikih zaključaka — samo ono što je bilo korisno za naš posao.

Prvo: razgovor o podacima se promenio. Pre dve-tri godine, klijenti iz prerađivačke industrije pitali su 'kako da povežem sistem A sa sistemom B'. Sada pitaju 'kako da znam da su podaci koji stižu tačni i da li mogu da im verujem za odlučivanje'. To je pomerak koji osećamo i u razgovorima sa našim postojećim klijentima — sve više pažnje ide na kvalitet i konzistentnost podataka, a manje na samo tehnički aspekt integracije.

Drugo: SAP ekosistem je aktivan. Videli smo nekoliko manjih firmi koje rade slične stvari kao mi, ali su se uglavnom fokusirale na cloud-only pristup. Naši klijenti još uvek imaju on-premise instalacije i ne planiraju migraciju u narednih pet godina — što znači da naš segment nije nestao, ali da moramo da pratimo kako SAP menja interfejse u novim verzijama.

Treće: bezbednost podataka dolazi u razgovor ranije nego pre. Dva potencijalna klijenta s kojim smo razgovarali na sajmu odmah su pitali gde se podaci čuvaju i kakvi ugovori postoje. To nije bio slučaj pre godinu-dve.

Nisimo doneli nikakav gotov zaključak, ali je sajam bio koristan za potvrdu nekih pretpostavki i za nekoliko konkretnih razgovora koje ćemo nastaviti u narednim nedeljama.

title: Services — ŠtitNet d.o.o.
text:
We monitor, detect, and respond to security incidents so that your internal team does not have to carry that load alone.

**SOC Monitoring**
Our Security Operations Centre runs around the clock, every day of the year. Each client environment is assigned a named analyst responsible for understanding your network, your applications, and what normal looks like for you. When something changes, you hear from that analyst — not from an automated ticket.

**Incident Response**
Clients on a retainer agreement have guaranteed response times. When a confirmed incident occurs, our response team can be working the problem within two hours of detection, remotely or on-site in Vojvodina and Belgrade within four hours.

**SIEM Deployment and Tuning**
We deploy and manage Wazuh and Elastic-based SIEM environments. We write the detection rules. We tune out the noise. We handle upgrades. You get dashboards and a monthly report.

**Vulnerability Management**
Scheduled internal and external scanning, combined with periodic manual penetration tests carried out by our own staff. Findings are ranked by exploitability in your specific environment, not just by generic CVSS score.

**Compliance Gap Assessments**
If your organisation needs to demonstrate alignment with NIS2 or domestic information security regulations, we can assess your current controls against the relevant requirements and produce a written gap report with prioritised recommendations.

All services are priced on a fixed monthly basis. We do not charge per alert or per analyst hour during an incident — that model creates the wrong incentives. Our contracts run for 12 months with a 90-day exit clause.

If you want to understand what we would actually do for your organisation before signing anything, we offer a one-week free visibility assessment: we connect to your environment in read-only mode, run our standard detection logic, and show you what we find. No obligation.

title: Security Analyst — Mid-Level (SOC, Night Rotation)
text:
ŠtitNet is looking for an analyst to join the SOC on a rotating shift schedule that includes night coverage. This is a full-time position based in Novi Sad.

**What you will do**
You will monitor client environments using Wazuh and the Elastic Stack, triage incoming alerts, investigate anomalies, and escalate confirmed incidents to the response team. You will also contribute to detection rule development — we expect every analyst to propose and test at least two rule improvements per month based on what they see in the queue.

**What we need**
- At least two years of hands-on SOC or network security work
- Comfort reading and writing Elastic Query Language or Lucene queries
- Familiarity with common attacker techniques at the level of the MITRE ATT&CK framework
- Ability to write a clear, factual incident report in English and Serbian
- Willingness to work a rotating schedule including two or three night shifts per week

**Nice to have**
- Experience with Zeek logs or network flow analysis
- Any scripting ability in Python or Bash — we use both for automation
- Exposure to TheHive or any other case management platform

**What we offer**
Fixed salary in the range of 1,600–2,100 EUR net depending on demonstrated experience. The shift schedule is published three weeks in advance and does not change on short notice. You will work in the NTP Novi Sad building with the rest of the SOC team — this is not a remote position.

Send a CV and a short note about the most interesting alert you ever investigated to posao@stitnet.rs. We do not use recruitment agencies.

title: Threat Intelligence Analyst (New Role)
text:
This is a new position at ŠtitNet, created because we are investing in building a regional threat intelligence capability that goes beyond what commercial feeds provide.

**The gap we are filling**
Our SOC analysts are good at investigating alerts. They are not resourced to also monitor Serbian and regional online communities for emerging threats, extract indicators, and maintain a live intelligence picture. We need someone who will own that function.

**What the role involves**
You will monitor a defined set of sources — forums, paste sites, Telegram channels, and others we will agree on together — for indicators and tactics relevant to our client sectors. You will extract structured data (IPs, domains, hashes, TTPs) and load it into our MISP instance with appropriate tagging. You will write short daily and weekly intelligence summaries for the SOC team and monthly reports for clients who subscribe to our threat intelligence add-on. You will also help us figure out how to automate more of the extraction work over time — we are aware that manual monitoring does not scale, and we want this person to help us think through tooling.

**What we need**
- Strong reading comprehension in Serbian, including Cyrillic script; understanding of regional slang and informal language is a real advantage
- Familiarity with MISP or another threat intelligence platform
- Understanding of indicator types and the difference between an indicator and a TTP
- Methodical working style — the value of this role is in consistent, reliable output, not occasional brilliance

**Nice to have**
- Python scripting for data extraction or text processing
- Prior experience with OSINT collection methods
- Knowledge of OpenCTI

Salary range: 1,500–1,900 EUR net. Location: Novi Sad, NTP building. Contact: posao@stitnet.rs.

title: ŠtitNet Selected for NTP Novi Sad Scale-Up Programme
text:
ŠtitNet d.o.o. has been accepted into the Science Technology Park Novi Sad's Scale-Up Programme for 2024, a cohort of ten Vojvodina-based technology companies selected for mentoring, co-working support, and access to the park's research collaboration network.

We have data, we have a working environment, and we need people who want to work on something real. That is what we are hoping to find through NTP."

ŠtitNet will participate in the programme's matchmaking sessions beginning in May, where the company's three registered challenges — relating to alert prioritisation, regional threat intelligence extraction, and NIS2 compliance mapping — will be presented to research teams for potential project scoping.

The company will continue its standard commercial operations throughout the programme. Clients have been notified that participation will not affect service levels or staffing of the SOC.

Further information about the NTP Scale-Up Programme is available at the science park's website.

title: What 18 months of SIEM data actually looks like — and why we have not used it yet
text:
We have a problem that we suspect is common but that people rarely describe honestly, so we are going to describe it.

Over the past 18 months we have been tagging every alert that goes through our SOC — true positive, false positive, or inconclusive — as part of a discipline exercise. Every analyst does it. It adds maybe 20 seconds per alert. The result is a labelled dataset sitting in Elastic that now covers several clients, multiple industries, and a wide range of alert types generated by Wazuh and our custom Zeek-based detection logic.

We have never done anything systematic with it.

The reason is straightforward: nobody on our team was hired to build machine learning pipelines, and none of us have had time to learn how. We know the data is there. We know in principle that a model trained on 18 months of labelled alerts from real client environments — with analyst ground truth attached — is worth something. We just have not been able to turn that knowledge into action.

What the data looks like: each labelled event includes the raw Elastic document, the analyst label, a free-text comment field (used inconsistently, but often usefully), the client industry tag, and a timestamp. The false positive rate overall is around 99.7 percent, which is the core of the problem — our analysts are spending most of their time confirming that things are fine.

We are sharing this publicly because we are actively looking for someone who wants to work on it with us. We are not looking for a product to buy. We are looking for a collaboration where we contribute the data and the domain context, and a technical partner contributes the modelling and pipeline knowledge. If that sounds relevant to what you do, contact us.

We are not expecting a perfect solution. We are expecting something that works well enough to give our analysts a ranked queue instead of a flat list, and that does not introduce new ways to miss real incidents. The cost of a false negative in our business is much higher than the cost of a false positive, and any approach that forgets that will not work for us.

title: ŠtitNet at SecForum Beograd 2024 — Booth and Panel Session
text:
ŠtitNet will be present at SecForum Beograd 2024, the annual information security conference held at the Sava Centre on 10–11 June.

We will have a stand in the exhibition hall on both days. If you are a potential client, a researcher, or someone interested in the kind of collaboration work we have been writing about recently, come and find us — we will have two analysts and our operations lead on-site throughout the event.

On the afternoon of the first day, our director Tatjana Vuković will take part in a panel discussion titled "Regional Threat Actors: What Serbian Companies Are Actually Facing." The panel will cover incident trends from the past 12 months as seen by practitioners working in Serbia, the gaps in currently available threat intelligence for the region, and what the NIS2 transposition means in practice for companies that are not sure whether it applies to them.

Tatjana will be speaking from operational experience, not from a theoretical framework. We will share anonymised statistics from our SOC where they are relevant to the discussion.

We will not be running any prize draws, sponsored refreshments, or lead-capture activities at our stand. If you give us a business card we will use it to follow up on a specific conversation we had with you, not to add you to a mailing list.

SecForum Beograd 2024 is organised by the Serbian Information Security Association. Registration for the conference is handled through their website. Attendance at the exhibition hall is free; conference sessions require a delegate pass.

title: O nama — VoxelRealm a.d.
text:
VoxelRealm je studio za razvoj igara osnovan 2009. godine u Novom Sadu. Radimo iz NTP Novi Sad, gde smo počeli s petoro zaposlenih i jednim nedovršenim projektom. Danas nas je 120 i imamo šest igara koje svakodnevno igraju stotine hiljada registrovanih korisnika u Srbiji, Rumuniji, Mađarskoj, Bugarskoj i Poljskoj.

Naš rad se zasniva na live-service modelu — igre koje lansiramo ne završavaju se na dan objave. Redovna ažuriranja, sezonski eventi i direktna komunikacija s igračima su sastavni deo svakog naslova. Imamo tim za korisničku podršku koji svakodnevno čita povratne informacije i prosleđuje ih direktno u razvojne timove.

Tehničku osnovu čini naša interna NetCore biblioteka za mrežnu sinhronizaciju, koju razvijamo i unapređujemo od 2011. godine. To nam daje kontrolu nad performansama igara na mrežama različitog kvaliteta — što je važno za tržišta na kojima radimo.

Nije nam cilj da budemo najveći studio u regionu. Cilj nam je da igre koje napravimo rade pouzdano, da igrači imaju razlog da se vraćaju, i da tim koji ih pravi ima stabilno radno okruženje. Svi naši naslovi su razvijeni u Novom Sadu. Planiramo da tako i ostane.

Ako vas zanimaju slobodna radna mesta, partnerske mogućnosti ili saradnja na istraživačkim projektima, kontaktirajte nas putem stranice za kontakt ili posetite nas u NTP Novi Sad, zgrada C, treći sprat.

title: Tražimo: Senior mrežni inženjer (3 pozicije)
text:
VoxelRealm traži tri iskusna mrežna inženjera koji bi se priključili timu koji razvija i održava serversku infrastrukturu naših live-service igara.

Šta ćete raditi:
— Rad na internoj NetCore biblioteci za mrežnu sinhronizaciju (C++)
— Projektovanje i implementacija serverske arhitekture na AWS (EC2, Lambda, ECS)
— Optimizacija matchmaking sistema i upravljanje cloud resursima
— Saradnja s timovima za razvoj igara na rešavanju mrežnih problema u produkciji
— Analiza logova i metrika performansi u PostgreSQL i Redis okruženju

Šta tražimo:
— Najmanje pet godina iskustva u radu s mrežnim sistemima ili distribuiranom infrastrukturom
— Solidno poznavanje C++ ili C#
— Iskustvo s AWS servisima ili sličnim cloud platformama
— Sposobnost rada u timu koji koristi agilne metode
— Poželjno: iskustvo u gaming industriji ili rad s real-time sistemima niske latencije

Uslovi rada:
— Puno radno vreme, Novi Sad (hibridni model rada: minimum tri dana u kancelariji)
— Kompetitivna plata prema tržištu u Srbiji uz godišnji pregled
— Relokacioni paket za kandidate koji dolaze iz drugog grada ili inostranstva
— Pristup NTP infrastrukturi i programima stručnog usavršavanja

Zašto VoxelRealm:
Radite na sistemima koje koriste stotine hiljada igrača svakodnevno. Problemi koje rešavate su stvarni i vidljivi. Tim ima iskustvo i stabilan raspored projekata.

Prijave šaljite na posao@voxelrealm.rs s naslovom 'Senior Network — 2024'. Pozicije su otvorene do popunjavanja.

title: Tražimo: Backend inženjer — cloud infrastruktura
text:
Uz tri pozicije za mrežne inženjere, VoxelRealm otvara i poziciju backend inženjera specijalizovanog za cloud infrastrukturu i automatizaciju.

Kontekst: Naš matchmaking sistem trenutno koristi fiksnu alokaciju serverskih instanci, što znači da plaćamo pune AWS resurse i tokom perioda niske aktivnosti. Tražimo osobu koja može da analizira postojeći sistem i predloži rešenje za dinamičku alokaciju — uz implementaciju u saradnji s backend timom.

Očekujemo da kandidat poznaje:
— AWS (EC2, ECS, Lambda, Auto Scaling)
— Docker i Kubernetes ili sličan alat za orkestraciju kontejnera
— Python ili Go za skripte i automatizaciju
— Osnove mrežnog programiranja i razumevanje latencije u real-time aplikacijama

Plus, ali ne obavezno:
— Iskustvo s Redis Cluster konfiguracijom
— Poznavanje specifičnosti gaming infrastrukture (dedicated game serveri, session management)

Ovo je pozicija za osobu koja voli da radi na konkretnim problemima s merljivim ishodom. Imamo podatke o opterećenju servera iz 2023. godine i tim koji može da pomogne s kontekstom NetCore biblioteke.

Uslovi su isti kao i za ostale inženjerske pozicije: hibridni rad, Novi Sad, kompetitivna plata, relokacioni paket po dogovoru.

Prijave: posao@voxelrealm.rs, naslov 'Backend Cloud — 2024'.

title: VoxelRealm na GameDev Central Expo 2024 u Budimpešti
text:
Tim VoxelRealm prisustvovao je ovogodišnjem GameDev Central Expo koji se održao od 18. do 20. aprila u Budimpešti. Ovo je treća godina zaredom da smo prisutni na ovom sajmu, a ovoga puta smo imali i prezentacioni štand na kom smo pokazali ažurirani stadionski mod igre ArenaForge.

Proizvođač zvuka Milena Draganović i lead dizajner Branimir Kovačević vodili su demonstracije za posetioce i prikupljali povratne informacije. Na štandu se zaustavilo oko 340 posetilaca tokom tri dana, a 62 od njih pristalo je da ispuni kratak upitnik o iskustvu igranja.

Rezultati upitnika potvrđuju ono što smo čuli na internim focus group sesijama: igrači primećuju i cene vizuelni doživljaj stadionskog moda, ali zvuk publike ocenjuju kao slab element. Ovo je korisna potvrda da je zvučni sistem prioritet za sledeće ažuriranje.

Pored toga, na sajmu smo imali dva razgovora s potencijalnim distributivnim partnerima za mađarsko i rumunsko tržište. Konkretnih dogovora još nema, ali kontakti su uspostavljeni.

Sledećeg meseca učestvujemo na regionalnom networking događaju u NTP Novi Sad gde ćemo predstaviti aktuelne projekte i otvorene pozicije. Više informacija biće dostupno na našem sajtu.

title: Zašto smo odlučili da ozbiljno shvatimo problem lažnih banovanja
text:
Ovo nije najugodniji tekst za pisanje, ali mislimo da igrači zaslužuju direktno objašnjenje.

U prvom kvartalu 2024. naša dnevna aktivna baza igrača pala je za 7% u poređenju s istim periodom prethodne godine. Analizirali smo razloge: deo otpada na sezonsku varijaciju, deo na konkurenciju. Ali znatan deo — ne možemo da precizno izmerimo koliki, ali dovoljno da nas brine — vezan je za poverenje u naš sistem za borbu protiv varanja.

BehaviorWatch, sistem koji koristimo za detekciju neregularnog ponašanja, označava oko 900 naloga dnevno. Naš tim za ručnu proveru može da pregleda 200. Ostatak ili čeka ili biva automatski suspendovan. Čitali smo forume. Znamo da legitimni igrači dobijaju banove. Znamo da neki od njih ne pišu žalbe — samo odlaze.

Probali smo fino podešavanje pragova u sistemu. Svaki put kad smanjimo broj lažnih pozitiva, propustimo više stvarnih prevaranata. To nije prihvatljivo rešenje — ni za igrače koji se fer ponašaju, ni za zajednicu u celini.

Zato smo odlučili da potražimo stručnu pomoć izvan studija. Imamo 18 meseci anonimizovanih podataka o ponašanju igrača — 2,3 miliona zapisa — i voljni smo da ih podelimo s partnerima koji mogu da pomognu u razvoju boljeg sistema za automatsko odlučivanje. Sistem koji nam treba ne samo da detektuje prevarante, već i da objasni zašto je određeni nalog označen, kako bi naši moderatori mogli brže i tačnije da odlučuju.

Ako radite na ovom problemu i mislite da možete pomoći, javite nam se. Ozbiljno.

title: VoxelRealm na NTP Tech Meetup — oktobar 2024.
text:
VoxelRealm biće jedan od domaćina na oktobarskom NTP Tech Meetupu koji se održava 17. oktobra 2024. u prostorijama NTP Novi Sad.

Na događaju ćemo imati dva kratka izlaganja:

1. 'Šta smo naučili iz 15 godina live-service razvoja' — Dragan Filipović, tehnički direktor VoxelRealm. Dragan će govoriti o arhitekturnim odlukama koje smo doneli 2011. kada smo počeli da razvijamo NetCore, šta bismo danas uradili drugačije, i gde vidimo prostor za unapređenje.

2. 'Podaci o igračima kao istraživački resurs' — kratak pregled anonimizovanih skupova podataka koje studio ima i koji bi mogli biti korisni za istraživanja u oblastima detekcije anomalija, audio sinteze i optimizacije resursa u distribuiranim sistemima.

Posle izlaganja organizujemo neformalnu diskusiju uz osveženje. Cilj nam je da povežemo naš tim s istraživačima i inženjerima koji rade na sličnim problemima — ne u svrhu prodaje, nego konkretnog razgovora o tome gde nam treba podrška i šta možemo da ponudimo zauzvrat.

Učešće je besplatno. Registracija putem NTP Novi Sad platforme za događaje. Broj mesta ograničen na 60.

Ako imate pitanja, pišite na events@voxelrealm.rs ili direktno Draganu Filipoviću putem LinkedIn profila studija.

title: What We Build and Who We Build It For
text:
EduForge Tehnologije builds learning management software for institutions that need something they can actually rely on. Our platform, LearnCore, covers everything a university or secondary school needs to run courses online or in a blended format: content delivery, assignment submission, automated and manual grading, attendance tracking, and communication between teachers and students. We also offer VirtualRoom for live sessions, ScoreAssist for automated grading assistance, and InsightDash for tracking learner engagement over time.

Our enterprise module, CorpPath, is used by companies that need to track structured internal training and demonstrate compliance to regulators or auditors. It connects to HR systems and produces audit-ready reports.

All of our products are built by our own engineers in Novi Sad. We do not white-label third-party platforms. When you call our support line, you speak to someone who has read the code. When a feature request makes sense, it goes into our actual roadmap.

We work with institutions that want a stable, long-term relationship with a vendor who understands how education works in this region — the grading conventions, the language requirements, the way academic calendars are structured, and the reality that most IT departments at schools and universities are small and stretched thin.

Our clients range from a faculty of 800 students to a bank with 3,000 employees going through mandatory certification cycles. What they share is a preference for a platform that does not require a consultant to configure every time something changes.

If you want to see the platform before committing to anything, we offer a 60-day pilot with full support. No automatic renewal.

title: Senior Backend Engineer — Java, Distributed Systems
text:
EduForge Tehnologije is looking for a senior backend engineer to join our core platform team in Novi Sad. This is a direct replacement hire following the departure of two experienced engineers at the end of 2023, and the role is important to us getting back on schedule.

What you will work on:
The majority of your time will be on LearnCore's backend — a set of Java Spring Boot microservices handling course management, grading workflows, user permissions, and integrations with external identity providers. There is a significant piece of work outstanding on a permissions and roles rework that the previous engineers started but did not finish. You will also contribute to the new REST API layer we are building for CorpPath.

What we are looking for:
— Five or more years of professional backend development, with strong Java skills
— Experience designing or maintaining microservice architectures
— Comfortable with PostgreSQL at reasonable scale (we are not talking about billions of rows, but query performance matters)
— Some experience with Kubernetes or container orchestration in general
— Able to work in person at NTP Novi Sad at least three days a week

Nice to have:
— Experience with WebRTC infrastructure or media servers
— Prior work on EdTech or SaaS platforms

What we offer:
Competitive salary by local market standards (we will discuss the number early in the process — we are not going to waste your time or ours), private health insurance, 25 days of annual leave, and a team that has low tolerance for unnecessary meetings.

We are aware that senior engineers have options. If salary is the main obstacle, let us have that conversation directly rather than losing you to it at the end of a long process.

Send a CV and a brief note about the most complex backend system you have worked on to careers@eduforge.rs.

title: Machine Learning Engineer — NLP, Learner Analytics
text:
EduForge Tehnologije is hiring a machine learning engineer to work on two active product problems: automated essay grading and learner engagement prediction. Both are real features in production use; neither is working as well as it needs to.

Context:
ScoreAssist, our grading assistant, performs acceptably on short answers but agreement with human graders drops significantly on longer written responses in Serbian, Bosnian, and Croatian. We have a labelled dataset of approximately 4,200 essays and we have experimented with multilingual transformer models, but the results are not yet good enough for university use. We need someone who can take this further — better feature engineering, better fine-tuning strategy, or a different approach entirely.

InsightDash includes a dropout-risk model based on behavioural signals. Its precision is currently around 54% on validation data, which means teachers are ignoring it. We have four years of log data for roughly 60,000 students. The problem is likely as much about feature engineering and model selection as it is about raw data volume.

What we are looking for:
— Solid grounding in machine learning, particularly classification and NLP tasks
— Hands-on experience with Python ML tooling (scikit-learn, Hugging Face, spaCy or similar)
— Ability to work with real, messy data rather than clean benchmark datasets
— Comfort explaining model behaviour to non-technical stakeholders — teachers and school administrators need to understand why a flag was raised

The role is based in Novi Sad. Hybrid arrangements are possible but the team works primarily on-site.

If you have worked on low-resource language NLP or educational data mining, mention that specifically — it is directly relevant to what we are doing.

title: EduForge Signs Multi-Year Agreement with Consortium of Vocational Schools in Bosnia and Herzegovina
text:
EduForge Tehnologije has signed a three-year licensing and support agreement with a consortium of fourteen vocational secondary schools operating under the coordination of an education development network based in Sarajevo. The rollout will cover approximately 9,500 students and 620 teaching staff across schools in Sarajevo, Banja Luka, Tuzla, and Mostar.

The agreement covers LearnCore for course and assignment management, VirtualRoom for practical demonstration sessions that cannot always be held in person, and InsightDash for tracking student progress across the school year.

The procurement process took just over eight months. The consortium evaluated three platforms and made their decision primarily on the basis of language support — our platform operates natively in Bosnian with grading terminology that matches the local curriculum structure — and on the cost of local support. Two of the other platforms evaluated would have required the consortium to engage a separate implementation partner.

Milorad Čović, who coordinates digital tools for the consortium, said the schools had been using a patchwork of free tools and that the main requirement was something that would not require a dedicated IT administrator at each location to keep running.

Onboarding for the first four schools begins in April. The remaining ten will come onto the platform in September, aligned with the start of the new academic year. EduForge's implementation team will run three in-person training sessions in Sarajevo and provide remote support for the transition period.

This agreement brings the total number of active institutions on EduForge platforms to 43.

title: Why Our Virtual Classroom Feature Has a 35-Person Limit and What We Are Doing About It
text:
We want to be straightforward about something that comes up regularly when we talk to universities: VirtualRoom, our live virtual classroom tool, is not reliable above 35 participants. Teachers and IT staff have noticed. We have had it raised in three renewal conversations in the past six months, and we think it is better to explain what is happening and what we are working toward than to keep giving vague reassurances.

The technical background is this: VirtualRoom is built on Janus Gateway, an open-source WebRTC server. When we originally built the feature in 2019, typical session sizes were seminars of 15 to 25 people. The way we distribute media streams across server instances was designed for that load. A university lecture with 80 or 100 students sends significantly more traffic through the system than we designed for, and the balancing logic does not cope well. The result is dropped frames, audio lag, and occasionally a session that crashes entirely.

Our infrastructure team diagnosed this clearly last autumn. The fix requires redesigning how we allocate and scale media server capacity — specifically the load balancing layer that decides which Janus instance handles which streams. This is not a trivial change, and it requires expertise we do not currently have in-house.

We are currently in discussions with two technical contacts at NTP who may be able to help us approach this differently than the commercial vendors we spoke to, whose quotes were well outside what we can spend on a single infrastructure project.

Our goal is to support sessions of up to 120 participants stably. We do not have a firm date to give you yet. What we can say is that this is the top infrastructure priority for 2024 and we are not treating it as a minor inconvenience. If you are a current client and this is affecting your operations, please contact your account contact — we want to know the specific cases so we can prioritise testing with real session patterns.

title: EduForge at EduTech Adria 2024 — Booth and Panel Session
text:
EduForge Tehnologije will be present at EduTech Adria 2024, a regional conference on educational technology taking place in Zagreb on 14 and 15 May. The conference brings together institutions, technology providers, and policy makers from across the former Yugoslav region to discuss practical developments in digital learning.

We will have a booth in the main exhibition hall where visitors can see live demonstrations of LearnCore, ScoreAssist, and InsightDash. Members of our product and implementation teams will be available for conversations about platform capabilities, integration with existing student information systems, and the practicalities of running a platform rollout across multiple institutions simultaneously.

On the afternoon of 14 May, our product lead Vesna Topalović will participate in a panel discussion titled 'Automated Assessment in Practice: What Works and What Does Not.' The session will look at where automated grading tools are genuinely useful in current deployments, where they fall short, and what the realistic expectations should be for institutions considering adding them. Vesna will speak specifically about the gap between short-answer scoring and longer written response evaluation, drawing on data from our deployments across the region.

If you are attending the conference and would like to schedule a specific time to meet rather than stopping by the booth, contact us at events@eduforge.rs before 10 May.

EduTech Adria 2024 takes place at the Zagreb Convention Centre. Full programme information is available on the conference website.

title: Potpisan ugovor sa Kern Antriebssysteme GmbH za razvoj ASIL-B modula
text:
Na početku ove godine potpisali smo ugovor sa Kern Antriebssysteme GmbH iz Štutgarta za razvoj softverskog modula za asistenciju pri kočenju koji mora dobiti ASIL-B sertifikaciju prema standardu ISO 26262.

Sa Kern Antriebssysteme GmbH sarađujemo od 2015. godine i ovo je naš najkompleksniji zajednički projekat do sada. Kern isporučuje elektromehanske kočione sklopove tier-1 dobavljačima u nemačkoj automobilskoj industriji, a zahtevi njihovih kupaca za formalnom bezbednosnom sertifikacijom postaju sve stroži.

Za nas ovo znači nekoliko stvari. Prvo, moramo izgraditi kompetencije za vođenje formalnog funkcionalnog bezbednosnog procesa – nešto što do sada nismo radili u punom obimu. Drugo, rok je konkretan: Q3 2025. godine. Treće, ovo je prilika da steknemo iskustvo koje će nam biti korisno i na budućim projektima sličnog tipa.

Trenutno formiramo tim koji će raditi na ovom projektu i tražimo inženjera sa iskustvom u ISO 26262 procesu koji bi nam pomogao da izgradimo tu kompetenciju interno. Oglas je objavljen na našem sajtu.

Detalji projekta su poverljivi, ali možemo reći da je reč o softveru koji radi na jednom AURIX mikrokontroleru i komunicira sa ostatkom sistema putem CAN FD magistrale.

title: O nama i uslugama – VeloSoft Inženjering
text:
VeloSoft Inženjering razvija softver koji se ugrađuje u komponente vozila. Radimo za tier-2 dobavljače koji isporučuju sisteme za kočenje, upravljanje i pogon evropskim proizvođačima automobila. Naš posao nije da pričamo o softveru – naš posao je da on radi.

Šta radimo:
- Razvoj ugrađenog upravljačkog softvera u C-u, sa poštovanjem MISRA-C smernica
- Implementacija i prilagođavanje AUTOSAR Classic softverskih komponenti
- Razvoj dijagnostičkih alata za UDS i OBD-II komunikaciju
- Verifikacija i validacija na HIL test benču
- Integracija bootloader rešenja za ažuriranje firmvera na terenu

Sa kim radimo:
Naši klijenti su uglavnom kompanije koje prave elektronske upravljačke jedinice ili elektromehanske sklopove i koje moraju isporučiti provereni, dokumentovani softver nагоре u lancu. Kern Antriebssysteme GmbH, Petrovič Elektronik iz Budimpešte i Holzer Mechatronik iz Graca su kompanije sa kojima sarađujemo duže od tri godine.

Kako radimo:
Radimo u dvonedeljnim sprintovima sa fiksnim milestone-ovima dogovorenim sa klijentom. Svaki modul koji isporučujemo dolazi sa test izveštajem i pratećom dokumentacijom. Ne prepuštamo testiranje klijentu.

Tim:
Trideset i četvoro nas radi u kancelariji u Novom Sadu. Većina je završila elektrotehniku ili računarstvo, nekoliko kolega ima iskustvo iz automotive kompanije u inostranstvu pre nego što su se vratili. Jezik komunikacije sa klijentima je engleski ili nemački, zavisno od projekta.

title: Oglas: Inženjer za funkcionalne bezbednosne procese (ISO 26262)
text:
VeloSoft Inženjering traži inženjera koji se razume u funkcionalne bezbednosne procese prema standardu ISO 26262.

Zašto ovo tražimo:
Dobili smo projekat koji zahteva ASIL-B sertifikaciju modula za asistenciju pri kočenju. Niko u timu do sada nije vodio kompletan proces od HARA analize do revizije dokumentacije za sertifikaciono telo. Tražimo nekoga ko to poznaje iz prakse.

Šta biste radili:
- Učestvovanje u izradi HARA (Hazard Analysis and Risk Assessment)
- Definisanje i praćenje bezbednosnih zahteva kroz životni ciklus projekta
- Pregled tehničke dokumentacije i priprema za eksternu reviziju
- Prenos znanja ka ostatku razvojnog tima

Šta očekujemo:
- Iskustvo na bar jednom projektu koji je prošao ISO 26262 reviziju (ASIL-A ili više)
- Poznavanje C-a i razumevanje ugrađenih sistema
- Sposobnost rada sa dokumentacijom na engleskom i/ili nemačkom jeziku
- Nije obavezno: posedovanje zvaničnog Functional Safety Engineer sertifikata, ali je prednost

Šta nudimo:
- Puno radno vreme, rad iz Novog Sada
- Plata po dogovoru zavisno od iskustva
- Konkretan projekat sa realnim rokom i jasnim ciljem
- Tim koji nije previše formalan ni previše haotičan

Prijave slati na karijere@velosoft-ns.rs sa kratkim opisom relevantnog iskustva.

title: Oglas: Inženjer za statičku analizu i verifikaciju softvera
text:
Tražimo inženjera koji može da nam pomogne da bolje iskoristimo naš pipeline za statičku analizu koda.

Kontekst:
Koristimo Polyspace Bug Finder u okviru Jenkins CI/CD pipeline-a. Svaki release generiše oko 900 upozorenja. Problem nije broj – problem je što ne znamo brzo koje od njih zaslužuje pažnju. Trenutno to rešavamo ručno, a to nije dobro ni za efikasnost ni za moral tima.

Šta biste radili:
- Analiza i klasifikacija izlaza iz Polyspace alata
- Razvoj ili prilagođavanje skripti za automatsko rangiranje upozorenja prema kontekstu koda
- Saradnja sa razvojnim timom na definisanju kriterijuma za bezbednosno-kritične putanje koda
- Dugoročno: unapređenje procesa verifikacije u celini

Šta očekujemo:
- Solidno poznavanje C-a i razumevanje čestih grešaka u ugrađenim sistemima
- Iskustvo sa alatima za statičku analizu (Polyspace, PC-lint, Coverity ili slično)
- Razumevanje MISRA-C pravila
- Prednost: iskustvo sa skriptovanjem u Python-u ili sličnom jeziku za obradu podataka

Šta nudimo:

title: Zašto smo prestali da ignorišemo upozorenja statičke analize (i zašto je to teže nego što zvuči)
text:
Svako ko je ikada radio na projektu sa stotinama hiljada linija C koda zna kako izgleda izlaz statičkog analizatora posle nekog vremena. Mnogo cifara, malo konteksta.

Kod nas je situacija već neko vreme ista: Polyspace Bug Finder generiše oko 900 upozorenja po releazu. To nije broj koji smo otkrili juče – znali smo to godinama. Problem je bio u pristupu: svaki inženjer na timu prolazio je kroz deo liste i na osnovu iskustva odlučivao šta je važno. To funkcioniše dok tim ne poraste i dok projekti ne postanu složeniji.

Prošle godine smo pokušali sa filter skriptama – razvrstavanje po tipu upozorenja, po fajlu, po modulu. Pomoglo je malo. Isti tip upozorenja u drajveru koji nikad ne ulazi u bezbednosno-kritičan put nije isti kao isti tip upozorenja u rutini koja direktno utiče na kočenje. Naše skripte to nisu razlikovale.

Nemamo gotovo rešenje. Ali imamo podatke: istorijat koji upozorenja su u prošlim releasima zahtevala izmenu koda, a koja su zatvorena kao 'lažni alarm'. Imamo mapiranje koda na funkcionalne celine. Imamo test izveštaje koji pokazuju gde su greške zaista pronađene.

Verujemo da se iz toga može napraviti nešto korisno – sistem koji bi uzeo u obzir i tip upozorenja i kontekst u kome se javlja i rekao: ovo provjeri prvo. Ako to smanji vreme trijažiranja za polovinu, za nas je to uspeh.

Ako se bavite ovom oblašću i imate ideju o pristupu, rado ćemo popričati. Kontakt je na sajtu.
